findings.title: First pairing does not authenticate the coordinator
findings.detail: The initial pair request accepts whichever self-signed certificate answers and uses that observed fingerprint to pin the claim request. An attacker who intercepts the first connection can relay the pairing request to the real coordinator, learn the pairing secret, and intercept the token returned after approval. Comparing the code does not prevent this because the attacker can relay the real code unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Establish coordinator identity before sending or receiving pairing credentials, for example by requiring an independently verified fingerprint during pairing and ensuring the approved worker token is not returned over a connection authenticated only by an unverified first-use certificate.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pairs over a network where an attacker can terminate TLS and relay requests. The owner approves the real pending code; the attacker observes the claim response and obtains the worker token.

findings.title: A previous release blocks active unowned entries during rollback
findings.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty `run_id` so the new code can decode it as null, but the previous release reads that field as a required run ID. If the daemon rolls back while an unowned entry is active, its land worker looks up run `""`, fails with “run … is gone,” and marks the entry blocked. The additive migration keeps old inserts valid, but does not keep these new entries resumable by the previous release.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-safe representation or handling path for active unowned entries so the previous release will not claim and permanently block them. Add a compatibility test that opens an active unowned row through the previous-release behavior and verifies it remains resumable.
findings.failure_scenario: Queue an unowned PR, leave it in `checking` or `waiting_ci`, then roll back to the previous daemon release. On restart, that release reads `run_id` as `""`, fails to find a run, and marks the land blocked instead of resuming it.

findings.title: Timeout signal immediately leads to a group kill
findings.detail: The monitor’s TERM trap sends TERM to the timeout process group, including the `timeout` process itself. That bypasses GNU `timeout`’s configured `--kill-after=30s` grace period; the wrapper’s EXIT trap then sends KILL to the group as soon as `wait` returns. A check that needs time to flush logs or shut down after TERM can therefore be killed immediately, contrary to the intended TERM-then-graceful-kill behavior.
findings.suggestion: Keep the timeout process alive to enforce its grace period, and arrange for the monitor to report the tree without terminating the timeout process group. Then let timeout deliver TERM and KILL according to its configured deadlines.
findings.failure_scenario: The CI check receives TERM at 20 minutes and has a child that ignores TERM while flushing diagnostics; the group kill happens immediately, so the child is killed before the configured 30-second grace period.

findings.title: Intent records can name a different run than the owning row
findings.detail: beginLeaseIntent checks the runId argument against the existing row, but never checks that intent.record.run equals runId. It can therefore persist a row owned by run A with a desired record claiming run B; reconciliation may then confirm that record as ownership while the row still records run A. This breaks the association between the row’s owner and its journaled intent.
findings.suggestion: Reject the intent unless intent.record.run === runId before inserting or updating the row, and add a test asserting the mismatch is rejected without changing storage.
findings.failure_scenario: Call beginLeaseIntent(repo, ref, "run-a", { op: "acquire", before: zeros, record: { ...validRecord, run: "run-b" }, commit: null }). The row is stored with run_id "run-a" and an intent whose desired record names "run-b"; recovery can later confirm run B’s record under run A’s row.

output.summary: Found a mismatch in superseded-intent recovery: when the row has no confirmed ownership, recovery clears the intent but leaves confirmed state null instead of marking it lost as required. The focused tests could not run because the installed Zod lacks `prefault`.

findings.title: Superseded never-confirmed intents are not marked lost
findings.detail: `markLeaseLost` deliberately leaves `confirmed_state` null when `confirmed_generation` is null. But `reconcileLeaseIntent` calls it after identifying a higher-generation tip even when the row was never confirmed. The request requires superseded recovery to set confirmed state to `lost`; the new test at `test/lease-store.test.ts` instead codifies the contrary behavior. A later caller cannot distinguish this superseded row from a never-confirmed row eligible for forgetting and reuse.
findings.suggestion: When reconciliation classifies a pending intent as superseded, persist a lost state even if no prior generation was confirmed, and update the test to assert that state. Preserve confirmed generation/tip only when they actually exist.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A journals an acquisition for generation 1 without a confirmed lease; another holder's generation 2 is observed during recovery. Recovery returns `superseded`, clears the intent, and leaves `confirmed` null. The row then appears never-confirmed and can be forgotten or reused as though no successor had superseded A's intent.

findings.title: Post-merge checkpoint can persist before observation finalization
findings.detail: `confirmPostMerge` is given `ctx.save("post-merge-confirmed")`, which writes the checkpoint before the following save finalizes observations. If the process stops between these calls, the run resumes as already post-merge-confirmed while the observations remain unfinalized; the resume path may not repeat confirmation or finalization. This violates the required atomic finalization with the checkpoint and the restart invariant.
findings.suggestion: Make the final `post-merge-confirmed` state write and observation finalization one `ctx.save` transaction. Avoid persisting that completion checkpoint in the callback passed to `confirmPostMerge` before finalization is included.
findings.failure_scenario: A post-merge gate has an unfinalized observation; `confirmPostMerge` returns and its `ctx.save("post-merge-confirmed")` commits the checkpoint. The process stops before the next save runs. On restart, the run observes the checkpoint and skips confirmation, leaving the observation unfinalized indefinitely.

findings.title: Recovery matches superseded leases by ref alone

If the second row was already confirmed lost and its pending intent was dropped during recovery, it also satisfies the remaining state checks and receives a spurious `onLost` callback.
findings.suggestion: Carry repository and ref together in recovery results, or otherwise determine each row’s own reconciliation result before calling `lose`.

findings.title: Superseded-head response can name a stale SHA as current
findings.detail: When reviewableHead reports superseded, this passes recorded?.sha to the diagnostic. The response can therefore label an old SHA as “current head,” giving the caller the wrong recovery information.

findings.title: Shutdown clears the handle before stop cleanup
findings.detail: When shutdown aborts a re-attached invocation, the executor returns a cancelled result without cancelling the job. The implementation stage nevertheless sets implementationReadyRound and deletes agentJob before saving. Factory.stop() waits for scheduler.stop() and then calls cancelOpenAgentJobs(this.keptAgentJobs()); because the saved state no longer has the handle, the still-leased job is treated as an orphan and cancelled. This defeats the required detach-on-shutdown behavior and prevents the same worker session from surviving a coordinator restart.
findings.suggestion: Do not save implementation-ready or clear agentJob when the invocation was cancelled by shutdown. Preserve the handle so stop-time orphan cleanup keeps the job for restart reconciliation.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker job is leased and its run is in implementStage. Factory.stop() aborts the run with Error("shutdown"); lanAgentExecutor returns a cancelled result while leaving the job alone. implementStage saves implementation-ready and clears agentJob, then Factory.stop() finishes scheduler.stop() and cancels the job because keptAgentJobs() can no longer find its id. The next boot cannot re-attach the session.

If such a run starts and fails between polls, reconciliation can observe only the final failed state; when the failed label was already present, it skips the label write and creates no new failure event. A trusted priority event from after the previous failure can then satisfy re-approval for this later failure.

findings.title: Terminal status prevents scheduler from resuming an incomplete rollback
findings.detail: The rejection save sets the run status to `needs_human` before `rollbackRejectedMerge` resets and cleans the worktree. Scheduler startup only requeues `running` and `waiting_input` runs; it does not resume `needs_human` runs. Therefore a restart after this save (including after the reset but before rollback state is saved) leaves the worktree in the merged state and never completes the recorded rollback. The new tests call `executeRun` directly after reopening the store, so they bypass this startup behavior.

Land observation collection/finalization has a claim race that can finalize a lost attempt as interrupted before the entry reaches a terminal state. Focused tests could not execute because the checkout lacks the `entities` dependency.

findings.title: Lost land claims can finalize observations prematurely
findings.detail: The land-specific post-insert check finalizes all open observations for the entry whenever the entry is terminal. It does not verify that this attempt still owns the claim or that it is the active attempt. If an older check finishes after the entry has already been blocked/landed/cancelled by a replacement claim, it calls `finalize(run_id)` and classifies its own open rows as `interrupted`; the old attempt's finalizer cannot then replace that history because finalized rows are skipped. This can misclassify the attempt that actually completed the checks.
findings.suggestion: Only finalize the current attempt when its owned claim reaches terminal state, and keep lost-attempt rows open until the entry's terminal transition finalizes them as interrupted. Include attempt/claim identity in the finalization selection so a late old executor cannot finalize the replacement attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: Attempt 1 loses its claim while executing. Attempt 2 is reclaimed and blocks the entry, which finalizes attempt 1 as interrupted. If attempt 1 then inserts/finishes after that terminal transition, this code calls unscoped `finalize('land:<id>')` and marks its rows interrupted even though its checks returned; alternatively, if attempt 1 is still running when attempt 2 finishes, an insertion after the terminal transition is marked interrupted immediately and cannot be finalized with its actual retry result.

findings.title: Post-merge checkpoint is saved before observation finalization
findings.detail: `confirmPostMerge` invokes this save callback after persisting each confirmation. The code then performs a separate save at line 3610 that finalizes observations. If the process stops after the callback save and before the second save, the `post-merge-confirmed` checkpoint is already recorded while the observation remains unfinalized. A resumed run can proceed past confirmation without revisiting this finalizer, violating the requirement to finalize in the transaction that saves this checkpoint.
findings.suggestion: Make confirmation persistence and observation finalization part of the same `post-merge-confirmed` save transaction. Preserve per-confirmation durability as needed, but do not advance this checkpoint until finalization is included.
findings.failure_scenario: A post-merge gate has an observation; coordinator confirmation completes and `ctx.save("post-merge-confirmed")` succeeds through the callback; the process terminates before the subsequent save. On restart, the checkpoint indicates confirmation completed, but the observation still has `finalized_at = NULL`.

output.summary: The lease implementation has a concrete pending-intent ordering defect: cross-run acquisition can refuse before reconciling the existing intent, contrary to the required wait-and-reconcile behavior. findings.title: Cross-run acquire bypasses pending-intent reconciliation
findings.detail: This early return refuses a different run whenever the stored row has an intent, before calling `reconcile`. If the intent is unresolved, the required behavior is to return `wait` without changing anything and retry reconciliation on a later operation or loop tick. The caller instead receives `refused: live`, so it may abandon the run even though the row's ownership is still uncertain. This also violates the stated rule that every operation reconciles a pending intent first.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the row's pending intent under the ref mutex before applying cross-run refusal logic. If reconciliation remains pending, return `wait`; after it settles, re-read the row and apply the cross-run rules.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A has a pending acquisition intent with no confirmed ownership because its GitHub write outcome is unreadable. Run B calls `acquire` before the renewal loop reconciles it. This branch returns `refused: live` without reading GitHub or reconciling the intent, instead of `wait`; Run B can be discarded despite the pending state later resolving as dropped.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict trigger
findings.detail: A cached GitHub snapshot is used without checking whether it represents the land entry's approved head. If it is stale, startConflictTrigger marks the durable trigger as skipped. A later poll does not retry a skipped trigger, and it may not emit another pr.conflicting event if the conflict episode was already observed.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict trigger
findings.detail: When any saved PR snapshot exists, the trigger is consumed using that snapshot without refreshing it. findings.title: Executor events are never consumed by daemon gate runs

Its check and status events therefore never reach pipeline events or the landing log, defeating the shared executor interface's event path.

findings.title: Replaying a saved result skips the workspace state needed by retries

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed

Consequently its check and status events never reach pipeline event records or the landing log, so the executor interface does not preserve gate observability across implementations.
findings.suggestion: Consume the execution event stream in the shared path and forward its events to the appropriate pipeline and landing callbacks, avoiding duplicate local notifications.

findings.title: Resume discards handles for in-flight retries

findings.title: Retry executions are discarded instead of reattached after restart
