findings.detail: The change only filters the MCP change view. Verify-change review prompts also include a raw unified patch, and the literal credential redaction used around model invocations cannot match a multiline value interrupted by diff prefixes. The request requires other diff-rendering outputs to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups; neither is done here.
findings.suggestion: Apply shared patch-aware credential filtering to review prompt diffs, or explicitly document this output as a follow-up as allowed by the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change run reviews an added file containing a registered `alpha-secret\nbeta-secret` credential. Its review prompt includes `+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret`, which does not match the registered literal and is sent to the reviewer model.

output.summary: The added patch filter covers the main added-file case, but a diff in the report returned by the same tool can still expose a multiline credential. The targeted MCP test could not run because the checkout lacks the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency.

findings.title: Redact line-prefixed credentials in returned reports
findings.detail:
The new reconstruction filter is applied only to the file patch. A persisted report containing a diff still passes through literal privacy matching, so prefixes between credential lines prevent a match and the report is returned with both lines visible. This is an existing leak left unresolved by the request, which explicitly includes diffs in reports or requires them to be listed as follow-ups. A targeted check reproduced the matcher behavior: `bun -e 'import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const secret="alpha-secret
beta-secret"; const report="```diff
+alpha-secret
+beta-secret
```"; console.log(JSON.stringify({matches:privateMatches(report,[{value:secret,entry:0}]),report}));'` output `{"matches":[],"report":"```diff
+alpha-secret
+beta-secret
```"}`.
findings.suggestion: Apply equivalent line-prefixed credential protection to diff content in reports before paging, and add a regression test for a report containing a multiline credential.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains a fenced diff with `+alpha-secret` and `+beta-secret` on consecutive lines, and the registered credential is `alpha-secret\nbeta-secret`; limitless_get_change returns both lines in report text.

output.summary: Reviewed the setup, prompt, validation, cache, and timing paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout has an incompatible Zod installation and is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk.

findings.title: Invocation errors can be counted as preparation time
findings.detail: Review trials do not set roundsUsed, so an exception after the reviewer starts enters this branch and overwrites the already-recorded preparationMs with the elapsed time since preparation began. The reported preparation time then includes the reviewer invocation and any wait before it.
findings.suggestion: Only calculate preparationMs in the catch path when preparation did not finish, preserving the recorded value after invocation starts.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup-enabled review finishes preparation, starts a reviewer, and the harness throws after a lengthy invocation; details.preparationMs includes that invocation time.

output.summary: Reviewed setup execution, prompt validation, cache identity, and timing paths. Targeted tests could not start because the available dependencies include an incompatible Zod version and lack the MCP SDK.

findings.title: Check the trial cache before running setup
findings.detail: Setup runs before the cache key is checked. A repeat of a previously successful setup-enabled trial therefore reruns its potentially expensive setup, and a transient setup failure records a preparation error instead of reusing the valid cached result. This defeats cache reuse precisely when dependencies cannot currently be installed.
findings.suggestion: Compute the cache identity and attempt reuse before executing gate setup; run setup only when a reviewer invocation is needed.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup-enabled trial succeeds and is cached. On a later identical eval, its package registry is unavailable: setup fails and the trial is recorded as an error even though the cached result is available.

output.summary: The change protects the tested credential by withholding the entire file, but that fails the requested visibility requirement and introduces a large-file regression. The targeted command `bun test test/mcp-proxy.test.ts` could not run because the checkout lacks `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js`.

findings.title: A credential match hides the entire patch
findings.detail: The implementation replaces the whole file's patch with a withholding message. The acceptance criterion requires withholding the lines spanned by the credential while keeping the rest of the file visible. The new test explicitly expects the whole-file message, so it does not verify that requirement.
findings.suggestion: Map matches on each reconstructed file side back to the corresponding patch lines and withhold those lines before paging. Assert that unrelated lines remain visible across pages.
findings.failure_scenario: An added file contains `public before`, a two-line registered credential, and `public after`; the change view returns only `[withheld: private text; 1 file]`, hiding both public lines.

findings.title: Small diffs become unavailable for large files
findings.detail: When any multiline credential is registered, the new check reads each complete blob through `sh`, which rejects output over 50,000,000 characters. Consequently, a small otherwise readable diff in a larger text file now fails the entire change view even when the credential is absent.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the relevant reconstructed patch sides without requiring a full blob to fit the subprocess output limit, or use a bounded streaming scan that can preserve the requested patch visibility.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered multiline credential exists and a one-line change is made to a text file larger than 50 million characters. `git show` exceeds `SH_OUTPUT_LIMIT` and the endpoint returns `Local comparison commits or Git inspection unavailable`.

findings.title: Review prompts still render unredacted multiline credentials in diffs
findings.detail: The request also covers other outputs that render diffs, or requires them to be listed as follow-ups. Verify-change review prompts embed `reviewDiff.patch` with diff prefixes, so a registered multiline credential is not matched as a literal and its parts can be sent to the review model. This path was not changed or identified as a follow-up.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same line-aware credential protection to rendered review diffs, or explicitly document this path as a follow-up as permitted by the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change diff adds consecutive lines containing the two halves of a registered multiline credential. The prompt contains them as separate `+` lines, preventing literal credential redaction.

output.summary: The change protects the tested credential by withholding its entire file, but that fails the requested visibility behavior. Another diff-rendering path also remains unaddressed. The targeted test could not run because the MCP SDK dependency is missing.

findings.title: Preserve non-secret lines in a matching file
findings.detail: When either file side contains a multiline credential, the implementation replaces the entire patch with a file-level notice. The request explicitly requires withholding the lines spanned by a match while keeping the rest of the file visible. The new tests instead assert the file-level notice, so they do not enforce that acceptance criterion.
findings.suggestion: Map matches in each reconstructed file side back to the affected patch lines and withhold those lines before paging; assert that unrelated lines remain visible.
findings.failure_scenario: An added file contains a two-line registered credential between public source lines. The response hides the public lines along with the credential, preventing review of the file.

findings.title: Protect or document the reviewer prompt's rendered diff
findings.detail: The verify-change reviewer prompt still receives a unified diff containing line-prefixed credential fragments. Literal credential redaction cannot match a multiline value across those prefixes. The request requires other outputs that render diffs to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups; neither is present in this change.
findings.suggestion: Apply shared multiline-aware diff redaction before sending this patch to the reviewer, or explicitly document this diff-rendering path as a follow-up as the request permits.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change diff adds a file containing a registered two-line credential. The reviewer prompt includes both added lines with their '+' prefixes, so literal matching does not remove the credential before it is sent to the model.

output.summary: The targeted retry-file tests passed. Two broader test files could not load because installed dependencies are incompatible or missing: zod lacks number().overwrite, and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is unavailable. A direct probe confirmed that a security check can become nonblocking after a retry, contrary to the request.

findings.title: A passing retry makes a failed security check nonblocking
findings.detail: The retry classification treats every successful retry as flaky, with no exception for security checks. The request explicitly requires a security check's failure never to become a pass. A direct probe calling retryRegressions with a failed check named security and a passing fake retry returned verdict "flaky" and blocking false. Command: bun -e 'import {retryRegressions} from "./src/gates/run.ts"; const result={name:"security",command:"security-scan",ok:false,exitCode:1,durationMs:1,output:"vulnerability"}; const cfg={setup:[],checks:[{name:"security",run:"security-scan"}],source:"detected",protectedPaths:[]}; const runner=async()=>({setupOk:true,setup:[],checks:[{...result,ok:true,exitCode:0}]}); console.log(JSON.stringify(await retryRegressions([{name:"security",verdict:"regressed",blocking:true,result}],process.cwd(),cfg,[],new AbortController().signal,undefined,runner)));' Output included: "verdict":"flaky","blocking":false.
findings.suggestion: Represent security checks explicitly in trusted gate configuration and preserve a blocking failure regardless of retry success; cover both targeted and full retry paths.
findings.failure_scenario: A security scan passes on the baseline, detects a vulnerability after the change, and passes on retry; the gate labels it flaky and permits the run to proceed.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry, reporter, slot, and configuration paths. The focused retry-files tests passed. The feedback and executor suites could not load because the checkout has an incompatible Zod installation and a missing MCP SDK module.

findings.title: A passing retry clears a failed security check
findings.detail: The retry classification treats every successful retry as a nonblocking flake. It only preserves confinement failures, and has no corresponding protection for other security checks. This leaves the request's explicit requirement that a security check failure never become a pass unmet. A focused reproduction using a check named `security` produced `[{"verdict":"flaky","blocking":false}]` after its first scan failed and its retry passed.
findings.suggestion: Represent security checks explicitly in trusted gate configuration and preserve their blocking failure on every retry path; add a test covering a failed security check followed by a passing retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A baseline security scan passes, the post-change scan reports a vulnerability, and a subsequent scan passes. The gate marks the result flaky and nonblocking, allowing the change to proceed.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing and heartbeat implementation as the permitted first slice. The pairing exchange is vulnerable to interception, and worker credentials are not consistently denied to agent sandboxes. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/config-routing.test.ts` could not run: the checkout could not resolve `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js`, and its installed Zod lacks `z.number().overwrite`.

findings.title: Bind the pairing code to the coordinator certificate
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any TLS certificate, and the coordinator generates both the displayed code and claim secret. A network attacker can terminate TLS, relay the pairing request and its response to the real coordinator, and show the worker the same code the owner sees. The worker then pins the attacker's certificate, while the attacker knows the claim secret and can obtain the approved worker token. Comparing the codes therefore does not authenticate the coordinator.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the actual coordinator certificate and the pairing exchange, so relaying through a different certificate changes the code and cannot yield the approved token.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the first connection to the coordinator, proxies the pairing exchange, and obtains the worker token after the owner approves the matching displayed code.

findings.title: Protect persisted worker secrets in every agent-hosting process
findings.detail: Private-file denies are held in a process-local registry. Pairing releases the token and fingerprint registrations on return, and the separately launched worker registers them only in its own process. A daemon running agents on the same machine never registers those files; similarly, it registers the coordinator TLS key only while its listener is enabled. Claude's reader policy denies registered private files, but does not deny the whole home directory, so an agent can read these persisted credentials despite their mode 0600.
findings.suggestion: Register the known worker token, fingerprint, and coordinator key paths in every process that launches agent sandboxes, for as long as those files may exist, including when the listener or worker is stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine is paired as a worker and also runs a factory daemon. After pairing exits, a tool-enabled Claude reader launched by that daemon reads the worker token from the default data directory and can authenticate as the worker.

output.summary: Reviewed the listener, pairing, heartbeat, credential handling and owner API integration. The first-half split is documented, but pairing permits credential theft by an active network attacker and sandbox protection is process-local. Targeted tests could not start: the checkout lacks @simplewebauthn/server and has an incompatible Zod installation.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the TLS connection
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any TLS certificate and receives both the pairing code and claim secret through that connection. An active network attacker can proxy the request to the real coordinator, relay the same code to the worker and owner, and retain the claim secret. Once the owner approves the matching code, the attacker can claim the worker token. Pinning the attacker's certificate on subsequent requests does not prevent this.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the actual TLS session or certificate and ensure an intermediary cannot learn the secret used to claim the token.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, forwards the pairing exchange to the coordinator, and uses the observed claim secret after the owner approves the matching code.

findings.title: Worker credentials are protected only in the worker process
findings.detail: protectPrivateFile registers paths in an in-memory process-local map. The worker CLI and the daemon that launches local agents and gates are separate processes, so opening these files here does not add them to the daemon's sandbox deny list. The pairing command also releases its registrations on exit. Similarly, the coordinator TLS key is registered only while its listener is enabled. An agent sandbox with read access to the configured data directory can therefore read these persistent secrets despite the required read-deny rule. The new sandbox test masks this by registering all files in the same process that runs the gate.
findings.suggestion: Register persistent worker credential and TLS key paths when each sandbox-launching process starts, regardless of whether the worker or listener is running; test across separate processes and after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine runs the worker CLI and a separate Limitless daemon with a data directory readable by an agent; the agent reads the worker token or coordinator key because its daemon never registered that path.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing and heartbeat implementation and its permitted first-slice scope. The targeted workers test could not run because the checkout is missing the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents subsequent daemon starts
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates key.pem before invoking OpenSSL, but the error path leaves partially created TLS material in place. If OpenSSL fails or the process is interrupted before cert.pem is written, every subsequent startup fails with "Incomplete worker TLS material". When the worker listener is configured, this also prevents the daemon from starting.
findings.suggestion: Generate the key and certificate in protected temporary files and publish them only after both are valid, cleaning up incomplete generation on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The first listener startup is interrupted after creating key.pem but before OpenSSL writes cert.pem; restarting the daemon then repeatedly fails until an operator manually removes the partial file.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing-and-heartbeats split and its surrounding code. The targeted worker suite could not load because @simplewebauthn/server is missing. A focused TLS setup check reproduced a startup recovery defect.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents subsequent daemon starts
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates key.pem before invoking openssl, but leaves it behind if openssl fails or the process is interrupted. Every subsequent start then rejects the incomplete TLS material, so enabling the worker listener can leave the entire daemon unable to restart until an operator manually removes the partial file. A targeted check that invoked certificate() once with openssl unavailable and again with PATH restored printed `first: Command failed (-2): openssl req ...` followed by `second: Incomplete worker TLS material`.
findings.suggestion: Generate the key and certificate as a temporary pair and publish them only after successful generation, cleaning up partial files on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped during its first certificate generation, or openssl temporarily fails; later daemon starts fail even after the original problem is gone.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease, worker, validation, fallback, and resume paths. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout has a missing MCP SDK dependency and an incompatible installed Zod version.

findings.title: Do not cache a locally executed baseline as a LAN baseline
findings.detail: The baseline cache key is selected from configuration before execution. If LAN attempts fail, the executor runs the baseline locally, but its result is still stored under the LAN key. A later run can reuse that local baseline while its post-change gates run on a worker. Environment-dependent failures can then be classified as pre-existing or as regressions against a different machine.
findings.suggestion: Record the executor that actually produced the baseline and avoid caching a local fallback under the LAN key, or otherwise ensure the baseline and subsequent gates use the same executor.
findings.failure_scenario: No worker is available during baseline preparation, so the baseline runs locally and is cached. A worker is available on the next run and executes the post-change gates, which are compared with the cached local result.

findings.title: Reattach durable LAN jobs for retry and timeout executions
findings.detail: Resume only accepts stored handles for baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A shutdown during a timeout rerun or a baseline or regression retry leaves its LAN job durable, but resume discards that handle and enqueues a new execution. Completed work can repeat, and a job that finished while the coordinator was down has its result ignored.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to reattach each durable LAN execution after restart, including timeout and targeted retry purposes.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator shuts down while a worker is running a regression retry. On restart, the pending purpose is regression-retry, so the existing handle is cancelled and a new job is started even if the original job completed.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease, worker execution, result validation, fallback, and restart paths. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/gate-executor.test.ts` could not run: the installed dependencies lack `@simplewebauthn/server`, and the installed Zod does not provide `z.number().overwrite`. These environment errors are not findings.

findings.title: Reattach to durable retry and timeout jobs after restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate excludes timeout and retry purposes even though their LAN handles are persisted and deliberately retained on shutdown. On resume, the pending job is cancelled and a new job is enqueued instead of attaching to the existing job. This repeats gate commands that may already have completed and defeats the requested restart guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Resume persisted LAN handles for timeout and retry executions when their stage, round, purpose, and SHA match; add restart coverage for those purposes.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator shuts down after a worker completes a regression retry but before the pipeline records its result. On restart, the completed job is discarded and the retry runs again.

findings.title: Reject a final result that contradicts posted check failures
findings.detail: Check events and the final GateRun are validated independently. A worker can post a failed result for a requested check and then submit a passing result for that same check; the latter is accepted as the job result and can make the gate pass. The coordinator has already recorded evidence of the failure, so accepting the contradictory final result violates the requirement that infrastructure handling never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Validate the final run against the check events recorded for the current lease attempt and treat contradictory results as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts an event for check `test` with `ok: false`, then posts a final run containing `test` with `ok: true` and exit code 0. Both requests pass the current validation, and the pipeline receives the passing run.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry selection, base-config trust boundary, logging, and restart flow. The gate retry tests passed, but the land-queue tests could not run because the sandbox lacks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: A restart can erase the evidence for a recorded flaky landing
findings.detail: The flaky reason is persisted before the land advances out of checking. If the daemon stops after that write but before the pushed-SHA checkpoint, the resumed land reruns the checks and truncates the same log. A clean rerun leaves the earlier flaky reason in place, but removes the first failure and targeted retry that justify it. The eventual landed entry therefore reports a flake whose required evidence is no longer available.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the earlier attempt's log across checking restarts, or checkpoint the flake and its log together so the recorded outcome remains supported by the retained evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, the flaky reason is stored, and the daemon stops before recording pushedSha. On restart the full checks pass cleanly; the log is overwritten and the entry later lands with the old flaky reason.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry and landing paths. The gate-retry tests passed, but the land-queue tests could not run because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js was unavailable in the environment.

findings.title: Restart can retain a flaky outcome after overwriting its evidence
findings.detail: The flaky reason is stored before the land reaches its durable waiting-for-CI checkpoint. If the daemon stops after that write but before the checkpoint, the resumed land reruns checks and truncates the same log. If those checks pass cleanly, the old flaky reason remains and is preserved on landing, but the log no longer contains the failure or retry that it describes.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the earlier attempt's log across a checking restart, or clear and recompute the flaky outcome together with its evidence when checks restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, the daemon stops before pushedSha is recorded, and the resumed full checks pass. The landed entry says flaky while its log contains only the clean resumed checks.

output.summary: Reviewed the Claude reader settings and verifier smoke path. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout has incompatible or missing dependencies: Zod lacks `prefault`, and `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` is unavailable.

findings.title: Allow the Bun executable the verifier will actually invoke
findings.detail: The allowance is derived from the daemon's `process.execPath`, but a verifier invoking `bun test` resolves `bun` through its shell PATH. Those can be different installations. If the PATH-selected Bun is under a denied private root, it remains unreadable and the original verification failure persists. The new smoke check masks this case because it also invokes `process.execPath` explicitly.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the Bun executable from the environment used by the verifier, validate its canonical path against the credential denies, and make the live probe exercise `bun test` through that same PATH.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts using a system Bun while the verifier's PATH selects `~/.bun/bin/bun`; the settings allow only the system binary, and the verifier's `bun test` remains blocked despite the smoke probe passing.

output.summary: Reviewed the sandbox settings, verifier invocation path, and smoke probe. Targeted tests could not start because this checkout has no local dependencies and the inherited Zod version lacks prefault.

findings.title: Allow the Bun executable the verifier will actually run
findings.detail: The read exception is derived from the daemon's process.execPath, but a verifier normally invokes `bun test` through its PATH. Those can resolve to different Bun installations. If the PATH-selected executable is under a denied private root, it remains unreadable and verification still cannot run tests. The new smoke probe also invokes process.execPath directly, so it can pass while the verifier's ordinary command fails.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the Bun executable using the same PATH supplied to the reader, validate and allow that executable, and have the smoke probe run `bun test` through that PATH.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts with /opt/homebrew/bin/bun while its reader PATH resolves bun to ~/.bun/bin/bun. Only the former receives the exception, while the latter remains under the home-wide read deny.

output.summary: Reviewed the publication paths and squash delivery. The targeted test files could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. A standalone targeted probe reproduced an unsanitized local file URL.

findings.title: Local file URLs bypass path sanitization
findings.detail: The rewrite requires the link destination to start with the worktree or data directory. A Markdown file URL starts with file://, so it is returned unchanged and can publish the owner's absolute path. Once the username is included in the private-string list, it can also block delivery. A targeted probe using the extracted function produced: `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts)` → `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts)`.
findings.suggestion: Recognize local file URL destinations, convert them to filesystem paths before checking the roots, and add a publication test for them.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer report contains `[file](file:///Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/src/a.ts)`; the PR body publishes the absolute local URL unchanged.

findings.title: Escape the data placeholder for Markdown publication
findings.detail: The replacement emits `<data>` as raw Markdown. GitHub interprets it as an HTML tag and sanitizes the unrecognized element, so readers do not see the required placeholder; a published log path appears as `/runs/log.txt` instead of `<data>/runs/log.txt`.
findings.suggestion: Emit an escaped or entity-encoded placeholder that renders as literal `<data>` on GitHub, and cover the rendered Markdown behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: A report containing a link to `/factory/data/runs/log.txt` is published as raw `<data>/runs/log.txt`; GitHub removes the tag when rendering it.

output.summary: Reviewed the shared sanitizer and its delivery and land call sites. The targeted test could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package; direct sanitizer probes reproduced two privacy defects.

findings.title: Absolute paths in Markdown link labels pass through unchanged
findings.detail: The link matcher consumes the entire Markdown link, but rewriting considers only its destination. When the destination is relative, the original link is returned unchanged even if its visible label contains an absolute worktree or data-directory path. This can publish the owner's username and local directory layout, or block delivery once the username is added to private strings.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize path occurrences in link labels as well as destinations, while preserving ordinary relative links.
findings.failure_scenario: A report containing `[/factory/data/work/run/file.ts](file.ts)` is published unchanged because `file.ts` is a relative destination.

findings.title: Normalize traversal before classifying paths
findings.detail: The containment check uses a textual prefix without resolving `..` components. A path that starts inside the worktree but resolves outside it is consequently published as a repo-relative path rather than a `<data>` path. It can expose the names and layout of other runs or scratch files and produces a broken repository link.
findings.suggestion: Normalize path components before checking whether a local path belongs to the worktree or the factory data directory.
findings.failure_scenario: With worktree `/factory/data/work/run`, `/factory/data/work/run/../other/secret` is rewritten to `../other/secret` instead of a `<data>` placeholder.

output.summary: The outcome writes are fenced, but a reclaimed worker can still issue a merge or push inside the Git helpers and can remove the new worker’s checkout. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts` could not start because `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js` is missing.

findings.title: Fence the actual merge and push commands after helper awaits
findings.detail: The ownership checks run before calling helpers that themselves await several operations before issuing the external command. `mergePullRequest` awaits a PR view before invoking `gh pr merge`, and `pushExistingBranch` awaits revision resolution, remote lookup and an ancestry check before invoking `git push`. A reclaim during any of those awaits is invisible until the next heartbeat, so the old worker can still merge or push after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helpers and check it immediately before each merge or push attempt, including retries. Add tests that defer an internal preflight read, reclaim the entry, and verify the command is never issued.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker starts `mergePullRequest`, its `gh pr view` is deferred, another owner reclaims the entry, and the view returns before the heartbeat; the old worker then executes `gh pr merge`.

findings.title: Prevent a stale worker from deleting the reclaimed worker’s checkout
findings.detail: The new claim checks throw on ownership loss, but the enclosing `finally` still calls `discard` on a path shared by all attempts for the entry. If the new owner has already recreated that checkout, the stale worker removes its worktree and directory, disrupting the new attempt despite the requirement that a worker which lost its claim write nothing.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts independently owned checkout paths or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a checkout belonging to a newer claim. Cover the overlapping cleanup and reclaim sequence.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker is awaiting CI in `land-<id>`, another process reclaims the entry and recreates `land-<id>`, then the old CI response arrives and the old worker's `finally` removes the new checkout.

output.summary: The new checks protect outcome writes after a reclaim, but they do not prevent an already-started merge or push helper from issuing its command after the claim is lost. The targeted land queue test could not run because the checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge and push helpers before their commands
findings.detail: The ownership check precedes calling mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing gh pr merge, and can also retry after further awaits. A reclaim during one of those waits leaves the old worker free to issue a merge before its heartbeat aborts. The same gap exists in pushApproved: pushExistingBranch awaits Git operations before issuing its push. Checking ownership after either helper returns is too late to prevent those side effects.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helpers and invoke it immediately before each merge or push command, including retry attempts. Add deferred tests at those internal boundaries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters mergePullRequest and waits for gh pr view. Another owner reclaims the stale entry, then the view returns before the old heartbeat fires. The old worker issues gh pr merge despite no longer owning the claim.

output.summary: Reviewed the claim checks, merge and push paths, CI classification, and worktree cleanup. The targeted test command could not start because the checkout is missing the entities package.

findings.title: A rejected rerun can remain pending forever after a reclaim
findings.detail: The rerun claim is persisted before the POST. If ownership changes while that request is pending, the new guard discards even a definitive rejection response. The replacement worker sees the persisted rerun_requested record, but its reconciliation only resolves it when GitHub reports a later workflow attempt. A rejected POST creates no later attempt, so CI remains pending indefinitely and the land queue cannot finish.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable reconciliation path for an interrupted rerun request that can resolve a definitive refusal without allowing the stale worker to write after losing its claim. Extend the reclaim test to run the replacement worker through the rejected response scenario.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient CI failure triggers a rerun POST; another worker reclaims the land entry before GitHub responds with HTTP 422. The old worker discards the response, and subsequent inspections keep waiting for a workflow attempt that will never exist.

output.summary: Reviewed claim checks across landing, push, merge, CI inspection, and checkout cleanup. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency: `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts test/ci-classifier.test.ts test/github-delivery.test.ts` failed during module loading with `Cannot find package 'entities' from 'src/gates/publication.ts'`.

findings.title: A rejected push leaves a misleading resume checkpoint
findings.detail: The worker records pushedSha before pushExistingBranch reaches its new ownership guard. If another worker reclaims the entry while that helper is awaiting its remote lookup or ancestry check, the guard prevents the push, but the replacement inherits pushedSha and treats that commit as already published. It then waits for CI on a SHA GitHub has never received and eventually blocks the land.
findings.suggestion: Make the resume path distinguish a prepared push from a confirmed publication and safely complete or reconcile the push when the remote still has the approved SHA.
findings.failure_scenario: The base merge produces a new head; the old worker records it as pushedSha, loses its claim during pushExistingBranch's remote lookup, and the guard refuses the push. The new owner resumes against the still-unmodified PR head and cannot observe CI for the recorded SHA.

findings.title: A stale worker can still write into the replacement's gate log
findings.detail: Gate result callbacks append to a log path shared by all attempts without checking ownership. A reclaimed worker can therefore append its old results after the replacement has truncated or started writing the same file, leaving the newer claim's diagnostic log mixed with stale output. This also falls short of the request that a worker which lost its claim writes nothing.
findings.suggestion: Use an attempt-specific log path and guard result writes against claim loss.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate completes after its entry is reclaimed and the replacement has begun checks; the old onResult callback appends its output to the replacement's land log before the next heartbeat detects the loss.

output.summary: Reviewed the land queue, persistence, CLI and CI paths. The land store tests passed. The queue tests could not load because the checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js, so their behavior could not be verified by execution.

findings.title: PR numbers cannot identify an unowned PR
findings.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, although the requested command is `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>` and the existing command accepts PR numbers. A number with no matching factory run is rejected as `run not found`; if the same number belongs to a factory PR on another configured repository, the earlier lookup selects that run instead.
findings.suggestion: Resolve PR-number targets against an unambiguous configured repository, and require a repository-qualified target when the number is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless land 77 --sha <full sha>` for a hand-opened PR and receives `run not found` even though the PR is open on a configured repository.

findings.title: All fork pull requests are refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories, but this unconditional guard excludes PRs whose head is in a fork. Those PRs cannot use the new confined land path, even when the head is current and the branch is writable.
findings.suggestion: Support fork heads through the same pinned checks and merge flow, reporting a clear failure if the required branch update cannot be pushed.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository and has the supplied current SHA; the request fails with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`.

findings.title: Rollback permanently blocks in-flight unowned lands
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel satisfies the old schema, but the previous release treats every land entry as owned and looks up that string as a run ID. If a deploy rolls back while an unowned entry is queued or in progress, the older daemon claims it and marks it blocked because the run is gone. Returning to the new release will not resume the now-terminal entry.
findings.suggestion: Make unowned entries invisible to the previous release's queue consumer while retaining durable progress for the new release.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon is rolled back while an unowned land is waiting for CI; the previous release resumes it, fails to find run `""`, and records a blocked land.

output.summary: Reviewed the queue, persistence, CLI and UI paths. The focused store tests passed; the queue tests could not load because the MCP SDK dependency is missing from the checkout.

findings.title: Allow pull requests opened from forks
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories, but this check rejects every cross-repository PR. A contributor's fork is a normal source for such a PR, and the request does not exclude it.
findings.suggestion: Support fork-backed PR heads through the same pinned approval, confined checks and exact-head merge flow.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targets a configured repository but its head branch belongs to the contributor's fork; requesting its land fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

findings.title: Preserve active unowned lands across rollback
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel is readable by the previous release, but its queue treats that value as a required run ID. After rollback, the old worker claims an active unowned entry and permanently blocks it with "run  is gone", losing its resumable progress.
findings.suggestion: Use a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy that prevents an older worker from claiming and blocking entries it cannot handle.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when deployment rolls back to the previous release; the restarted old daemon claims it and changes it to blocked.

findings.title: Expose unowned land entries in the UI
findings.detail: The change creates runless entries and API feed events, but adds no UI path for displaying them. The existing UI associates land activity with run details, so an entry with no run has no corresponding screen. This leaves the request's UI acceptance criterion unmet.
findings.suggestion: Add a UI view that lists and identifies unowned land entries alongside factory lands.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator queues a hand-made PR and opens the UI to inspect its status or blocked reason; there is no run detail or land queue view through which to find it.

output.summary: Reviewed persistence, recovery, and the targeted cleanup tests. Eight tests passed; three startup and resume tests could not run because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing.

findings.title: Recovery loses descendants that were not yet claimed
findings.detail: Recovery only visits recorded PIDs and then deletes the invocation's records. Cleanup discovers processes in repeated sweeps, so a descendant forked after a sweep's snapshot is not recorded until a later sweep. If the daemon dies after freezing the recorded members but before that sweep, recovery kills the recorded members and permits the run to continue while the unrecorded descendant remains alive and can write to the checkout.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation ownership information to resume discovery as well as killing the recorded set, and do not clear the record until the resumed sweep confirms that no owned descendants remain.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked parent forks a child after the initial process snapshot; cleanup freezes the parent, then the daemon crashes before the next scan. On restart only the parent is killed and the new child survives.

findings.title: Persisted Linux birth identities do not distinguish boots
findings.detail: On Linux, processBirth returns the boot-relative start tick alone. A cleanup record can survive a reboot, after which an unrelated process can receive both the recorded PID and the same start tick. Recovery treats that as the original member and sends it SIGKILL.
findings.suggestion: Include a boot identity in persisted Linux process identities and treat a changed boot as proof that the old process is gone.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon crashes with a pending record, the host reboots, and a new process receives the same PID and boot-relative start tick before recovery runs.

output.summary: Reviewed persistence, recovery, and run-resume paths. The targeted cleanup test had one timeout that passed in isolation; three integration cases could not run because the local @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency was missing.

findings.title: A crash during discovery leaves unrecorded descendants running
findings.detail: Ownership is persisted one member at a time, and recovery only visits persisted members. If the daemon dies during the first discovery pass, before all identified processes have been recorded, the remaining marked descendants have no durable record. Recovery can delete the partial record and allow the next invocation to run while those descendants still have access to the checkout. The same problem occurs if the first ownership write fails: no record remains to block a later resume.
findings.suggestion: Persist an invocation-level cleanup record before discovery or signalling, and make recovery finish discovering and terminating its marked descendants before clearing that record and allowing the checkout to be reused.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation has two marked sleepers; the daemon dies after recording the first sleeper but before recording the second. On restart, recovery kills the recorded sleeper, clears the invocation, and leaves the second sleeper running.

findings.title: Linux birth identities can match unrelated processes after a reboot
findings.detail: On Linux, processBirth records only the boot-relative start tick. Persisted records survive a reboot, but those ticks and PIDs are reused on the next boot. An unrelated process with the same PID and start tick will pass this comparison and receive SIGKILL.
findings.suggestion: Include the Linux boot ID in the persisted identity and require it to match before signalling a recorded PID.
findings.failure_scenario: The machine reboots with a pending cleanup record; a new process receives the recorded PID and starts at the same boot-relative tick as the old process. Daemon startup kills the new process.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, and test-start markers. The targeted test passed on macOS; its two Linux-only timeout tests were skipped, so their behavior could not be verified here. The workflow change also requires the audit's stated `Allow: workflows` authorization.

Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, and marker tests. The marker test passed on macOS; the GNU timeout tests were skipped because this host is not Linux. The workflow change is explicitly requested, although the automated audit reports that it requires an Allow: workflows allowance.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup misses detached test subprocesses
findings.detail: Both cleanup signals target only the timeout process group. The suite routinely starts subprocesses in separate sessions through runProcess, which uses detached: true, so those descendants are outside that group and survive when their test worker is killed. This fails the requested child cleanup and can leave a hung subprocess running or holding inherited output open after the step times out. The existing timeout test covers only children that remain in the original group.
findings.suggestion: Capture and terminate the descendant tree, including separate process groups, before its parents disappear, and test a detached child that sleeps past the limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A test hangs while waiting for a detached subprocess started by runProcess; the timeout kills the Bun worker's process group but leaves that subprocess alive.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit, round-feedback, and publication-diagnostic paths. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package.

findings.title: Large text logs with terminal escapes bypass the size warning
findings.detail: The size map excludes every blob that fails reviewableText, even when Git classifies it as text. That predicate rejects control bytes such as the ESC used in ANSI-colored command output, so a large new gate log can bypass the warning intended to catch scratch output.
findings.suggestion: Record sizes for files classified as text without requiring the stricter executable-content reviewability check.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer commits a 200 KiB UTF-8 gate log containing ANSI color escape sequences at report.txt. Git classifies it as text, but its size is omitted from headTextSizes and auditDiff emits no large-text-addition warning.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit, feedback, and publication paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Large text logs with terminal escapes do not receive the size warning
findings.detail: The size map excludes files that fail reviewableText, which rejects ANSI escape bytes. Git still treats a NUL-free UTF-8 log containing those bytes as text, but auditDiff receives no size for it and does not issue the requested large-text warning.
findings.suggestion: Record sizes for text files independently of the stricter reviewable-text classification, and add a test with a large ANSI-colored log.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer adds a 150 KiB gate log at reports/output.txt containing ANSI color sequences. It is outside a root hidden directory and receives neither of the new scratch-output warnings.

output.summary: The audit filename checks include registered credentials, but the production publication paths do not. The new base64 decoder also misses nested encodings. The targeted test files could not run because the checkout has no installed dependencies: Bun could not resolve the entities package.

findings.title: Publication checks do not include registered credentials
findings.detail: publicationMatches only checks the entries supplied by its caller. Production publication callers supply private-strings entries, not registered credentials, so the new base64 support does not prevent a base64-encoded credential from being published. The new test constructs a combined list manually, which does not exercise those callers. A targeted probe, `bun -e 'import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; import { registerCredential } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const secret="synthetic-publication-credential"; registerCredential("review", secret); const encoded=Buffer.from(secret).toString("base64"); console.log(JSON.stringify(privateMatches(encoded, [])));'`, printed `[]`.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected entries used by every production publication check, including blob checks, and test through a production publication entry point.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential absent from private-strings.txt is base64-encoded in a staged file or PR text; the publication check accepts it.

findings.title: Base64 decoding stops before other encoding layers can be examined
findings.detail: base64Match replaces a run only if its first decoded form already contains the protected value. Consequently, the existing successive decoding loop never sees a percent-encoded credential wrapped in base64, or a credential encoded in base64 twice. A targeted `privateMatches` probe returned `[]` for both forms while returning a match for a single base64 encoding.
findings.suggestion: Inspect bounded successive decoding combinations before deciding that a base64 run is unrelated, while retaining a bound on work and false positives.
findings.failure_scenario: An audit filename contains the base64 encoding of a percent-encoded registered credential; the filename and diagnostic are retained with the encoded credential instead of being withheld.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit and publication redaction paths. Focused tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities dependency. A direct decoder probe confirmed that nested base64 encodings are missed.

findings.title: Publication checks do not include registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 matcher only checks the entries supplied by its caller. Production publication calls supply private-strings entries, while registered credentials are added only to the filename diagnosis. Literal credential redaction does not remove their base64 encodings, so encoded credentials can still be published in PR text or repository content. The added publication test manually supplies credentials and therefore does not exercise the production path.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the authoritative publication checks for text and published content, and test through a production caller.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential that is absent from private-strings.txt appears base64-encoded in a PR body or changed file; publication proceeds with the encoded credential intact.

findings.title: Base64 decoding stops before inspecting nested encodings
findings.detail: A base64 run is decoded only when its immediate decoded bytes already contain the protected value. Consequently, base64-wrapped percent encodings and double-base64 encodings never reach the successive decoding layers, including in audit filenames. A targeted `bun -e` probe calling `privateMatches` with the credential `synthetic-secret-value` returned `base64 of percent ... []` and `double base64 ... []` for both encodings.
findings.suggestion: Inspect bounded successive decoding of candidate base64 runs before deciding whether they contain a protected value, and cover nested encodings in publication and audit tests.
findings.failure_scenario: An audit filename contains the base64 encoding of the percent-encoded registered credential; the filename and diagnostic retain the encoded secret instead of being withheld.

output.summary: Reviewed the stored invocation aggregation and its CLI and HTTP callers. The targeted test command reported 19 passes, 11 failures and one error; CLI tests could not start because the installed Zod lacks prefault, and the HTTP test could not load the MCP SDK module. Those environment failures are not treated as findings.

findings.title: Panel eval work is attributed to one provider and invocation
findings.detail: A trial without implementation rounds is represented as one provider call using the trial's model and provider, but review panel trials can combine several finder and verifier calls, potentially across providers. Their combined tokens and cost are therefore charged entirely to the trial's target, and the invocation count and success share do not describe the calls actually made.
findings.suggestion: Use persisted per-call evidence where available, and avoid attributing combined panel usage to a single provider when its constituent calls cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A review panel invokes provider A and a verifier on provider B; the result reports one invocation and all combined cost under A, with no corresponding work under B.

findings.title: Implementation evals discard stored cache totals
findings.detail: Every eval with round evidence sets both cache measurements to null, even though the trial stores aggregate cache-read and cache-write totals. Since summarize returns null if any row lacks a measurement, a single implementation eval makes the provider's entire eval cache and uncached-input totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the trial-level cache totals in aggregates where they can be attributed, while retaining unknown values only for breakdowns whose allocation cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens; its provider's eval totals report both as null instead of the stored amounts.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and invocation storage paths. The targeted workload tests passed, but the HTTP and CLI checks could not run successfully because the installed dependencies lacked the MCP client module and a compatible Zod version.

findings.title: Review panel calls are attributed to the trial's provider
findings.detail: A review trial can invoke multiple finders and verifiers on different providers and models. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial totals, but this code assigns those totals to the trial's selected provider and model and counts them as one invocation. The resulting provider workload can charge one provider for another provider's work and omit the latter entirely.
findings.suggestion: Use individually attributed call records where available. Where the stored trial cannot distinguish the calls, expose the attribution as unknown rather than assigning the combined work to the selected provider and model.
findings.failure_scenario: A review trial selects provider A and invokes a verifier on provider B; the statistics report both calls' combined tokens and cost as one invocation for A, with no corresponding work for B.

findings.title: Recorded eval rounds discard available cache-token totals
findings.detail: The eval runner accumulates cache-read and cache-write tokens on the trial even when it records rounds. This code replaces both values with null for every round, so a single ordinary implementation eval makes the provider's aggregate cached and uncached input totals unknown even when the stored trial supplies those totals.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache totals in aggregates where their attribution is known, while marking only genuinely unavailable per-round breakdowns unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation eval with one recorded round and stored cacheReadTokens of 100 reports null cache-read and input-token totals for its provider instead of the recorded values.

output.summary: Reviewed signature selection, excerpt construction, and rerun compatibility. The targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities dependency. Direct probes reproduced two evidence-selection defects.

findings.title: An unrelated later test can replace the first failure signature
findings.detail: After an error line, the search treats the next failure-shaped line as belonging to the same Bun assertion block, regardless of intervening content or distance. An earlier independent error can therefore be attributed to a later failing test, and changes to the earlier failure will not change the signature.
findings.suggestion: Associate an error with a Bun test result only when the intervening lines establish that they belong to the same failure block; otherwise retain the error line.
findings.failure_scenario: For `error: first failure\n(fail) unrelated later test`, ciSignature returns `(fail) unrelated later test` as the signature line.

findings.title: A long failing test name can be absent from its excerpt
findings.detail: For a Bun assertion block, the tail window keeps the end of the block. If the failing test name alone exceeds that window, it drops the beginning of the chosen signature line, including `(fail)`. The resulting excerpt does not identify the selected failure.
findings.suggestion: Reserve space for the beginning of the selected signature line when constructing the excerpt.
findings.failure_scenario: With `error: assertion`, a 3,000-character diff, and a `(fail)` line containing a 2,500-character test name, ciSignature returns the failing line as its signature but its 1,999-character excerpt does not contain `(fail)`.

findings.title: Change substantially exceeds the requested line budget
findings.detail: The request budgets about 80 lines including tests; this diff adds 354 lines and deletes 36, including a generalized credential-redaction window API. The overrun increases the review and maintenance surface and was not explained in an implementer report.
findings.suggestion: Reduce the change toward the stated budget or explain why the additional scope is necessary.
findings.failure_scenario: Reviewers must assess changes to the shared credential redactor and extensive unrelated window behavior for a CI evidence-selection fix.

output.summary: Reviewed failure selection, excerpt construction, rerun compatibility, and credential redaction. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout lacks the entities package; a direct Bun probe exposed one excerpt edge case.

findings.title: Long Bun failure names lose their identifying prefix in the excerpt
findings.detail: When an assertion is followed by a sufficiently long failing test line, the tail window takes the end of that line. The excerpt then omits the `(fail)` prefix and the beginning of the chosen signature line, leaving the fix round without the identifying part of the test name. A targeted probe, `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(ciSignature("test", "error: assertion failed\n(fail) " + "x".repeat(2200), "fallback")))'`, returned a line beginning `(fail) xxx...` but an excerpt beginning `error: assertion failed\nxxx...`, with no `(fail)` marker.
findings.suggestion: Reserve space for the beginning of the selected failure line when building the excerpt tail.
findings.failure_scenario: A Bun assertion is followed by a failing test name longer than the remaining excerpt budget.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker execution, event reporting, checkout, and fencing paths. Targeted tests could not load: `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/agent-test.test.ts` reported missing package `entities` and an incompatible Zod installation (`floors.prefault is not a function`).

findings.title: Event sequence numbers restart when a job is retried
findings.detail: Each attempt starts at sequence zero, but event rows are keyed by job ID and sequence and the coordinator silently ignores conflicts. Events from a later attempt can therefore be discarded while the job completes with a transcript from an earlier attempt.
findings.suggestion: Make event sequences unique across attempts, or explicitly reset or separate the stored event stream when an attempt is reassigned.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batch 0 and then loses its lease. Worker B runs the requeued job and posts its own batch 0; the coordinator ignores it as a conflict and can still accept worker B's result.

findings.title: A rejected event batch aborts without reporting failure
findings.detail: The rejection handler aborts the job controller, so the catch block subsequently skips the failure POST because `jobSignal.aborted` is true. The coordinator retains a leased job until its lease expires instead of promptly recording the batch failure and requeueing it.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish event-post failures from cancellation and report a sanitized failure using a separate bounded signal while the lease is still held.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an oversized or invalid event batch with HTTP 400 while the lease is valid. The worker stops the harness and removes the job locally, but sends no failure report; the job remains leased until expiry.

findings.title: Polling fence can leave agents running beyond the lease period
findings.detail: The fence only checks at heartbeat-sized intervals, so a failed heartbeat immediately after a check can leave an agent running for almost one additional interval after the lease period has elapsed. The coordinator may already have expired and reassigned the lease while the original harness continues consuming quota.
findings.suggestion: Schedule or reset a one-shot fencing deadline from each successful heartbeat, and abort jobs as soon as that deadline expires.
findings.failure_scenario: With the default 60-second lease and 10-second heartbeat interval, a last successful heartbeat just after a fence check can leave a partitioned agent running for nearly 70 seconds after that success.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker lease, execution, event, and fencing paths. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` package; it exited before running tests.

findings.title: A rejected event batch leaves the job leased
findings.detail: A rejected event post aborts the job controller. The error handler then skips the failure post because the job signal is aborted, so the coordinator retains the lease until it expires instead of immediately failing the attempt. The new rejection test only checks that the job is not done and therefore accepts this outcome.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish an event-post failure from cancellation, abort the harness, and report the failure using a signal that remains usable for the failure request.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator returns 400 for an invalid event batch while the worker still holds the lease. The harness stops, but no failure is posted and the job remains leased until a later sweep.

findings.title: Fencing can occur a heartbeat interval after lease expiry
findings.detail: The fence checks elapsed time only once per heartbeat interval and uses a strict greater-than comparison. With the default 60-second lease and 10-second interval, an agent can continue running for nearly 70 seconds after the last successful heartbeat, after the coordinator can expire and reassign its lease.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing for the lease deadline derived from the last successful heartbeat, resetting the timer on each success, and prevent starting an agent when that deadline has passed.
findings.failure_scenario: Heartbeats fail immediately after a successful heartbeat. The coordinator expires the lease at 60 seconds, but the worker's next fence check can occur at approximately 70 seconds, allowing overlapping paid sessions.

findings.title: Batching by event count can exceed the server's body limit
findings.detail: The worker flushes only by event count or time, while the events endpoint accepts at most 1 MiB. A single large tool result, or a batch of smaller results exceeding that limit, cannot be accepted. Depending on the server response, the worker either abandons the lease or retries the same oversized batch until the attempt ends.
findings.suggestion: Bound batches by serialized byte size as well as event count, and define a way to handle an individual event that exceeds the endpoint limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A harness emits a tool result containing more than 1 MiB of output. The resulting events request exceeds the endpoint's read limit and the otherwise valid session cannot complete.

output.summary: Reviewed the restart, reconciliation, adoption, and worker-reporting paths. The targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` package: `bun test test/lan-agent.test.ts test/agent-jobs.test.ts` failed during module loading.

findings.title: Restart grace expires at the freshness threshold instead of one lease period
findings.detail: The freshness check fails a resumed job once `fresh` has elapsed from `resumedAt`, even though its lease receives a full lease-period extension. With the default timings, this happens after 30 seconds rather than the documented 60-second lease period. A result arriving during the remaining lease window is rejected because the result route sweeps first.
findings.suggestion: Keep resumed jobs eligible for the full restart lease period before applying the stale-heartbeat failure, while retaining the attempt deadline.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushed while the coordinator was down and reconnects 40 seconds after restart. The first sweep marks its job disconnected before accepting its result, so the pushed commit cannot be adopted and the run can end NeedsHuman.

output.summary: Reviewed worker restart, reconciliation, adoption, and late-report paths. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities package.

findings.title: Check for an unreported push before falling back from a dirty worktree
findings.detail: When reconciliation rejects an open job, the executor cancels it and proceeds to prepare(). If the worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs locally without detecting a commit already pushed by the cancelled worker. This bypasses the required NeedsHuman outcome for a push without an accepted report.
findings.suggestion: After cancelling a rejected open job, check its remote branch against the stored request before any local fallback, including when prepare() cannot publish because the worktree is dirty.
findings.failure_scenario: A leased worker pushes its commit while the coordinator is down. Before restart, the coordinator worktree becomes dirty. Reconciliation rejects and cancels the job, prepare() returns null on the dirty worktree, and a local session starts even though the remote contains an unreported worker commit.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker dispatch, refusal, result validation, and review routing paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` dependency: `bun test test/lan-agent.test.ts test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts test/workers.test.ts test/config-routing.test.ts` reported `Cannot find package 'entities'` and ran zero tests.

findings.title: Keep local panel finders off workers when review models are pinned
findings.detail: The shared review call supplies checkout metadata to local finders too. Their `free_only` routing constraint does not enforce locality when a run pins review models: the router ignores the billing filter for a pinned chain. A pinned Claude or Codex target without backend credentials therefore satisfies worker eligibility and runs the local finder on a worker, contrary to the request.
findings.suggestion: Carry the finder's local-only intent to the shared call and omit checkout metadata or otherwise prevent worker dispatch for that call.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel has a finder configured with `local: true`, the run pins a Claude review model, and review workers are enabled for the repository. The finder creates a worker job instead of running locally.

output.summary: Reviewed worker dispatch, validation, fallback, restart, and review routing. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Keep local panel finders off workers when the review model is pinned
findings.detail: The shared review call supplies checkout metadata to every finder, and worker eligibility does not retain the finder's local designation. A run-level review model chain overrides the free-only routing constraint, so a local finder can select a Claude or Codex subscription target and become eligible for worker dispatch. This violates the requirement that local finders stay local.
findings.suggestion: Carry the local-finder designation into the call and omit worker checkout metadata or otherwise explicitly prevent worker dispatch for that finder.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel has a finder configured with local = true, the run pins its review model to a Claude or Codex target, and workers are enabled for review. The local finder is queued on a worker instead of running locally.

output.summary: Reviewed the generator, eval runner, report format, and repository cache. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. The checkout also contains no implement dataset at the generator's default path.

findings.title: The documented generator cannot start from this checkout
findings.detail: The generator immediately reads the default implement cases file, but this revision contains no evals/implement directory or cases.json. The documented command therefore exits with ENOENT before fetching or validating any PR. The tests mask this by always supplying a separately created casePath.
findings.suggestion: Provide the dataset at the expected path or add a supported initialization and dataset-location mechanism that works from a fresh checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: Run bun scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts --repo owner/name --pr 123 from a fresh checkout of this revision; reading evals/implement/cases.json fails.

findings.title: The replay-v2 tag cannot select the generated cases
findings.detail: The requirement says a v2 eval selects the tagged cases with --cases, but the existing CLI passes those values as case IDs and validateRequest rejects anything that is not an ID. findings.title: Verify the snapshot checkout's HEAD before recording evidence
findings.detail: The result is recorded under the original tree hash without checking whether setup or the test command changed the snapshot checkout's HEAD. The normal gates stage explicitly checks HEAD before creating gate evidence. A command can therefore run tests against another revision and have that result reused as evidence for the original tree.

findings.title: Apply the gates-stage timeout retry to session gate runs

It returns the first timeout to the implementer and refuses to record it, so the gates stage subsequently runs the full suite again. This differs from the normal gate behavior and defeats the requested reuse when a transient timeout is followed by a successful retry.
findings.suggestion: Use the same bounded timeout retry and first-attempt recording as the gates stage before deciding whether the execution is reusable.
findings.failure_scenario: The first full-suite attempt times out transiently, while a second attempt would pass. The session reports failure and the gates stage runs the suite again instead of carrying the normal retry result forward.

findings.title: Snapshot gate runs against a different commit than the round
findings.detail: The snapshot checkout uses a synthetic commit with its own SHA and message, but reuse is keyed only by tree. findings.title: Record gate evidence even if the check changes HEAD

The normal gates stage explicitly checks HEAD before producing gate evidence, because a check that moves HEAD cannot attest to the checked commit. Reusing this record bypasses that safeguard and can make verify accept a result produced against another revision.

output.summary: Reviewed the executor, lease and restart paths. The targeted command `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts` could not run because the checkout lacks the `entities` package; no test assertions ran.

findings.title: Serialize job creation per worktree
findings.detail: The check for existing jobs and the insertion of the new job happen separately, with an await and checkpoint between them. Two callers can both see an empty worktree and enqueue jobs for it. With two executor processes, both jobs can then lease and run concurrently in the same checkout.
findings.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusivity atomically when creating or leasing a job, and retain ownership until the previous job is confirmed stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: Two gate requests for the same cwd start concurrently while no prior job exists; each passes the query, then each enqueues a job that a different executor leases.

findings.title: Use a fresh executor heartbeat, not only process existence
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only the PID and process birth time; there is no heartbeat timestamp. A stopped or wedged executor therefore remains available indefinitely. After its job lease expires, waitStopped also waits indefinitely for that same live but unresponsive process, so the daemon cannot fall back or resume the run.
findings.suggestion: Track executor freshness and provide a bounded, safe recovery path that confirms its gate processes have stopped before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor is suspended or its event loop hangs while running a gate. Its lease expires, but its PID remains alive, so the daemon remains in waitStopped forever.

findings.title: Resume targeted retry jobs
findings.detail: The resume predicate only permits baseline, initial and rebase purposes. A restart during an in-place targeted regression retry treats the durable handle as a mismatch and cancels the surviving job instead of attaching to it. The resumed stage starts its earlier gate work again, defeating the requested restart behavior for targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough stage progress to resume the targeted retry at its recorded purpose and attach to its matching leased job.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long regression-retry-targeted job is leased and running; the resumed gates stage cancels that job and reruns gate work.

findings.title: Do not reattach to an unleased queued job
findings.detail: A queued in-place job is considered resumable whenever any executor process exists. The request explicitly limits reattachment to jobs whose lease is still held by their executor. This path instead preserves a job that was never picked up and waits for its pickup timeout.
findings.suggestion: Require a live matching executor lease for reattachment and cancel or replace queued jobs on resume.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after enqueueing but before an executor leases the job; the resumed stage attaches to the queued row and waits rather than starting fresh.

findings.title: Interrupted retry gates are cancelled instead of reattached
