A targeted or full retry has a durable in-place handle, but after a daemon restart the stage's earlier resume check treats that handle as a mismatch and cancels it. The stage then repeats earlier gate work rather than receiving the running retry's result.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the recorded retry at its original purpose and attach while its lease is valid.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted check is running; the new daemon cancels that job and reruns gate work.

findings.title: Process existence is treated as a fresh executor heartbeat
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only the PID and process birth time; the executor never records a heartbeat. If its event loop stalls while a job is running, the lease expires, but waitStopped continues waiting for the still-existing process indefinitely. The daemon cannot fall back or start another gate, and the abort-free discard path can also block restart recovery indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Track executor freshness and provide a bounded, safe recovery path for an unresponsive owner that confirms its gate processes have stopped before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops responding during a gate. The job lease expires, yet the daemon waits forever for stopped=1.

findings.title: Single-flight can bypass reattachment to a surviving baseline
findings.detail: The cache lookup bypasses cached results when a prepare handle exists, but the surrounding singleFlight can return another run's result without invoking that lookup or runBaseline. The resumed run then retains its in-place handle and proceeds while its own executor job may still be modifying its worktree.
findings.suggestion: Bypass single-flight whenever a surviving prepare gate must be attached, and wait for that job before advancing the run.
findings.failure_scenario: After restart, another run becomes the single-flight leader for the same baseline key before the resumed run reaches this call. The resumed run consumes the leader's passing result while its own baseline job is still running.

findings.title: Recognize structured authentication failures during retries
findings.detail: The captured stream reports `error_status: 401` and `error: authentication_failed` in `system/api_retry` events, but the parser ignores those events. If the invocation reaches its timeout or idle timeout before Claude emits the final assistant and result events, it is returned as a timeout or stuck result without an authentication classification. On a worker that result is returned as the round result, so an implementer that never authenticated can still consume a round and proceed to gates.
findings.suggestion: Track the structured authentication rejection in retry events and preserve that classification when the process ends before a terminal result, while retaining explicit caller cancellation.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude emits the fixture's 401 `api_retry` events and is terminated by the invocation deadline before its final result; the worker returns a timeout and the coordinator continues the implementation round.

findings.title: Avoid rerunning a worker session that already made changes
findings.detail: The parser classifies any final 401 as an authentication failure, including one after a session has already executed tools. The worker publishes its changes and this path adopts the resulting commit before unconditionally invoking the same round locally. A token expiring during a session can therefore cause the local implementer to repeat work or side effects that the worker already performed; a coordinator-side failure likewise falls back on an already modified worktree.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a login rejection before the session ran from an authentication error after meaningful session activity, and only apply the no-session fallback to the former.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker implementer edits files or runs a command, then its next model request receives a 401. Its changes are published and adopted, after which the local implementer runs the original prompt again.

output.summary: Reviewed the lifecycle, queue eligibility, notifier, and report changes. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk packages.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are restricted to enabled queue repositories
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation runs only when the issue queue is configured with trusted accounts, and it skips repositories outside the queue list. The request requires updates for issue-linked runs from every start path, independently of queue admission.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation for all configured repositories with issue-linked runs, independently of whether issue queue picking is enabled.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run with `Closes #7` in a repository without an enabled issue queue receives no lifecycle labels or comments.

findings.title: Status events can disappear before they are checkpointed
findings.detail: Comments for needs_human, failed, and cancelled are derived only from the run's current status. A pending effect is recorded only when polling reaches the comment write. If the status changes before that poll, or before a failed label write is retried, the event is lost permanently. A later needs_human episode is also suppressed by the single completed `comment:needs_human` cursor.
findings.suggestion: Persist lifecycle events and their intended effects at the state transition, with an identity for each status episode, and reconcile those durable records.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and the owner resumes it before the next poll; no needs-you comment is ever posted. If it later reaches needs_human again after an earlier comment was posted, that second episode is also never commented.

findings.title: Re-approval accepts a priority label that is no longer applied
findings.detail: The post-failure check accepts any trusted priority application event, even if that label was subsequently removed. A different priority label applied before the failure can remain current and satisfy the separate approved-label check, allowing the old approval to pick the issue again.
findings.suggestion: Require the post-failure trusted application to be the current trusted application of a priority label that remains on the issue.
findings.failure_scenario: An issue retains priority:2 from before failure; a trusted user applies and then removes priority:5 after failure. The issue is eligible using the old priority:2 approval despite no current post-failure approval.

findings.title: A completed label cursor prevents repair of later label changes
findings.detail: Once the stored label cursor equals the desired label, the reconciler never reads GitHub labels again for that run. Removing or changing a lifecycle label externally therefore persists indefinitely. In particular, removing the failed label can bypass the new failure-label eligibility guard for runs that are not recorded as issue-sourced runs.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the current GitHub label set rather than treating a previous successful write as proof that the label remains present.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed CLI run linked by `Closes #7` receives the failed label, which is later removed. The next poll does not restore it, and the queue has no issue-sourced latest run to require re-approval.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle events when they occur, not only when polled
findings.detail: The reconciler derives needs-human and failure comments solely from the run's current status. No pending effect is recorded until a poll observes that status, so a transition that occurs and is resolved between polls is permanently lost. The single `comment:needs_human` key also suppresses subsequent needs-human episodes for the same run.
findings.suggestion: Record each lifecycle event and its publication-safe payload durably when the transition occurs, then have the poller deliver each recorded event.

findings.title: Prevent re-pick while a failure label write is pending

The existing latest-run eligibility check only considers issue-source runs, so a failed CLI or MCP run linked by `Closes #n` provides no local re-approval guard. If writing its failure label fails, the queue sees the old trusted priority label and can immediately create a new run.

findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run with `Closes #7` fails, GitHub rejects the failed-label write, and issue #7 still has its original trusted priority label. The same poll selects #7 again without a new approval.

findings.title: Run lifecycle reconciliation outside enabled queue repositories
findings.detail: Lifecycle handling is restricted to repositories listed in an enabled issue queue, and the reconciler is started only with that queue. The request requires updates for every start path; it does not restrict lifecycle updates to repositories configured for automatic issue selection. Consequently, manual, MCP and webhook runs in other repositories receive no lifecycle labels or polling comments.
findings.suggestion: Start lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission and process linked runs for all applicable repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository has GitHub integration configured but is absent from `githubQueue.repos`; an owner starts a CLI run with `Closes #7`. No in-progress label or start comment is posted.

findings.title: Require the later approval to apply to a current priority label
findings.detail: The re-approval test accepts any trusted priority-label event after the failure, even if that label was subsequently removed. Separately, `approved` can be satisfied by a different priority label whose trusted application predates the failure. This combines unrelated historical events into an approval that is no longer present on the issue.

findings.failure_scenario: An issue retains priority:2 from before failure; after failure, a trusted user applies and then removes priority:1. The issue is eligible again although its only current approval predates the failure.

findings.title: Do not trust arbitrary issue comments as proof of a posted effect
findings.detail: On retry, any comment containing the predictable marker is treated as the factory's completed side effect, without checking its author. A user able to comment can insert that marker before a pending retry and cause the required factory comment to be marked done permanently.
findings.suggestion: Verify the comment was authored by the configured GitHub identity, or use another durable reconciliation mechanism that cannot be satisfied by untrusted comments.
findings.failure_scenario: A lifecycle comment POST fails, leaving its effect pending. An issue commenter posts `<!-- limitless-lifecycle:<run-id>:failed -->`; on the next poll the factory marks the failure comment done without posting its reason.

findings.suggestion: For a failed latest run, require evidence of the failure-label application followed by trusted priority re-approval, including while label delivery is pending.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails, a trusted user reapplies priority, and the subsequent failed-label GitHub write fails. The queue sees no failed label and admits the issue based on the priority event after `finishedAt`.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit, verify-change handling, worker publication, and delivery paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` dependency; Bun reported `Cannot find package 'entities'` before running any tests.

Reviewed the audit matcher, allowance parsing, verification handling, and local and worker publication paths. No concrete defect was identified. The targeted pipeline tests could not run because the checkout lacks the `entities` dependency.

Reviewed the rejection checkpoint and scheduler recovery. The targeted restart test could not run because the checkout lacks the entities package; the scheduler inspection reveals a production restart failure.

findings.title: Terminal status prevents interrupted rollback from resuming
findings.detail: The rejection is saved with status needs_human before rollback starts, but scheduler startup only requeues running and waiting_input runs. A restart after this write therefore never calls rollbackRejectedMerge. The new tests bypass the scheduler by calling executeRun directly, so they do not exercise actual daemon recovery. A rollback error or shutdown is also swallowed as needs_human, leaving no automatic retry.
findings.suggestion: Keep the rejection checkpoint in a resumable status until rollback completes, or explicitly teach scheduler recovery to resume incomplete rejected rollbacks. Exercise the restart through scheduler startup.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts immediately after the rejection update or after reset but before clean and the state save. The run remains needs_human with the merged checkout or incomplete cleanup and is never resumed.

output.summary: The rejection is persisted before rollback, but its terminal status prevents the scheduler from resuming interrupted rollback. The targeted restart test could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package.

findings.title: Keep an interrupted rejection eligible for scheduler recovery
findings.detail: The rejection checkpoint immediately sets the run to needs_human, but scheduler startup only requeues running and waiting_input runs. A daemon restart after this write therefore never calls rollbackRejectedMerge: the checkout and persisted head can remain at the rejected merge, or rollback can remain partially completed. The new tests call executeRun directly on the terminal run, bypassing the scheduler behavior that controls real restart recovery. Rollback errors are also caught and returned as needs_human without making the run eligible for another attempt.
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while leaving rollback recoverable by the scheduler, then mark the run needs_human after rollback completes. Exercise the crash windows through scheduler restart rather than invoking executeRun directly.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts immediately after the rejection checkpoint is saved, before git reset runs. On startup, the scheduler excludes the needs_human run, so the checkout remains at the rejected merged SHA and rollback never finishes.

output.summary: Reviewed the queue, webhook, and transaction paths. The targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`; it failed before executing tests.

findings.title: An initially empty repository discards its first commands
findings.detail: A successful poll with no open issues stores no boundary. When the first issue and command appear later, the next poll treats them as the initial snapshot and skips the command permanently. The added test at line 3015 explicitly expects this behavior, although the command arrived after the first successful poll.
findings.suggestion: Establish a durable GitHub-time enable boundary even when the first poll returns no open issues, and test a command posted after that poll.
findings.failure_scenario: The queue polls an empty repository successfully; a trusted user then opens an issue and posts `/limitless fix this`. Every subsequent poll skips that command.

findings.title: The boundary can precede commands posted before queue enablement
findings.detail: The maximum timestamp among currently open issues is not the time the queue was enabled. A closed issue can already have a newer command than every open issue in the first response. If it is reopened later, that old command passes the boundary check and starts a run, contrary to the explicit reopened-issue requirement.
findings.suggestion: Use a GitHub-derived enable boundary that also excludes pre-enable comments on issues absent from the first open-issue snapshot.
findings.failure_scenario: The newest open issue was updated on Monday; a trusted command was posted on a closed issue Tuesday; the queue is enabled Wednesday; reopening that issue Thursday causes the Tuesday command to run.

findings.title: Identity lookup failures bypass the factory-author check
findings.detail: A failed identity lookup is converted to null, but slash commands continue to be processed. With no bot login, the factory-author comparison cannot reject a factory-authored comment. If the bot login is included in the trusted list, such a comment can create a run despite the invariant that factory comments never do.
findings.suggestion: Leave commands retryable until the posting identity can be determined, so the factory-author exclusion can be enforced.
findings.failure_scenario: The configured trusted logins include the app bot, its identity lookup temporarily fails, and the bot has posted an unedited `/limitless ...` comment without the marker substring; the poll creates a run from it.

output.summary: Reviewed the queue, webhook, and transaction paths. Two boundary cases can miss or wrongly start commands. The targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`.

findings.title: Initialize the boundary when the first successful poll has no open issues
findings.detail: An empty response leaves the repository uninitialized. The next poll that sees an issue establishes the boundary from that issue and skips all its comments, even when those comments were created after queue enablement. The added test explicitly expects this lost command.
findings.suggestion: Establish a durable GitHub-time boundary on the first successful poll even when there are no open issues, then process later commands against it.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the queue for a repository with no open issues. After its first successful poll, create an issue and post a trusted command before the next poll. That poll uses the command timestamp as the boundary, so the command never starts a run.

findings.title: Do not treat the newest open issue timestamp as the enable time
findings.detail: The newest timestamp in the open-issue response can predate queue enablement by an arbitrary amount. A previously closed issue can contain an old command newer than that timestamp; reopening it after enablement causes the old command to pass the boundary check and start a run.
findings.suggestion: Obtain and persist a GitHub-side timestamp representing the enable poll rather than using the last activity among currently open issues.
findings.failure_scenario: The newest open issue was updated on Monday. A trusted user posted a command on a closed issue on Tuesday, the queue was enabled on Wednesday, and the issue was reopened on Thursday. The Tuesday command is later than the stored Monday boundary and runs despite predating enablement.

findings.title: Do not reject trusted requests merely for containing a marker string
findings.detail: The marker check searches the entire comment body, so an otherwise valid trusted command is silently skipped if its request quotes a Limitless HTML marker. The command definition places no such restriction on request text.
findings.suggestion: Identify factory-authored comments using their author or a validated factory marker in the position used by factory comments, without rejecting arbitrary request text.
findings.failure_scenario: A trusted user posts `/limitless fix parsing of <!-- limitless-lifecycle:... -->`. The queue ignores the command on every poll.

output.summary: Reviewed the evidence checkpoint, finalization, classification, attribution, and replay paths. Targeted tests produced 34 passes, but the pipeline and worker test files could not load because the local entities dependency is missing.

findings.title: A cancellation can leave a newly inserted observation unfinalized
findings.detail: Terminal finalization runs when the run status is updated, but the evidence insert can happen afterward. There is an await between the gate result returning and observe(), so cancellation can mark the run terminal and finalize its existing rows before the returned failure is inserted. The subsequent cancellation check throws, leaving the new row unfinalized with no later terminal update required to repair it.
findings.suggestion: Coordinate evidence insertion with terminal status handling so an observation inserted after terminal transition is finalized as interrupted in the same transaction.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate returns a failure, the run is cancelled while gate:executed is awaited, and the cancellation status update commits before observe() inserts the failure row.

findings.title: Injected load source is bypassed for production in-place executions
findings.detail: For an in-place job, observation reads the load saved by the executor's WorkerStore. The production in-place executor constructs its own WorkerStore with the default hostLoadPerCore source, so EngineDeps.loadSource is never used there. The integration fake sets its WorkerStore source manually and therefore does not exercise this production path.
findings.suggestion: Make the injected source available to the component recording coordinator job completion, or otherwise capture the injected value durably for in-place executions.
findings.failure_scenario: An engine is configured with loadSource returning 3.25 and a failing gates stage runs through the real in-place executor; its observation contains the host's actual load instead of 3.25.

output.summary: Reviewed execution replay, classification, attribution, persistence, and terminal handling. The targeted test run was partly blocked because the checkout lacks the entities package; the classification and observation-store tests passed.

findings.title: A result can be inserted after terminal finalization
findings.detail: The fault hook is awaited after the result returns, and observation insertion happens before the subsequent cancellation check. If cancellation finalizes the run while that await is pending, terminal handling sees no observation; execution then inserts an unfinalized row after the run is already terminal. Nothing subsequently finalizes it.
findings.suggestion: Make evidence insertion and the terminal-state decision atomic, or ensure an observation inserted for an already-terminal run is finalized in the same transaction.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate fails, the run is cancelled while gate:executed is suspended, and terminal handling commits before the hook resumes. The failure row is inserted with null class and history and remains unfinalized.

findings.title: A rejected timeout rerun is recorded as a failed rerun
findings.detail: When a timeout rerun passes but validateRetry rejects its provenance, the comparison has a passing result.retryAttempt and a failing firstAttempt, but no retryOriginal. This branch records rerun_failed instead of the required retry_rejected history. A targeted probe of observationHistory with that result returned rerun_failed.
findings.suggestion: Detect a rejected passing retryAttempt independently of retryOriginal, before deriving timeout-rerun history.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial gate times out, then the timeout rerun passes after modifying tracked files. The durable observation reports rerun_failed even though the passing rerun was rejected for provenance.

output.summary: Reviewed executor installation, deploy rollback, recovery, and release following. The targeted test command could not start because the installed dependencies lack Zod's prefault method and the entities package.

findings.title: Restore the executor when inspection fails during replacement
findings.detail: The replacement catch immediately rethrows ServiceInspectionError, bypassing the journal's restore path. By this point the old plist has been removed, the new plist written, and the new label enabled. If launchctl print then times out or returns an unrecognized error, installation fails while the replacement remains enabled and potentially loaded, and the old plist is not restored. This violates the requirement that a failed executor replacement restore the old plist and leave the executor unloaded and disabled.
findings.suggestion: Attempt the executor journal's fail-closed restoration on inspection errors as well; if shutdown cannot be confirmed, preserve the journal and report recovery instructions without claiming restoration succeeded.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing executor is replaced during service install; enable succeeds, but launchctl print of the replacement times out. The command exits with an error while the replacement plist and enabled label remain in place.

The queue test could not start because the checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. Review found a repository-resolution regression caused by lowercasing the configured slug before run creation.

findings.title: Preserve the registered repository identity when creating runs
findings.detail: The lowercased repository value is passed into issue and comment run requests. Repository resolution uses case-sensitive getRepoBySlug lookups, so an existing registration such as Owner/Repo is not found when the queue requests owner/repo. The resolver instead queries GitHub and creates a second registration with default settings, losing the existing repository's settings and identity for the queued run.
findings.suggestion: Use a canonical key for queue maps, comparisons, and deduplication while preserving or resolving the registered repository slug for run creation.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue configured for Owner/Repo has an existing Owner/Repo registration with a non-default merge policy. An approved issue is admitted with repo owner/repo, causing a separate repository registration and a run using the default merge policy.

output.summary: Reviewed the queue, configuration, and store changes. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js. The change also alters repository resolution for existing mixed-case configurations.

findings.title: Preserve the registered repository spelling when creating runs
findings.detail: The queue now lowercases the repository passed into run requests, but resolveRepo and getRepoBySlug match registered slugs case-sensitively. An existing repository registered as Owner/Repo is therefore not found when the queue requests owner/repo. Resolution instead calls GitHub and registers a second repository, losing the existing repository's settings and potentially failing admission if GitHub resolution is unavailable.
findings.suggestion: Use canonical lowercase keys for queue comparisons while preserving or resolving the configured repository spelling for run creation and other operations that require the registered slug.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue configured for Owner/Repo has an existing Owner/Repo registration. An eligible issue causes createRun to resolve owner/repo, which misses that registration and creates a separate repository record or fails during the GitHub lookup.

output.summary: Reviewed lease persistence and recovery against the requested invariants. The focused test command could not run: the available Zod installation lacks `prefault`, so both test files failed during import before any tests executed.

findings.title: Classify the moved tip before discarding a release intent
findings.detail: Every `moved` result from a replay is treated as superseded, but `ClaimClient.write` also returns `moved` when the new tip is malformed or contains a different record from the same holder and generation. Neither establishes that ownership was superseded. This path clears the pending release and changes confirmed ownership to `lost`, even though recovery must retain the intent for a malformed or otherwise unclassifiable tip.
findings.suggestion: Classify `result.tip` using the same rules as the initial recovery read. Mark the lease lost only when the tip proves supersession; otherwise retain the intent and return `pending`.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed tip and starts replaying a release. Before the compare-and-swap, another writer moves the ref to a malformed commit. The write returns `moved`; recovery clears the final-status intent and marks the confirmed lease lost instead of preserving it for a later retry.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease storage and recovery paths. Targeted tests could not run because the installed Zod lacks prefault and both test files failed during module loading.

findings.title: Classify the new tip before declaring a replay superseded
findings.detail: A moved result is always treated as superseded, even when its tip is malformed or does not establish that a successor took ownership. This clears the pending release and marks confirmed ownership lost, contrary to the recovery rules that preserve the intent when the tip is malformed or otherwise unclassifiable.
findings.suggestion: Classify the returned tip using the same rules as the initial read; retain the intent for malformed or unclassifiable records and mark it lost only when the record establishes supersession.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed tip and starts replaying a release. Before the compare-and-swap arrives, another writer moves the ref to a malformed record. The write returns moved, and recovery clears the release intent instead of retaining it for later inspection and retry.

output.summary: Reviewed the land and post-merge observation paths. The targeted test command could not load because the checkout is missing the `entities` package; no tests ran.

findings.title: Preserve slow-regression evidence when resuming an observed execution
findings.detail: The lookup restricts observations to the current stage ID, but a resumed gates stage receives a new stage ID. If the primary execution was observed before interruption, resuming its durable handle encounters the existing observation through the insert's conflict handling, leaving it associated with the old stage. The selector then cannot find that row to set `slow_regression`, so a passing slow re-check is finalized as `flaky` instead of `load`.
findings.suggestion: Find the observation by the durable execution identity rather than requiring the newly created stage ID, and add a restart test that interrupts after observation but before the slow-regression selector runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A post-merge primary gate fails slowly, its observation is inserted, and the process stops before the re-check. On resume, the same execution is attached under a new gates stage; the re-check passes, but the observation retains `slow_regression=0` and is classified as `flaky`.

output.summary: Reviewed the observation, classification, land-check and post-merge paths. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities dependency.

findings.title: Preserve the slow-regression flag across a stage restart
findings.detail: The observation lookup only selects rows created by the current stage ID. A resumed gates stage receives a new stage ID, while an already-recorded primary execution retains its original ID. If the primary result is replayed after a restart before the selector runs, its observation is excluded, so the selector cannot set slow_regression. A passing re-check is then classified as flaky instead of load.
findings.suggestion: Find the observation by the durable execution identity rather than the current stage ID, and add a restart test between primary observation and the slow-regression selector.
findings.failure_scenario: A post-merge primary check fails slowly, the process restarts after its observation is stored but before retryRegressions selects it, and the resumed re-check passes. The finalized observation has slow_regression=0 and class=flaky instead of load.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease manager against the requested invariants and surrounding persistence and time APIs. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not load the tests: the installed Zod dependency reports `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` in `src/evals/settings.ts:14`.

findings.title: Recovered held leases are absent from the renewal loop
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated after a write returns `applied` in this manager instance. Recovery can confirm an acquisition that was previously unconfirmed, and existing confirmed held rows also survive a restart, but neither path populates that map. Those leases receive no periodic renewal even when `active` would return true.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate confirmed held rows for renewal, or restore their handles when constructing the manager and when reconciliation confirms an acquisition.
findings.failure_scenario: An acquisition reaches GitHub but returns `unconfirmed`; recovery confirms it after a restart. `start()` runs, but no handle is in `handles`, so the lease expires without a renewal.

findings.title: Replayed release bypasses send-time lease validation
findings.detail: The manager delegates pending intent reconciliation to `reconcileLeaseIntent`, whose release replay calls `client.write` without a `beforeSend` hook or a fresh GitHub-time decision. Consequently a release interrupted before sending can be replayed after the generation's renewable window has closed, violating the requirement that every same-generation write revalidate immediately before `updateRefs`.
findings.suggestion: Ensure release replay uses the manager's fresh time decision and send-time predicate, and leaves the intent unresolved when the write is no longer safe.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is persisted before its ref update, the process stops, and recovery runs after the lease has expired but before another holder takes over. Recovery sends the old generation's release without checking whether it is still renewable.

findings.title: Different-run requests skip pending-intent reconciliation
findings.detail: The early different-run check returns `refused` when a row has an intent, before calling `reconcile`. The requested contract requires pending intents to be reconciled before every operation and unresolved intents to return `wait`. This also prevents a new run from clearing a dropped first-acquisition intent through its own acquire call.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the row first under the mutex, return `wait` if it remains pending, then evaluate whether the resulting confirmed row permits the new run.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A leaves an unconfirmed first acquisition with no confirmed ownership. Run B calls `acquire` after the ref is readable and the intent could be dropped; it receives `refused: live` without attempting reconciliation.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease manager and its recovery, timing, and renewal paths. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not load the tests because the installed Zod API lacks `prefault` (`TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` in `src/evals/settings.ts:14`).

findings.title: Replayed releases bypass send-time lease validation
findings.detail: Reconciliation can replay a pending release through `reconcileLeaseIntent`, whose `client.write` call has no `beforeSend` hook or time check. The manager can therefore write the old generation after its lease window has expired, contrary to the required validation for every same-generation write.
findings.suggestion: Make release replay use a fresh time decision and the same send-time validation as other same-generation writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A release is interrupted before its ref update; the manager restarts after the lease expires while the ref still points to the old held tip. Reconciliation sends the release without checking whether that generation is renewable.

findings.title: Reconcile another run's pending intent before refusing it
findings.detail: The different-run check returns before reconciliation whenever an intent exists. An unresolved acquisition must return `wait` and be reconciled first; once dropped, its unconfirmed row must be forgotten so another run can acquire. This early return can leave the next run refused until the separate renewal loop happens to reconcile the intent.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the pending intent before evaluating whether the confirmed row blocks the requested run.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition is unconfirmed and leaves a pending intent. Run B calls acquire before the loop ticks, after the remote ref becomes readable and shows A's write did not happen. B gets `refused: live` instead of reconciling the dropped intent and acquiring.

findings.title: Forget unconfirmed rows dropped during startup recovery
findings.detail: Startup calls `recoverLeases` directly, but only handles its superseded results. If recovery drops a never-confirmed acquisition intent, the empty row remains. A later different-run acquisition reaches `forgetLease` only after reading the ref, but the retained row can also interfere with the specified recovery lifecycle and remains indefinitely if no acquisition follows.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same cleanup used by the manager's `reconcile` helper to dropped startup recovery results.
findings.failure_scenario: The process restarts with run A's first acquisition intent pending and the remote ref unchanged. Startup drops the intent but leaves A's unconfirmed row in SQLite rather than forgetting it.

findings.title: Renew recovered confirmed leases
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which starts empty and is populated only by writes made through this manager instance. Confirmed held rows restored from SQLite, including acquisitions confirmed by startup or tick reconciliation, are never considered for renewal unless another operation first successfully writes them.
findings.suggestion: Restore or derive handles for confirmed held rows and include them in the renewal loop, while retaining the active-hook and ownership checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager restarts with a confirmed held lease, starts with an active hook returning true, and receives renewal ticks. No update is sent, so the lease expires despite the run being active.

output.summary: Reviewed the verification, preview and resume changes. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout’s available dependencies are incomplete or incompatible: Bun reported a missing `entities` package and a Zod version without `number().overwrite()`.

findings.title: Require positive browser setup evidence before converting blocks
findings.detail: The engine treats a ready preview and the absence of a `browser_unavailable` event as proof that browser setup succeeded. That warning is emitted when constructing the MCP configuration fails; it does not establish that the MCP server or Chromium subsequently started successfully. A launch failure can therefore leave no warning while the verifier correctly reports that browser tools are unavailable. The engine then converts the environment block to `unclear`, sends the run into the implementation feedback path, and falsely claims the browser was available.
findings.suggestion: Record an engine-owned positive browser setup outcome for the same invocation and convert blocked rows only when that outcome is confirmed. Preserve environment-block handling when setup is unavailable or unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview is ready and browser MCP configuration is constructed, but the MCP server or Chromium fails to launch. The verifier reports the marked check blocked because the browser tool is unavailable; no `browser_unavailable` configuration warning was recorded, so the row becomes `unclear` and triggers implementation feedback.

output.summary: Reviewed the verification flow and browser setup handling. The focused tests could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package.

findings.title: Do not infer successful browser setup from the absence of a warning
findings.detail: The code marks the browser available whenever the preview is ready and no browser_unavailable event was recorded. That warning only covers failures while constructing the MCP configuration; it does not establish that the MCP server or Chromium actually started. A later MCP startup or launch failure can therefore turn a legitimate infrastructure block into unclear, causing implementation feedback instead of the bounded environment-block path.
findings.suggestion: Record an engine-owned positive browser setup outcome for the invocation and convert blocked rows only when that outcome confirms availability. Preserve unavailable or unknown handling when startup cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: The preview starts and browserMcp returns a configuration, but the MCP server fails to launch or Chromium cannot start. The verifier reports a marked browser check blocked; no browser_unavailable event exists, so the engine incorrectly converts it to unclear.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle publication, recovery, privacy checks, and answer-command dispatch. The targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts` could not start because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`; no test assertions ran.

findings.title: Publication failures log exception output instead of fixed codes
findings.detail: The delivery and recovery catch passes the exception to logFailure, which writes its string representation after credential redaction. GitHub command errors can contain stderr or stdout, and parsing errors can contain response fragments. Configured private strings are not removed by credential redaction, so a failure can put private content from a GitHub response into diagnostics. This also violates the requirement that publication diagnostics use fixed codes and never exception output.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed publication or recovery failure code without including the exception text, and cover a fake gh failure containing a configured private string.
findings.failure_scenario: A question POST or recovery request fails and gh returns an error containing a configured private string; the lifecycle log records that string.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle publication, recovery, privacy checks, and answer-command dispatch. The targeted issue-queue test could not run because the checkout is missing the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency.

findings.title: Lifecycle delivery failures log exception output
findings.detail: The delivery catch passes the exception to logFailure, which only redacts registered credentials. A GitHub response or subprocess error can contain configured private strings or other withheld content. This also violates the requirement that publication diagnostics use fixed codes rather than exception output.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed delivery or recovery failure code without including the exception text.
findings.failure_scenario: A comment recovery request fails with a GitHub error containing a configured private string in its response; the error is written to lifecycle diagnostics because that string is not necessarily a registered credential.

findings.title: Recover uncertain posts before closing their checkpoints
findings.detail: The saved body is reinspected before marker recovery, and an inspection failure immediately marks the effect done even when page indicates that a POST may already have been issued. This closes an uncertain checkpoint without checking GitHub, contrary to the required recovery behavior; if the POST failed before acceptance, the question set is permanently suppressed even after the transient inspection problem clears.
findings.suggestion: Recover an uncertain POST using the independently generated marker and checkpointed author before closing its checkpoint; apply current publication checks before any subsequent POST.
findings.failure_scenario: A question POST fails before acceptance after page 1 is checkpointed. Before the next poll, private-string inspection temporarily fails. The effect is marked done without recovery, and reopening or later successful inspection never publishes the still-open question set.

output.summary: Reviewed trigger persistence, eligibility, delivery, restart, and rollback paths. The targeted command `bun test test/conflict-rounds.test.ts` could not run because the installed Zod lacks `number().overwrite`; it failed during test loading before any tests executed.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict
findings.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the land trigger is evaluated against it without refreshing the PR. If that snapshot predates the approved head, `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped as `PR head moved`. The trigger is no longer pending when the poller later observes the actual head, and the blocked land entry does not generate another trigger.
findings.suggestion: Refresh or defer evaluation when the saved snapshot does not match the land trigger’s approved SHA; preserve the trigger until a current observation can decide it.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B, and B is approved and blocked by a base conflict before the next poll. The trigger for B is permanently skipped against snapshot A.

findings.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the PR and round
findings.detail: The conflict delivery path disables GitHub auto-merge before `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush` verify the current grant, PR identity, state, and head. A stale or invalid round can therefore change PR settings even though its push is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the stored grant and the current PR identity and head before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the awaited mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: While a conflict round runs, the PR head branch changes or the round grant becomes invalid. Delivery disables auto-merge, then the existing authorization check rejects the push.

findings.title: Rollback lets the previous release treat conflict rounds as ordinary review rounds
findings.detail: The migration stores conflict rounds in the existing `review_rounds` table, but the previous release ignores the new `kind` column. After rollback, an unfinished conflict run is resumed by the old review-round machinery, which has no conflict-round preparation or resolution semantics. This violates the required compatibility for runs interrupted by deployment or rollback.
findings.suggestion: Keep conflict-round records and execution distinguishable to the previous release, or provide a rollback-safe mechanism that prevents the old engine from resuming them as review rounds.
findings.failure_scenario: A conflict round is queued or interrupted during preparation, then deployment rolls back. The previous daemon loads its row as a normal review round and follows the old review preparation and delivery path.

output.summary: Reviewed trigger persistence, eligibility, delivery, and restart handling. `bun test test/conflict-rounds.test.ts` could not reach assertions: the installed Zod reports `TypeError: z.number().overwrite is not a function` in existing `src/pipeline/schemas.ts:113`.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict trigger
findings.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the consumer uses it instead of fetching the current PR. `startConflictTrigger` then marks the trigger skipped if that snapshot's head differs from the approved head. A subsequent poll does not necessarily emit another `pr.conflicting` transition, so the blocked entry can remain without a conflict round. The same stale snapshot is consumed on startup before a fresh poll.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation before deciding a land trigger, and retain the trigger until a current observation can be checked.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last saved head A; the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll. The land queue finds a conflict at B, but the consumer compares the trigger with saved head A and permanently skips it as `PR head moved`.

findings.title: A comment failure leaves a delivered resolution without its required comment
findings.detail: The round is marked delivered immediately after the push, before fetching or posting the PR comment. If either GitHub call fails, the run exits through the normal failure path after the commit and approval invalidation have already been recorded. A failed run is terminal, so there is no durable pending comment operation to resume, and the PR may never receive the required resolution summary.
findings.suggestion: Persist and resume the comment publication separately from the push, including recovery after an uncertain comment outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: The push succeeds, then `gh pr view --json comments` or `gh pr comment` fails transiently. The new head is delivered and the round fails without a comment; restarting the daemon does not resume that terminal run.

output.summary: Reviewed the executor lifecycle, restart paths, retries, and landing checks. The focused command `bun test test/gate-executor.test.ts test/config-routing.test.ts` could not start: the installed Zod dependency lacks `z.number().overwrite`, so neither test file ran.

findings.title: Restarting a regression retry removes its required build output
findings.detail: On resume, the stage cleans the checkout before `runGateExecution` returns the persisted initial result. It then attaches to the regression retry without rerunning setup or the initial checks. The retry is deliberately configured with no setup, so files produced by the first attempt are gone. Previously the resumed stage reran the initial gates and recreated those files before retrying.
findings.suggestion: Preserve or reconstruct the required checkout state before resuming a local retry, and test a restart during a retry whose check depends on generated build output.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates an ignored build artifact, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its regression retry. `checkoutCommitted` removes the artifact; the resumed retry fails because setup is not rerun.

findings.title: Landing checks do not persist their execution handle
findings.detail: The landing queue calls `executeGate` without a persistence callback or stored handle. Its handle is discarded, so after a daemon restart the queue starts a new execution instead of attaching to the existing one. This breaks the requested durable executor lifecycle for landing checks and would duplicate work for an executor whose work survives the daemon.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle with the queue state before awaiting its result, and attach to it when the queue resumes.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-local executor starts landing checks and the daemon restarts before the result arrives. The resumed queue starts a second execution while the first continues.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: `executeGate` awaits only `execution.result` and never reads `execution.events`. Local executions happen to call the supplied hooks directly, but an injected executor can only report progress through its event stream. Its check events therefore never reach pipeline gate events or the landing log.
findings.suggestion: Consume the execution event stream and route its events to the appropriate hooks, while avoiding duplicate local events.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor emits check events while its result is pending. The pipeline records no per-check progress and the landing log contains no check output.

output.summary: Reviewed executor lifecycle, restart handling, retries, and event reporting. Targeted tests could not run: both `bun test test/gate-executor.test.ts` and `bun test test/gates.test.ts` failed during module loading because the installed Zod lacks `z.number().overwrite`; this appears to be an environment dependency issue.

findings.title: Cached attempts lose their checkout state across a restart
findings.detail: A completed initial attempt is returned from persisted results after restart, but the gates stage first runs `checkoutCommitted`, which removes generated and ignored files. A pending local regression retry is then replayed without setup or the build output produced by the initial attempt. Prepare similarly discards changes before resuming a baseline retry. This changes retry results and can incorrectly classify a regression or baseline failure.
findings.suggestion: Preserve or reconstruct the filesystem state required by a local retry before replaying it, while retaining the original result for comparison.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup command builds an ignored artifact and a check fails transiently. The daemon restarts after the initial result is saved or during its retry. On resume, cleanup deletes the artifact, the initial result is reused, and the retry runs without setup and fails because the artifact is missing.

findings.title: Redacting the local handle changes the request replayed after restart
findings.detail: The local handle contains the full gate request, and it is redacted before persistence. Local attachment executes that stored request verbatim. If a gate command contains a registered credential or terminal control sequence, the stored command differs from the command read from the base commit, so a restart executes a different check. Redaction of persisted data must remain, but the redacted request cannot be used as executable input.
findings.suggestion: Reconstruct local replay requests from trusted current run state and the base gate configuration instead of executing a redacted persisted request.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured gate command contains a registered credential literal. The daemon restarts after saving its local handle; attachment runs the command with the credential replaced by the redaction marker, causing a failure or checking the wrong target.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed by the daemon
findings.detail: `executeGate` only awaits `execution.result` and never iterates `execution.events`. Local reporting happens through private hooks, but an executor implementing the advertised interface has no access to those hooks. Its check and status events therefore never reach pipeline gate events or landing logs, and a producer that requires events to be drained can stall.
findings.suggestion: Consume executor events in the shared execution path and translate them into the existing pipeline and landing reporting hooks, avoiding duplicate local events.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits a failing check event and returns a GateRun. The stage verdict changes, but no corresponding gate event or landing check output is recorded.

output.summary: Reviewed the read policy, profile generation, and gate and editor call sites. Targeted tests could not fully run in this sandbox: access to the real ~/.ssh path was denied, real Seatbelt probes were skipped, and test/scratch.test.ts failed to load because the installed Zod lacks prefault.

findings.title: Gate allowlist exposes Cargo registry credentials
findings.detail: The gate profile grants reads to the entire Cargo home, but the credential deny list does not include Cargo's standard credentials files. Consequently, the later allow rule makes ~/.cargo/credentials and ~/.cargo/credentials.toml readable by untrusted gate code. Setting CARGO_HOME to scratch for the subprocess does not prevent reads by absolute path. Adding either file to sandbox.deny_read also makes every gate fail the overlap check instead of protecting it while retaining the toolchain allowance.
findings.suggestion: Permit only the Cargo toolchain paths gates actually need, or apply narrowly scoped credential denies after the Cargo home allowance while retaining a precise overlap check for unsafe allowances.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner has a registry token in ~/.cargo/credentials.toml and a candidate test reads that file by absolute path during a gate; the profile permits the read and the test can transmit the token over HTTPS.

output.summary: Reviewed the read-policy construction, sandbox profiles, and launch paths. Targeted sandbox and scratch tests could not complete reliably: this review environment denies access to the real credential paths, its Seatbelt is nested, and the installed Zod lacks prefault.

findings.title: Gate toolchain allowance exposes Cargo registry credentials
findings.detail: The gate profile allows reads throughout the owner's Cargo home, but the credential deny list does not include Cargo's credential files. The later allow rule therefore overrides the home-wide deny for these files. Setting CARGO_HOME to scratch for the command does not prevent a candidate from reading the original path directly.
findings.suggestion: Deny Cargo credential files explicitly while preserving the toolchain files gates need, and add a real Seatbelt probe for a stand-in credential file under the allowed Cargo home.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate runs untrusted code on a machine with a registry token in ~/.cargo/credentials.toml; the code reads that file by absolute path and can send the token over the network.

output.summary: Reviewed executor lifecycle, retry and landing paths. The targeted gate tests could not run: the installed Zod lacks z.number().overwrite, so both files failed during import before any tests ran.

findings.title: Restart discards handles for retry executions
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial and rebase handles are eligible for attachment. On restart during a timeout, baseline or regression retry, the saved handle is discarded and the stage starts work again. The new test explicitly expects this behavior, but it violates the requested guarantee that a restart between start and result attaches without starting again.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough preceding attempt state to resume each retry and attach its saved handle.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a regression retry is running on an executor whose work survives restarts; resume starts another execution instead of attaching to the existing one.

findings.title: Clear the handle only when the result is durably checkpointed
findings.detail: The handle is removed and saved before the caller records or acts on the returned GateRun. A crash after this save but before the stage checkpoint leaves neither the execution handle nor its result in durable state, so resume starts the same work again.
findings.suggestion: Keep the handle until the result and the stage's next durable state are saved together, or persist the result alongside the handle before clearing it.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops immediately after the gate-result save and before the gates stage saves its comparison; restarting launches a new execution even though the prior execution completed.

findings.title: Persist landing-check handles for restart
findings.detail: Landing checks call executeGate without a persistence callback or a stored handle. Consequently, their execution identity is lost on daemon restart and the queue cannot attach to surviving work.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle in durable queue state and use it when resuming checks.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a landing check is running on a durable executor; the resumed queue starts another check instead of attaching to the existing execution.

output.summary: Reviewed executor routing, persistence, cancellation and restart behavior. The targeted command `bun test test/gate-executor.test.ts` could not run: the installed Zod dependency lacks `z.number().overwrite`, causing an import-time TypeError in src/pipeline/schemas.ts before any tests executed.

findings.title: Retry executions are discarded instead of reattached after restart
findings.detail: The resume condition excludes timeout, baseline-retry and regression-retry handles. On restart the stage begins again with its initial execution, clears the persisted retry handle and starts new work. A restarted process cannot cancel the old execution through the process-local live map. This violates the executor's durable attach contract and can leave remote work running while duplicating checks. The new test explicitly expects this behavior for retry purposes.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough intermediate stage state to resume each retry at its execution point, and attach to its stored handle after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after persisting a regression-retry handle but before its result arrives. On restart it starts a new initial gate execution instead of attaching to the retry; an executor whose work survives the daemon continues the original retry too.

findings.title: Landing checks start without persisting their execution handle
findings.detail: The landing queue calls executeGate without a persistence callback or stored handle. Its handle is discarded, so a daemon restart during landing checks always starts another execution and cannot reattach to or cancel work that survived the restart. This leaves the shared executor interface incomplete for one of the required daemon gate paths.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing execution handle in durable queue state before attaching, and restore it when the checking entry resumes.
findings.failure_scenario: A landing check is running on an executor that survives daemon restarts when the daemon stops. The resumed checking entry starts a second execution while the first remains untracked.

output.summary: The targeted sandbox tests passed where runnable; real Seatbelt probes skipped because nested Seatbelt is unavailable. The scratch tests could not load because the installed Zod lacks prefault. A policy check confirmed that gate profiles grant reads to files directly under home.

findings.title: Ancestor manifest exceptions expose files under the denied home
findings.detail: The ancestor exceptions grant file-read access to package.json, bunfig.toml, tsconfig.json and jsconfig.json at every ancestor of an allowed checkout or toolchain, including the home directory and intermediate factory directories. These grants follow the home deny in the Seatbelt profile, so candidate gate code can read those files by absolute path. This violates the requested home-wide boundary and can expose private configuration or tokens stored in those files. The targeted check `bun -e 'import { ancestorReadPolicy } from "./src/harness/read-policy.ts"; console.log(ancestorReadPolicy(["/Users/example/.limitless/runs/current/worktree"], ["/Users/example"]).literals.filter(p => p === "/Users/example/package.json"))'` produced `[ "/Users/example/package.json" ]`.
findings.suggestion: Restrict discovery exceptions so they do not grant reads to files under denied home ancestors, and add a real Seatbelt probe for an ancestor manifest.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate runs in a checkout under the owner's home and reads a private `~/package.json` or an ancestor `bunfig.toml` by absolute path.

output.summary: Reviewed the gate and editor read-policy paths and ran focused sandbox tests. The gate profile exposes files directly under home through ancestor exceptions. Real Seatbelt probes were skipped because nested Seatbelt is unavailable in this sandbox. The combined test command also could not load scratch.test.ts because the installed Zod lacks floors.prefault; that dependency error is not treated as a finding.

findings.title: Ancestor exceptions expose files directly under the home directory
findings.detail: The gate profile grants file-read access to package.json, bunfig.toml, tsconfig.json and jsconfig.json in every ancestor of an allowed path. Because the home directory is normally an ancestor of the checkout or toolchain, these literal grants override the home-wide deny for those files. They can contain private configuration or credentials, and the request explicitly requires files directly under home to remain unreadable.
findings.suggestion: Avoid granting content reads to these filenames outside the allowed roots, or otherwise ensure home-level files remain denied while preserving toolchain discovery.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner has a ~/bunfig.toml containing a private registry token. A gate command reads that file by absolute path because the generated profile explicitly allows it.

output.summary: Reviewed the preview confinement and process lifecycle. The targeted command `bun test test/preview.test.ts` could not exercise server-dependent behavior because this sandbox denied loopback binding with `EPERM`; the real Seatbelt test was also skipped in the nested sandbox.

findings.title: Readiness deadline includes confinement verification
findings.detail: The readiness clock starts while the serve command is still undergoing confinement verification. The Seatbelt preflight has its own subprocess timeouts of up to 30 seconds, so a slow but successful verification can consume the entire 20-second readiness budget before the server starts. The preview then reports a readiness timeout and aborts a valid launch.
findings.suggestion: Start the readiness deadline when the confined payload starts, while separately bounding and reporting confinement verification failures.
findings.failure_scenario: On a loaded machine, serve confinement verification takes 21 seconds and then succeeds; startPreview times out after 20 seconds even though the server has not yet had an opportunity to bind its port.

output.summary: Reviewed preview confinement, process cleanup, and the added tests. The targeted preview suite could not exercise startup because this sandbox denied loopback binding with EPERM; the real Seatbelt test also skipped under nested confinement.

findings.title: Handle rejection from abort-triggered cleanup
findings.detail: The abort listener discards the promise returned by stop(), but stop() now rejects when process termination cannot be confirmed. That rejection can be reported as unhandled before the pipeline reaches its own cleanup, potentially terminating the daemon instead of propagating the confinement failure through the run.
findings.suggestion: Attach a rejection handler to the abort-triggered cleanup while retaining the same promise for callers to await and observe the termination error.
findings.failure_scenario: A running preview is cancelled and runProcess fails to confirm that its serve process tree stopped, causing serving to reject with ProcessTerminationError. The abort listener calls void stop(), leaving its rejection unhandled.

output.summary: Reviewed the change-view redaction paths and found a holdout disclosure gap. Targeted MCP tests could not run because the checkout lacks the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency.

findings.title: Partial quotations of holdout prose can remain visible in reports
findings.detail: Report redaction matches complete holdout phrases and selected syntax-shaped literals. A report line that quotes only part of ordinary holdout prose can therefore pass through unchanged. This also affects clipped verifier evidence in a public acceptance-criterion row: the report renderer truncates evidence to 300 characters, while the catalogue may contain only the longer complete phrase. The change’s section removal protects the holdout table but does not protect quotations elsewhere in the report.
findings.suggestion: Make report filtering account for partial and clipped holdout quotations, including verifier evidence rendered outside the holdout section, and add a regression test using ordinary prose without distinctive literals.
findings.failure_scenario: A holdout description is “Use the red umbrella to trigger the silent fallback.” A public report line says “The verifier checked the red umbrella.” Neither the complete description nor a harvested syntax-shaped literal appears in that line, so the quotation is returned to the reviewer.

output.summary: Reviewed the change-view redaction paths and tests. Targeted MCP tests could not run because the checkout lacks the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency; this environment error is not a finding.

findings.title: A file present in the head can expose holdout-only base content
findings.detail: The presence check exempts the entire patch from holdout filtering whenever the path exists in the delivered head. A patch also contains removed lines, context lines, and hunk annotations from the base version, so those bytes need not be present in the PR tree or known to the implementer. This can disclose hidden test text through the change view.
findings.suggestion: Limit the exemption to content established to be in the delivered head, and continue holdout filtering for base-only patch content and annotations.
findings.failure_scenario: The base commit contains a hidden test file with a private sentinel. The delivered head replaces that file's contents with a harmless line but leaves the path present. The returned diff includes the removed hidden test and its sentinel without holdout redaction.

output.summary: Reviewed the four requested behaviors and their persistence paths. GitHub notifier tests passed, but the land queue, MCP proxy, and CLI HTTP tests could not load because the MCP SDK is missing from the environment.

findings.title: A failed post-merge lookup permanently publishes null merge fields
findings.detail: If the lookup after a successful merge fails or returns a stale OPEN observation, landed() immediately sets merged with null metadata. The run.merged feed trigger captures those null values at that moment. Later reconciliation can update the run from a saved snapshot, but it neither corrects the existing feed item nor fetches missing metadata for already-merged runs. With polling disabled, the metadata can remain missing from the run as well.
findings.suggestion: Keep the successful merge checkpoint retryable until authoritative merge metadata is available, and ensure the resulting feed item contains that metadata without repeating the merge.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts the merge, but the subsequent PR lookup times out. The parent run emits run.merged with null mergedBy and mergedAt; a later successful observation does not repair that feed item.

findings.title: MCP approvals still default to reviewer human
findings.detail: The consumer field is optional, and submitReview retains the human fallback when it is omitted. Existing MCP clients, including clients following the tool's documented required arguments, therefore continue to create review.approved items attributed to human. The new test explicitly accepts this behavior, leaving the requested provenance fix incomplete.
findings.suggestion: Require an MCP consumer for approvals or obtain a reliable consumer identity from the MCP session, and record it with the mcp: prefix.
findings.failure_scenario: A client calls limitless_review with run, verdict approve, and reviewedSha but no consumer; the approval and feed still show reviewer human.

output.summary: Reviewed the merge, MCP approval, change-view and CLI authentication paths. The notifier tests passed, but the land queue, MCP proxy and API-token test files could not run because the MCP SDK dependency was unavailable.

findings.title: A cancellation during the new metadata lookup is overwritten
findings.detail: The post-merge lookup adds an await after the merge succeeds. If cancellation or shutdown aborts that lookup, its rejection is converted to null and landed() still runs. Cancellation can therefore be overwritten with landed, and shutdown can write after its abort. The queue's existing abort handling is bypassed.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, check the abort signal and current entry state before writing; keep confirmed-merge reconciliation separate from overwriting a cancelled entry.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR merge succeeds, the metadata client is still pending, and cancel(id) aborts it and records cancelled. The catch returns null and landed() changes the entry to landed.

findings.title: A failed post-merge lookup can leave merge metadata missing permanently
findings.detail: The queue marks the run merged even when its new metadata request fails or returns a stale OPEN observation. This branch then refuses to fetch metadata for already-merged runs and only consults a saved poller snapshot. With polling disabled or no matching snapshot, a transient failure of that single lookup leaves mergedBy and mergedAt null indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded, retryable reconciliation path for missing merge metadata when no authoritative saved observation exists.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub confirms the merge, the immediately following gh pr view fails transiently, and PR polling is disabled. Later reconciliation passes skip network lookups for the merged run, so its merge fields never fill.

findings.title: Later metadata repairs leave the merge feed event incorrect
findings.detail: When the initial merge observation lacks metadata, landed() emits run.merged with null fields. This repair only updates mergedBy and mergedAt on the run; the feed trigger emits a merge event only on the false-to-true merged transition. Consequently the original event remains null even after the run is repaired, including for already affected runs.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the feed exposes corrected merge metadata when a later authoritative observation fills it, while preserving the intended event semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: The immediate post-merge observation has null metadata, then a later saved MERGED snapshot contains the actor and timestamp. The run fields become populated, but its run.merged feed item continues to report both as null.

output.summary: Reviewed the merge, approval, change-view and CLI error paths. The merge metadata recovery has a restart and transient-failure gap. GitHub notifier tests passed, but the land queue, MCP and CLI tests could not run because the MCP SDK dependency was unavailable.

findings.title: A failed metadata lookup can leave merge fields null permanently
findings.detail: Landing marks both runs merged before the metadata lookup. If that lookup fails, times out, returns incomplete metadata, or is interrupted by a restart, reconciliation only reads an existing saved snapshot and does not fetch one for merged runs. The poller also excludes merged runs from tracking, so an earlier OPEN snapshot will never be refreshed through that path. The parent and round can therefore retain null merge fields indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Make incomplete merge metadata durably retryable after landing and restart, while preserving the recorded merge and avoiding duplicate merge transitions.
findings.failure_scenario: The queue successfully merges a PR while its saved poller snapshot is OPEN; the subsequent GitHub metadata request times out or the daemon restarts before it completes. Both runs are marked merged with null mergedBy and mergedAt, and later reconciliation never obtains the missing values.

output.summary: Reviewed the merge, MCP review, change-view, and CLI token paths. The targeted test command passed 62 tests but could not load four test files because the MCP SDK dependency was unavailable in the checkout.

findings.title: Merged runs cannot recover metadata after the queue's lookup fails
findings.detail: The queue marks both runs merged before its metadata lookup. If that lookup fails, times out, returns incomplete metadata, or the daemon stops before it completes, reconciliation only reads an existing saved snapshot and never fetches another observation. The poller excludes merged runs from tracking, so an earlier OPEN snapshot will remain stale and the merge fields can stay null permanently.
findings.suggestion: Make missing merge metadata durably eligible for a bounded later observation, including after restart, without repeating the merge.
findings.failure_scenario: The merge succeeds, the metadata request fails, and the saved PR snapshot still says OPEN. After restart, neither reconciliation nor polling fetches the merged PR, leaving both runs' mergedBy and mergedAt null.

findings.title: Updating an already delivered feed item loses the metadata for consumers
findings.detail: The initial merge transition publishes a run.merged item with null metadata, then this code edits that item's data in place. Feed consumers advance and acknowledge an ID, so a consumer that reads the event before the metadata request finishes will never receive the corrected fields. The update also does not create a new feed item for long-polling consumers.
findings.suggestion: Publish a subsequent feed item when metadata becomes available, or arrange for the original event to contain the metadata before it becomes visible while retaining durable merge recording.
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer reads and acknowledges run.merged while the post-merge GitHub request is in flight. The request then supplies the actor and timestamp, but the consumer's next feed read starts after the edited event and never sees them.

output.summary: Reviewed patch reconstruction, paging, and other diff-rendering paths. The focused MCP test suite could not start because the checkout lacks the MCP SDK dependency. A dependency-free privacy probe confirmed that a diff embedded in a saved report can still expose both lines of a registered credential.

findings.title: Redact multiline credentials in diffs embedded in reports
findings.detail:
The new patch-line filter is applied only to the `diff` field. Saved reports are passed through `privacy(report)`, which looks for the uninterrupted credential and therefore accepts a Markdown diff containing `+alpha-secret` and `+beta-secret` on separate lines. Such a report can be returned through the same change-view API, despite the request requiring other diff-rendering outputs to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups. The dependency-free check `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR="$TMPDIR" bun -e 'import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {loadOutputPrivacy} from "./src/util/private-output.ts"; registerCredential("TEST", "alpha-secret
beta-secret"); const p=loadOutputPrivacy(); const report="## Diff
```diff
+alpha-secret
+beta-secret
```"; console.log(p ? p(report) : "policy unavailable");'` printed the complete report with both secret lines unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Apply line-prefix-aware credential filtering to diff blocks in reports before paging, or explicitly document this output as a follow-up as requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted report contains a fenced unified diff with two added lines forming a registered multiline credential; `limitless_get_change` returns both lines in its report pages.

output.summary: Reviewed the patch redaction and surrounding output paths. A targeted privacy check confirmed that a diff embedded in a report can still expose a multiline credential. The MCP test file could not run because the checkout lacks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js.

findings.title: Apply line-prefixed credential protection to diff excerpts in reports
findings.detail:
The new reconstruction filter is applied only to the generated patch.
