The same response returns persisted report text through the existing literal privacy check, so a report containing a diff excerpt can still expose both lines of a registered multiline credential. This leaves the request's other diff-rendering outputs unprotected and does not list them as follow-ups. A targeted check, `bun -e 'import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const credential="alpha-secret
beta-secret"; const report="```diff
+alpha-secret
+beta-secret
```"; console.log(JSON.stringify({matches:privateMatches(report,[{value:credential,entry:0}]),report}));'`, returned `{"matches":[],"report":"```diff
+alpha-secret
+beta-secret
```"}`.
findings.suggestion: Apply a shared line-prefixed diff redactor to report excerpts before paging, and cover a persisted report containing a multiline credential in a diff with a regression test.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted report contains a fenced diff with `+alpha-secret` and `+beta-secret` on adjacent lines, while `alpha-secret\nbeta-secret` is registered as a credential. The report privacy check finds no literal match and limitless_get_change returns both lines.

output.summary: Reviewed setup execution, prompt validation, cache identity, and trial timing. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout has an incompatible installed Zod and is missing the MCP SDK client module.

findings.title: Run setup only after checking for a reusable trial
findings.detail: Review setup runs before the cache key is computed and before cached trials or resumed predecessors are checked. Consequently, a previously successful trial cannot be reused if setup now fails, and every cache hit repeats potentially expensive setup commands.
findings.suggestion: Compute the review cache identity and check for reusable results before executing setup; run setup only when a reviewer invocation is needed.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup-enabled trial succeeds and is cached. On a later identical eval, its dependency installation encounters a transient failure: the trial is recorded as a preparation error instead of reusing the successful cached result.

output.summary: Reviewed the setup, prompt, cache and policy paths. Targeted tests could not run: the installed Zod lacks number().overwrite, and the MCP SDK module is missing.

findings.title: Setup variants make policy evidence depend on system order
findings.detail: Allowing setup to distinguish otherwise identical standard systems breaks the policy generator's assumption that at most one production-eligible system exists per target. selectEvidence accepts both systems, but generatePolicy calls summarize(...)[0], so it uses only the first system's results and silently discards the other arm. Reversing the systems can therefore change the generated routing policy.
findings.suggestion: Define which setup variant is eligible for production routing and filter consistently when selecting and summarizing evidence, or otherwise select an explicit arm per target.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains standard single-review systems for the same model and implementer-report setting, one with setup: true and one without. Both pass validation; policy generation uses whichever system appears first, even if their grades differ.

output.summary: The patch withholds entire files instead of preserving public lines, and quoted multiline credentials can still escape through reports. The targeted MCP test could not run because the MCP SDK dependency is missing.

findings.title: Preserve public lines in a file containing a credential
findings.detail: A multiline match replaces the entire patch with a single withholding marker. The request requires mapping matches back to their patch lines and keeping the rest of the file visible. The new test instead asserts that the whole file is withheld.
findings.suggestion: Map matches in the old and new projections back to their contributing patch lines, withhold those lines, and retain the remaining patch before paging.
findings.failure_scenario: An added file contains public lines before and after a two-line registered credential. Neither public line appears in the change view.

findings.title: Redact credentials in line-prefixed report text
findings.detail: The new projection check applies only to the selected Git file. Reports still pass through literal privacy matching, although report generation prefixes every request line with `> `. A multiline credential in that request therefore survives in the returned report. A targeted check with `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR="$TMPDIR" bun -e 'import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {loadOutputPrivacy} from "./src/util/private-output.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_EXAMPLE", "alpha-secret\nbeta-secret"); const text = "> alpha-secret\n> beta-secret"; console.log(loadOutputPrivacy()?.(text));'` printed both `> alpha-secret` and `> beta-secret`.
findings.suggestion: Apply line-prefix-aware credential redaction to quoted report content before paging, and cover it with an end-to-end change-view test.
findings.failure_scenario: A run request contains a registered two-line credential. The persisted report quotes each request line with `> `, and limitless_get_change returns both credential lines in reports.

findings.title: Avoid making small diffs of large files unavailable
findings.detail: When any multiline credential is registered, each selected file is read in full through `sh`, which rejects output over 50,000,000 characters. A small patch to a larger text file therefore returns a Git inspection error even if the patch itself is small and contains no credential.
findings.suggestion: Inspect large blobs with bounded streaming while preserving matching across chunk boundaries.
findings.failure_scenario: A multiline credential is registered and a one-line change is made to a text file larger than the subprocess output limit; the change view returns unavailable.

output.summary: The patch protects the tested credential case by withholding the entire file, but that fails the visibility requirement. Diff-formatted text in reports can also expose the credential. The targeted test could not run because the MCP SDK dependency is missing.

findings.title: Preserve unrelated patch lines when a credential matches
findings.detail: A multiline match replaces the entire patch with a file-level placeholder. The request requires withholding the lines spanned by the match while leaving the rest of the file visible. The new test instead asserts the file-level placeholder, so it does not verify that acceptance criterion.
findings.suggestion: Map matches in each reconstructed file side back to the affected patch lines and withhold those lines before paging, preserving unrelated lines.
findings.failure_scenario: An added file contains `public before`, a two-line registered credential, and `public after`. The response contains only `[withheld: private text; 1 file]`, so neither public line is visible.

findings.title: Protect diff-formatted credentials in returned reports
findings.detail: The new file inspection protects only `diff.text`. Reports are still checked as complete raw text and then returned through the existing report redactor. A report containing a quoted unified diff with `+` or `-` prefixes between credential lines does not contain the registered literal, so both lines can be returned. The request also covers other outputs that render diffs.
findings.suggestion: Apply line-prefix-aware credential protection to diff-formatted report text before paging, and test a report containing a multiline registered credential as patch lines.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted report contains consecutive lines `+alpha-secret` and `+beta-secret`, and `alpha-secret\nbeta-secret` is registered. Neither the raw report nor either individual line contains the complete literal, so the report page exposes both halves.

findings.title: Avoid making small diffs unavailable for large files
findings.detail: When any multiline credential is registered, every selected text file is read in full through `git show`. The subprocess wrapper rejects output over 50,000,000 characters, and the enclosing catch makes the entire change view unavailable. Previously a small diff of such a file could be returned without reading its full contents.
findings.suggestion: Inspect file content with a bounded streaming approach that can detect matches without the subprocess output limit, while failing closed if inspection cannot complete.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository has a text file over 50 million characters with a one-line change, and the daemon has any multiline credential registered. Selecting that file returns `Local comparison commits or Git inspection unavailable` instead of the small patch.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry, JUnit parsing, configuration, and execution paths. The focused JUnit and retry-file tests passed. Two broader targeted test files could not load because the installed dependencies are incomplete or incompatible: `bun test test/gate-retry-files.test.ts test/gate-executor.test.ts test/gate-feedback.test.ts` reported `z.number().overwrite is not a function` and a missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js` module.

findings.title: A security check can become non-blocking after a retry
findings.detail: The retry classification treats every check alike: if the full retry passes, it sets the verdict to `flaky` and clears `blocking`. There is no security-check classification or guard preventing that transition, despite the request requiring a security check's failure never to become a pass.
findings.suggestion: Carry a trusted security-check classification into retry handling and preserve a blocking failure for those checks, including when a retry passes.
findings.failure_scenario: A security check passes on the baseline, fails after the change, and passes on its full retry. The comparison becomes `flaky` and non-blocking.

findings.title: Changed-file failures never receive the requested targeted retry
findings.detail: The existing `pointsAt` exclusion is retained before selecting targeted retries. Consequently, a failure whose output identifies a changed file is not retried even when JUnit supplies its failing file. This excludes a common regression case from the new behavior and from its confirmation path.
findings.suggestion: Apply the changed-file exclusion only where still intended for the old full-retry behavior, and allow known failing files to receive the requested targeted confirmation.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed test file fails with output containing `example.test.ts:12`, and the JUnit report names that file. `retryRegressions` returns the original comparison without invoking the targeted retry.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry flow, JUnit parsing, configuration boundary, and focused tests. The retry-file tests passed. The executor and feedback tests could not load because installed dependencies were incomplete or incompatible.

findings.title: A passing retry clears a failed security check
findings.detail: The retry classification treats every passing retry as a non-blocking flake, with no exception for security checks. This leaves the request’s requirement that a security failure never become a pass unmet. The behavior predates this diff, but the change does not address it. A focused reproduction using `retryRegressions` with a failed check named `security` and a passing fake runner returned `[{"verdict":"flaky","blocking":false}]`.
findings.suggestion: Represent security checks explicitly in trusted gate configuration and keep their original failures blocking after any retry. Add a fake-runner test covering both targeted and full retries.
findings.failure_scenario: A security scan passes on the baseline, reports a vulnerability after the change, and passes on its full retry; the comparison becomes non-blocking `flaky` despite the original security failure.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing and heartbeat slice, including TLS and sandbox registration. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout resolved a missing MCP dependency and an incompatible Zod version. The request permits splitting gate execution into a later PR, so its absence is not reported here.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any TLS certificate and receives both the code and claim secret over that connection. A network attacker can proxy the request to the coordinator, relay the same code to the worker, and retain the claim secret. The owner sees matching codes and approves, after which the attacker can claim the worker token. Pinning the attacker's certificate for subsequent requests does not prevent this.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-compared pairing code to the coordinator certificate and the pairing exchange, or use another authenticated pairing protocol that prevents a relay from learning the claim credential.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts a worker's first connection, relays the pair request and code to the real coordinator, and claims the approved token using the observed secret.

findings.title: Worker credentials are protected only in the worker process
findings.detail: Private-file registrations live in a process-local map. The worker CLI registers its token and coordinator fingerprint in its own process, but a separate Limitless daemon on the same machine builds agent sandbox policies without those registrations. After pairing exits, its registrations are also released. Consequently, an agent running under that daemon can read the persisted worker credentials despite their mode 0600, because it runs as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential paths in every process that constructs agent or gate sandboxes, before launching work, including when the worker CLI is not running.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine is paired as a worker and also runs the daemon; a sandboxed agent launched by the daemon reads the worker token from the data directory and impersonates the worker.

findings.title: Disabling the listener removes protection from its existing TLS key
findings.detail: The coordinator key is registered as private only when the listener starts. If the owner disables workers.listen after previously enabling it, the key remains on disk but the daemon no longer registers it in sandbox deny paths. Sandboxed agents running as the same user can then read it.
findings.suggestion: Protect the persistent coordinator key path independently of whether the listener is currently enabled.
findings.failure_scenario: A coordinator is restarted with workers.listen unset after its TLS key was generated; a subsequent agent reads the retained key from the data directory.

output.summary: Reviewed the listener, pairing, heartbeats, credential handling, and the proposed split into a first slice. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/config-routing.test.ts` could not run: the checkout lacked `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js`, and its installed Zod lacked `z.number().overwrite`. No test assertions ran.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator certificate
findings.detail: The first request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker pins the certificate from that connection after displaying the coordinator-supplied code. An attacker between the worker and coordinator can relay the pairing request and its response, display the genuine code to the worker, and retain the pairing secret. Owner approval then lets the attacker claim the worker token, while the worker pins the attacker's certificate. Comparing the displayed codes does not detect this relay.
findings.suggestion: Bind the human-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate and pairing exchange, or require the coordinator fingerprint to be verified through an independent trusted channel before sending pairing secrets.
findings.failure_scenario: An on-path attacker proxies the initial pairing request to the real coordinator and forwards its code and secret to the worker. The owner approves the matching code, and the attacker claims the resulting token.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation permanently blocks listener startup
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the key file before starting OpenSSL, but an error or process interruption leaves partial TLS material behind. Every later startup rejects an incomplete pair, so a transient failure during first startup prevents the daemon from starting until an operator manually removes the files.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names and publish them only after successful validation, cleaning up incomplete temporary material on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped after creating key.pem but before OpenSSL writes cert.pem. On every subsequent start, certificate() throws "Incomplete worker TLS material" and startDaemon fails.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing, heartbeat, TLS, CLI and persistence changes. The request explicitly permits this first split without gate jobs. Targeted tests could not run: the checkout's dependencies lack @simplewebauthn/server and provide a Zod version without number().overwrite.

findings.title: The temporary worker token is readable by concurrent agents
findings.detail: The token is first written to a randomly named sibling file. Its protection is registered only in the pairing CLI process, while the daemon builds agent sandbox policies from its own process-local private-path registry and protects only the final token path. A concurrently running agent with home-directory read access can read the temporary file before rename; mode 0600 does not protect it from agents running as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Publish the token through a path that the daemon's sandbox policy already denies, including for agents started before pairing begins.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker is paired on a machine whose daemon is running an agent while the token temporary file exists; the agent reads that file and obtains the worker bearer token.

findings.title: An approved pairing that was never claimed prevents a new pairing
findings.detail: Approval permanently changes the row to approved, but the claim still expires after ten minutes. If the worker cannot claim before expiry, a subsequent pairing with the same name is rejected indefinitely until the owner manually revokes it.
findings.suggestion: Allow an expired, never-claimed approval to be replaced, or provide an explicit recovery path.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner approves just before expiry or the worker loses connectivity after approval; the claim expires and rerunning worker pair with the same name fails.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation leaves the listener unable to start
findings.detail: The key file is created before the asynchronous OpenSSL command, and failures leave partial material behind. Every later start rejects an incomplete key/certificate pair instead of recovering, so a transient failure or interruption during first start requires manual file cleanup.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files in temporary paths and publish them only after successful validation, cleaning up partial output on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after creating key.pem but before OpenSSL creates cert.pem; all subsequent starts with the worker listener enabled fail with incomplete TLS material.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing, heartbeat, TLS and sandbox paths. The request permits this pairing-and-heartbeat-only split. Focused tests could not load: the installed dependencies lack @simplewebauthn/server and provide an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Temporary worker credentials are not protected in other processes
findings.detail: privateFile registers the randomly named temporary file only in the pairing process's in-memory private-path registry. A daemon running under the same data home protects the final token and fingerprint paths, but does not know this temporary path. An agent sandbox created by that daemon can therefore read the temporary token during the write-to-rename interval if its policy otherwise permits reading the worker directory.
findings.suggestion: Publish credentials through a location that is already denied to all agent processes, or use a cross-process protection mechanism that covers temporary files before they are written.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker is paired while a daemon on the same machine has a tool-enabled reader running; the reader accesses the token's temporary file after it is written and before it is renamed.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation permanently prevents startup
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates key.pem before invoking openssl, but failure or interruption leaves that file behind. Every subsequent start sees incomplete TLS material and throws, including when the listener is enabled during daemon startup. A transient openssl failure or daemon interruption therefore requires manual removal of the partial material before the daemon can start again.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files in temporary paths and publish them only after successful generation, with cleanup or recovery for interrupted first starts.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped after creating key.pem but before openssl writes cert.pem; the next daemon start fails with "Incomplete worker TLS material".

output.summary: Reviewed the lease lifecycle, worker result validation, fallback, and restart paths. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout’s installed dependencies are incomplete or incompatible: `test/workers.test.ts` could not find `@simplewebauthn/server`, and `test/gate-executor.test.ts` encountered a Zod version without `number().overwrite`.

findings.title: A completed failing check can disappear after an infrastructure retry
findings.detail: Check events from an attempt are streamed, but the executor returns only the final attempt’s GateRun. If a worker posts a failing check and then loses its lease before posting the final result, a second worker or local fallback can pass that check and the pipeline receives a clean pass. The earlier failure is retained only as an event and does not affect the verdict.
findings.suggestion: Carry completed check outcomes across infrastructure attempts and preserve a failing outcome when a later attempt passes, using the existing flaky-result semantics where appropriate.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts a failed test check, disconnects before posting its GateRun, and worker B passes the same check; the returned GateRun reports a pass.

findings.title: Persisted LAN jobs cannot resume after switching back to the local executor
findings.detail: A run can checkpoint a LAN handle before the daemon restarts. On restart with the executor configured as local, executeGate rejects that stored handle as unavailable instead of reattaching or safely resolving the pending job. Rolling back to the previous release has the same compatibility problem because that release cannot execute a LAN handle. This leaves an in-progress run unable to resume after a supported rollback or configuration change.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable compatibility path for pending LAN handles across executor changes and rollback, or arrange for the older release to handle the persisted state before writing it.
findings.failure_scenario: A run checkpoints a LAN gate job, the daemon stops, and the operator rolls back or changes `gates.executor` to `local`; resuming the run throws `Unavailable gate executor: lan`.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease, execution, validation, cancellation and restart paths. Targeted tests could not load because this checkout lacks @simplewebauthn/server and its installed Zod lacks number().overwrite; no test assertions ran.

findings.title: Resume discards in-flight retry and timeout jobs
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial and rebase purposes. A LAN job checkpointed for a timeout rerun or regression/baseline retry is therefore cancelled on restart and a new job is enqueued, even if the original worker is still running or has already completed it. This defeats durable reattachment for those gate jobs and can repeat gate side effects.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to reattach every checkpointed LAN execution, and test restart during a retry and timeout rerun.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after checkpointing a regression-retry job but before consuming its result. On resume, the pending handle fails the purpose check, is cancelled, and the retry is submitted again.

findings.title: Enqueue and checkpoint can leave an orphaned gate job
findings.detail: The job is committed to the database before executeGate persists its handle in the run checkpoint. If the coordinator stops or checkpoint persistence fails in that interval, the queued job remains eligible for leasing, while the resumed run has no handle and enqueues another job. The orphan can execute and transfer repository code after the run has moved on or been cancelled.
findings.suggestion: Make job creation and durable association with the run checkpoint atomic, or add a recovery mechanism that identifies and cancels uncheckpointed jobs before they can be leased.
findings.failure_scenario: The process exits after workers.enqueue returns but before the gate-started checkpoint is saved. A worker leases the first job while the restarted run creates a second one.

findings.title: Worker-specific credential redaction invalidates legitimate check identities
findings.detail: The worker redacts every string in check events and results, including the configured check name and command. The coordinator validates those fields against the original request using only its own credential registry. If a worker credential occurs in a legitimate command or name but is unknown to the coordinator, the returned identity no longer matches and the coordinator treats the job as an infrastructure failure.
findings.suggestion: Use a stable check identity that does not require sending secret-bearing command text, and validate that identity independently of worker-local redaction.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker has a registered credential whose value appears in a gate command, such as a test fixture literal. The worker replaces that text before posting the event; validCheck compares it with the coordinator's unredacted command and rejects the result.

output.summary: Reviewed the land-check retry and restart paths. The gate retry tests passed (43 tests). The land queue tests could not run because the checkout is missing the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency.

findings.title: Skip retries when another check already requires blocking
findings.detail: The queue selects retry candidates before checking whether other results are independently blocking. Consequently, it runs a targeted retry even when lint failed without failed files, another check timed out, or a check reported a confinement failure. The request requires those cases to block with no retry. The added mixed-failure test instead expects the retry.
findings.suggestion: Before starting retries, determine whether any result requires an unconditional block; if so, block immediately.
findings.failure_scenario: The test check reports a failed file while lint exits nonzero without failed files. The queue runs the test retry and only then blocks on lint.

findings.title: Preserve flaky evidence across a restart before the CI checkpoint
findings.detail: A successful retry records the flaky reason while the entry is still checking. If the daemon restarts before pushedSha is recorded, checking runs again and truncates the same log. A clean rerun leaves the old flaky reason in place, but the landed entry's log no longer contains the first failure or its retry.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the earlier check attempts in the land log across checking resumes, and keep the recorded flaky reason consistent with that evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, then the daemon restarts during the private-range check before the waiting_ci checkpoint. The resumed checks pass cleanly and overwrite the log; the eventual landed entry still says flaky but its log has no failure or retry.

output.summary: Reviewed the land-check retry, logging and restart paths. The targeted gate-retry tests passed, but the land-queue tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js was unavailable in the sandbox.

findings.title: A restart can retain a flake reason after its evidence is overwritten
findings.detail: The flaky reason is stored before the checks are checkpointed as complete. If the daemon stops in that interval, the entry resumes from checking and reruns the checks. The next attempt overwrites the land log, but a clean pass does not clear the old reason. The landed entry can therefore report a flaky check whose first failure and retry are no longer in its log.
findings.suggestion: Keep the flaky evidence consistent with the attempt that authorizes landing, for example by resetting the reason when starting a fresh check attempt or preserving the prior attempt's log.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, the flaky reason is saved, and the daemon restarts before pushedSha is recorded. The resumed full checks pass cleanly; the entry lands with the old flaky reason while its rewritten log contains only the clean attempt.

output.summary: The new smoke check does not exercise the verification pipeline’s actual command-wrapper path. Focused tests could not run because this checkout has missing or incompatible dependencies: the command reported missing sandbox-runtime and MCP SDK modules and an incompatible zod API.

findings.title: Bun smoke check bypasses the verifier’s command wrapper
findings.detail: The check sets confineReads and supplies no commandPath, then invokes Bun by absolute path. Actual verification in engine.ts does not set confineReads; context.ts therefore installs the configured slotted-command wrappers, including the bun test wrapper in this repository. The smoke check can pass while the wrapper hangs or fails, which is the failure mode reported in the request.
findings.suggestion: Run the smoke invocation through the same verifier options and slotted-command setup as the pipeline, and have it execute bun test through PATH.
findings.failure_scenario: The verifier’s bun test wrapper cannot reach its lease service and hangs, while the direct absolute-path Bun command used by the smoke check succeeds; smoke reports a pass although verification remains blocked.

output.summary: Reviewed the sandbox settings, executable selection, and smoke-check path. The targeted test command could not load its test files because this checkout has missing or incompatible dependencies, including @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime and the installed Zod version.

findings.title: Allow the Bun executable verifiers actually resolve
findings.detail: The allowance covers only the daemon's process.execPath. A verifier invoking `bun test` resolves `bun` through its shell PATH, which can select a different installation under a denied private root. That executable remains unreadable, so the original verification failure can persist. The new smoke check also invokes process.execPath directly, so it can pass while the verifier's ordinary `bun test` fails.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the Bun executable from the verifier's effective PATH and grant its validated canonical spellings; have the smoke check run `bun test` through that same PATH.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts with Bun from one installation, while the verifier's PATH selects another Bun installation under the user's home directory. The smoke probe passes using the daemon executable, but `bun test` in the verifier cannot read the PATH-selected executable.

output.summary: Reviewed the shared sanitizer and its delivery and land call sites. The focused publication test could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; isolated execution of the sanitizer reproduced the findings below.

findings.title: Paths in Markdown labels and file URLs remain publishable
findings.detail: The matcher consumes an entire Markdown link and only examines its destination, so an absolute path in the label survives when the destination is relative. The negative lookbehind also prevents matching a path immediately after file://. Either form can publish the owner's username and data layout; once the username is added to the private strings list, it can instead block delivery. An isolated execution returned `[/factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts](src/a.ts)` and `file:///factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts` unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths throughout link text and handle file URLs, while preserving ordinary remote links.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains `[/factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts](src/a.ts)` or `file:///factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts`; the public report retains the absolute local path.

findings.title: Normalize paths before deciding whether they belong to the worktree
findings.detail: The prefix check treats paths containing `..` as worktree paths even when they resolve outside the worktree. Isolated execution of the sanitizer returned `[../other/secret.txt](../other/secret.txt)` for `[file](/factory/data/work/run/../other/secret.txt)`, although that path is under the data directory outside the worktree and should become plain text with a `<data>` prefix.
findings.suggestion: Normalize the path components before classifying the destination against the worktree and data-directory roots.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to `/factory/data/work/run/../other/secret.txt`; publication produces a repo-relative link rather than a `<data>` placeholder.

output.summary: Reviewed the publication rewrite and its delivery call sites. The focused test could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. A direct invocation of the transpiled rewrite function exposed the path cases below.

findings.title: Absolute paths in Markdown link labels bypass rewriting
findings.detail: The link expression consumes the entire link, but when its destination is already relative the callback returns the whole match unchanged. An absolute worktree path used as the visible label therefore reaches a public PR, or blocks delivery once the username is added to private-strings.txt. A direct invocation returned `[/factory/data/work/run/file.ts](file.ts)` unchanged for that input.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize link labels as well as destinations, including when the destination itself does not require rewriting.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains `[/factory/data/work/run/file.ts](file.ts)`.

findings.title: Traversal paths outside the worktree are classified as worktree paths
findings.detail: The containment check compares raw prefixes without resolving `..`. A direct invocation changed `/factory/data/work/run/../other/secret` to `../other/secret`, although that path points outside the run's worktree and should use the data-directory placeholder. Links can consequently point outside the repository instead of becoming plain text.
findings.suggestion: Normalize path components before deciding which root contains the path, while preserving any Markdown location suffix separately.
findings.failure_scenario: A report references a sibling run or scratch file through `/factory/data/work/run/../other/secret`.

findings.title: Data placeholders are emitted as Markdown HTML tags
findings.detail: The literal `<data>` is parsed as an inline HTML tag in GitHub Markdown rather than displayed as plain text. Thus a rewritten log link such as `<data>/runs/log.txt` does not visibly show the requested placeholder in the published report.
findings.suggestion: Escape the angle brackets or otherwise render the placeholder as literal text in Markdown.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to a log under the factory data directory and the resulting PR body is rendered on GitHub.

output.summary: The new checks protect the tested outcome writes, but claim loss can still precede a merge or push inside the asynchronous helpers. The targeted land-queue test could not start because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing.

findings.title: Recheck the claim inside the merge helper before each merge command
findings.detail: The ownership check happens before mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup and may retry before invoking gh pr merge. A reclaim during either wait leaves the old signal live until its next heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue the merge command.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helper and invoke it immediately before every merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker enters mergePullRequest, its PR view is delayed, another owner reclaims the entry, and the view returns before the old heartbeat; the old worker then runs gh pr merge.

findings.title: Recheck the claim immediately before the push
findings.detail: pushExistingBranch awaits commit resolution, a remote lookup, and an ancestor check after the queue's ownership check. If the claim changes during those waits, the old worker can still push before its heartbeat detects the loss.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard to the push helper and check it immediately before issuing the push command.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker passes the check at line 517, pauses during ls-remote, and another worker reclaims the entry; when ls-remote returns, the old worker pushes the merge commit.

findings.title: Prevent a lost worker from deleting the new worker's checkout
findings.detail: The finally block always discards the per-entry worktree, even when the worker exits because its claim was lost. Both attempts use the same land-<id> path, so a new owner can recreate that checkout before the old worker's cleanup removes it.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts distinct checkout paths or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a checkout belonging to a newer claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A reclaimed entry starts in another process and creates its checkout while the old worker is awaiting CI; the old response arrives, detects claim loss, and its finally block deletes the new worker's checkout.

output.summary: The new ownership checks protect several queue writes, but claim loss can still precede a merge or push inside the called helpers, and CI inspection can still write after reclaim. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before issuing the command
findings.detail: The ownership check occurs before calling `mergePullRequest`, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing `gh pr merge`, and may await further lookups and retries. A reclaim during one of those awaits leaves the old signal live until its next heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue a merge after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the merge helper and check it immediately before each merge attempt, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker enters `mergePullRequest`, its `gh pr view` response is deferred, another owner reclaims the entry, and the view returns before the next heartbeat. The old worker then runs `gh pr merge`.

findings.title: Recheck ownership immediately before the push
findings.detail: The guarded checkpoint precedes `pushExistingBranch`, which itself awaits revision resolution, remote inspection and an ancestry check before running the push. Reclaim during any of those awaits permits the old worker to push before its heartbeat notices the loss.
findings.suggestion: Provide the push helper with a claim guard and invoke it immediately before the remote push.
findings.failure_scenario: After `pushedSha` is recorded, the worker pauses in `pushExistingBranch` while reading the remote. Another owner reclaims the entry, then the read completes before the heartbeat and the old worker pushes its merge commit.

findings.title: Guard CI inspection writes after its awaited reads
findings.detail: Passing `current` to `ciDecision` does not guard every write in its implementation. In particular, `inspectCi` awaits the default-branch checks and then emits feed items and writes the `ci.main` setting before checking `current`; its rerun response path also writes an outcome after an await without rechecking. A reclaimed worker can therefore still change durable CI state.
findings.suggestion: Make the CI inspection check ownership transactionally with its writes, including after rerun responses.
findings.failure_scenario: A failing CI inspection is paused while fetching default-branch checks, the entry is reclaimed, and the response returns before the old heartbeat. The old inspection writes CI episode state and can emit a feed item despite having lost its claim.

findings.title: Do not remove the new owner's worktree on claim loss
findings.detail: The `finally` block always discards the entry's shared worktree path, including when an ownership check detects a reclaim. The replacement worker uses the same `land-<entry id>` path, so the old worker can remove the replacement's checkout while it is running.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts separate worktree paths or coordinate cleanup so an old attempt cannot remove a newer attempt's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A new owner reclaims an entry and creates its checkout while the old worker is awaiting CI. The old response arrives, the ownership check throws, and the old worker's `finally` removes the new owner's checkout.

output.summary: Reviewed the claim fencing, merge and push paths, CI inspection, and worktree cleanup. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the entities dependency.

findings.title: A refused rerun can remain pending after claim loss
findings.detail: The rerun is recorded as rerun_requested before the POST. If the land claim changes while the POST is in flight, the new guard discards the response. When GitHub refused the request, the replacement worker sees the persisted pending rerun and waits for a later workflow attempt that will never exist. The added test checks that the old worker makes no further writes, but does not resume the replacement worker. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts test/ci-classifier.test.ts test/github-delivery.test.ts` could not execute: `error: Cannot find package 'entities' from '.../src/gates/publication.ts'`.
findings.suggestion: Provide a recovery path for an unconfirmed rerun request that lets the current owner reconcile a refusal without letting the stale worker write.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient CI failure is marked rerun_requested, its rerun POST returns HTTP 422 after another worker reclaims the land entry, and the workflow attempt never advances. The replacement waits until the CI deadline instead of reporting the failure.

findings.title: Merged resumes leave the previous attempt's worktree behind
findings.detail: Worktree paths now include the attempt number, but this early merged-resume path discards only the newly claimed attempt's path. The crashed attempt's worktree and associated registration are cleaned only by checkout, which this path skips.
findings.suggestion: Clean older attempt worktrees on the already-merged resume path as well.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker merges the PR and crashes before its finally block; the next claim observes the PR already merged and removes land-<id>-<new attempt>, leaving land-<id>-<old attempt> on disk.

output.summary: Reviewed claim ownership, push and merge retries, CI handling, and restart behavior. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package.

findings.title: Recheck ownership before each push retry
findings.detail: The guard runs once before remoteSh, but remoteSh retries transient failures internally. A claim can be reclaimed while the first push attempt or its retry delay is pending, and the old worker then starts another push without checking ownership.
findings.suggestion: Run the claim guard inside the retry callback immediately before each push attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: The first git push fails transiently, another worker reclaims the entry before the retry, and the old worker issues a second push before its heartbeat detects the loss.

findings.title: Recover when a claim is lost before the recorded push
findings.detail: The worker records pushedSha before pushExistingBranch completes its internal reads. The new guard can then refuse the push after a reclaim, leaving the replacement worker with a SHA that was never pushed. The resume path accepts the still-approved remote head but waits for CI on the unpushed SHA, eventually blocking the entry.
findings.suggestion: Make the resume path distinguish an unperformed push from a completed push and safely complete or recover it under the new claim.
findings.failure_scenario: The base merge produces a new SHA; the worker records it, loses its claim during pushExistingBranch's remote lookup, and the guard prevents the push. The replacement waits for CI on a commit absent from the PR.

findings.title: Prevent stale gate callbacks from writing the replacement's log
findings.detail: Gate result callbacks append to a log path shared by every attempt without checking the claim. A gate already running when the entry is reclaimed can append after the replacement has started its checks, mixing stale results into the replacement's durable log. This also violates the requirement that a worker which lost its claim writes nothing.
findings.suggestion: Guard gate log writes against claim loss and isolate log paths by attempt so stale callbacks cannot alter another attempt's evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate result is deferred, a new owner reclaims the entry and starts a new attempt, then the old gate completes before its heartbeat fires and appends its output to the new attempt's log.

output.summary: Reviewed the runless queue, persistence, restart and CLI paths. The store tests passed; the queue tests could not load because the MCP SDK module is missing from the checkout.

findings.title: Accept PR numbers for runless land requests
findings.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, although the requested command is `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>` and the existing CLI accepts PR numbers. A PR number that has no matching factory run is rejected before GitHub is queried.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository using the CLI's repository context, then apply the same repository and head checks as for a URL.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless land 599 --sha <full-head-sha>` for an open, unowned PR and receives `run not found`.

findings.title: Do not reject all fork pull requests
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories, but this unconditional check rejects PRs whose head is in a fork. Those PRs cannot use the new confined landing path even when the factory has permission to update the head branch.
findings.suggestion: Support fork heads with the same pinned-head and publication checks, or provide a supported confined landing path for them.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targets a configured repository but was opened from a contributor's fork; requesting its land fails with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`.

findings.title: Preserve active runless entries across rollback
findings.detail: Runless entries are persisted with an empty `run_id`. The previous release reads that value as a run ID and its land worker blocks the entry with `run  is gone`. Thus a rollback while an unowned land is queued or in progress permanently changes it to blocked, rather than leaving it resumable after the newer release returns.
findings.suggestion: Make the persisted representation safe for the previous worker to ignore, or otherwise ensure old releases cannot claim and block runless entries.
findings.failure_scenario: A new daemon queues an unowned PR, then deployment rolls back before it finishes. The old daemon claims the active entry and marks it blocked because no run has the empty ID.

output.summary: Reviewed the queue, persistence, CLI, and resume paths. The land-store tests passed. The land-queue tests could not run because the sandbox checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: Unowned PR numbers are rejected
findings.detail: The unowned path accepts only a full GitHub URL, although the requested command is `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>` and the existing CLI accepts a PR number. A number for a PR without a factory run reaches this path and returns `run not found`.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL before applying the unowned PR checks, or provide an explicit repository selection when it is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless land 599 --sha <full-sha>` for an open unowned PR in a configured repository; the request is refused.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: Unowned entries are persisted with an empty `run_id`. The previous release reads that value as a run ID and its queue context throws `run  is gone`, permanently blocking an active entry after rollback. The additive column keeps old inserts working but does not preserve the previous release's ability to resume new entries.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and resume behavior for active unowned entries, or explicitly prevent an older daemon from claiming them without turning them into blocked entries.
findings.failure_scenario: A deployment creates an unowned land, stops while it is queued or waiting for CI, and rolls back. The previous daemon claims the entry and marks it blocked because no run has the empty ID.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are excluded from the requested feature
findings.detail: The new path rejects every cross-repository PR. The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding PRs contributed from forks, so these PRs cannot use the confined land queue.
findings.suggestion: Support fork heads while preserving the approved-head lease and publication checks, or obtain an explicit scope decision for excluding them.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targets a configured repository and its head is a contributor's fork; requesting land at its full current SHA fails with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`.

findings.title: A changed PR base can bypass checks for the actual merge target
findings.detail: The unowned request records the base branch once and subsequent processing fetches and checks that branch without confirming that GitHub still targets it. Changing a PR's base does not change its head SHA, so the head pin does not detect this. GitHub's final merge uses the PR's current base, which can differ from the base whose commit and checks were used.
findings.suggestion: Re-read and validate the PR's base branch before pushing and merging, and block if it differs from the approved entry's base.
findings.failure_scenario: After approval against `main`, someone retargets the PR to `release` without changing its head. The queue checks a merge of `main` and then squash-merges the PR into `release`.

output.summary: Reviewed cleanup persistence, recovery, startup and resume paths. The targeted test file could not fully run because the MCP SDK dependency was missing. One inspection test timed out in the full file but passed when rerun alone.

findings.title: Recovery misses descendants discovered after the crash
findings.detail: Recovery kills only identities already in the database and then deletes the invocation's records. Live cleanup deliberately rescans after freezing because descendants can fork between snapshots, but recovery never performs that rescan. A crash after the first freeze can therefore leave a later descendant running while recovery reports success and allows the next step to start.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation discovery information to resume the sweep, and retain the cleanup record until discovery and termination have both completed.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked process forks after the initial scan; the daemon freezes the initial claimed set and crashes before the next scan records the new child. Recovery kills the recorded members, deletes the records, and leaves the unrecorded child running in the checkout.

findings.title: Linux birth identities can match unrelated processes after reboot
findings.detail: On Linux, processBirth stores only the process start time in boot-relative clock ticks. Persisted records survive a reboot, so a process on the next boot can have the same PID and tick value as the old member. Recovery treats that collision as the original identity and sends SIGKILL to an unrelated process.
findings.suggestion: Include a boot identity in persisted Linux process identities and treat a record from a different boot as no longer owning a live process.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending record contains PID 100 and start tick 500; after reboot, an unrelated process receives PID 100 and also starts at tick 500. Daemon startup signals that unrelated process.

output.summary: Reviewed persistence, recovery, process identity, and the crash test. The targeted command `bun test test/process-cleanup.test.ts` reported 7 passes and 4 failures: one inspection test timed out, and three tests could not load the missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js` dependency. Those environment-limited results do not establish additional findings.

findings.title: Recovery clears a partial snapshot without finding remaining descendants
findings.detail: Cleanup persists members one at a time, and the normal sweep deliberately rescans because a process can fork between discovery and freezing. Recovery only kills the rows already recorded and then deletes them; it never resumes discovery or retains an unresolved invocation marker. A crash during the initial recording loop, or after a descendant forks but before the next sweep records it, leaves an unrecorded descendant running while recovery declares the invocation complete. Subsequent work can then start in the same checkout while that process can still write to it.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation-level discovery state before cleanup begins to resume the sweep after a crash, and clear it only after discovery and termination are confirmed complete.
findings.failure_scenario: Two marked descendants are discovered and the daemon dies after recording the first but before recording the second. On restart recovery kills the first, deletes the invocation's records, and allows the run to continue with the second descendant alive.

findings.title: Linux birth identities can match an unrelated process after reboot
findings.detail: On Linux, `processBirth` records only `/proc/<pid>/stat` start ticks since boot. Pending records survive reboot, but the tick count restarts, so an unrelated process can receive both the same PID and the same start tick on a later boot. Recovery then treats that process as the recorded member and sends it SIGKILL. The birth identity therefore does not establish identity across the lifetime of the persisted record.
findings.suggestion: Include a boot-unique identifier in Linux persisted identities and treat records from a different boot as no longer belonging to live processes.
findings.failure_scenario: A cleanup record survives a reboot; after reboot an unrelated process obtains the recorded PID and starts at the same boot-relative tick. Daemon startup signals that unrelated process.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, test markers, and subprocess handling. The marker test passed locally; the Linux-specific timeout tests were skipped on macOS, where GNU timeout was unavailable. The workflow change also has an automated audit flag requiring `Allow: workflows` in the request.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup leaves detached descendants running
findings.detail: The exit trap kills only the timeout process group. Descendants that create their own process group or session survive both that kill and the earlier TERM. This repository's subprocess runner uses detached processes, and some tests start detached grandchildren that inherit output streams. If one hangs, it can keep the step's output pipe open after the wrapper exits, allowing the outer job timeout to cancel the job and lose the log. It also fails the helper's requirement to stop its children.
findings.suggestion: Track and terminate the check's descendant process groups, including detached descendants, and add a Linux test with a detached child that holds an output stream open past the timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: A test hangs while a detached subprocess retains the step's stdout or stderr; the wrapper kills its own process group but the detached subprocess remains alive and keeps the runner's output pipe open.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, file-start markers, and targeted tests. The marker test passed; the two GNU timeout tests were skipped because this environment is not Linux, so their behavior could not be verified here. The workflow change is explicitly required by the request despite the audit flag.

Reviewed the audit warning, round feedback, and publication diagnostics. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; no actionable defect was established by inspection.

Reviewed the audit, feedback, and publication paths. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. A separate Git probe confirmed that ANSI-colored output is treated as text.

findings.title: Large text logs with ANSI control sequences miss the warning
findings.detail: The size map excludes blobs that fail the stricter reviewable-content check, even when Git treats them as text. Terminal and gate logs commonly contain ANSI escape sequences, so a large new log can bypass the large-text warning. A targeted Git probe with an ANSI escape followed by 102,401 characters produced `1\t0\treport.txt` from `git diff --cached --numstat`, confirming Git treats the file as text.
findings.suggestion: Record sizes for new text blobs independently of the stricter reviewable-content classification, and add a regression test using a large ANSI-colored log.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer commits a new 100 KiB-plus gate log outside a hidden root directory, and the log contains an ANSI color escape. It receives no large-text-addition warning or associated round feedback.

output.summary: Reviewed the decoding changes and publication callers. The targeted publication test could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; a direct decoding probe ran successfully.

findings.title: Publication checks do not include registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 matcher only checks the entries passed by its caller. Production publication checks pass private-string entries, while registered credentials are added only for refusal filename diagnosis. Consequently, base64-encoded registered credentials in published content, commit metadata, or PR text are not blocked. The new test constructs a combined entries list itself, so it does not exercise the production call path.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected entries used by every publication check, and test through a production publication caller.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential is base64-encoded in an added file and is absent from private-strings.txt; checkPrivatePublication scans it with private entries only and permits publication.

findings.title: Nested base64 encoding bypasses the decoding layers
findings.detail: A base64 run is decoded only if its immediate decoded text already contains a protected value. An outer base64 layer containing another base64 encoding therefore never reaches the next decoding round, leaving the protected value undetected in both publication and audit filenames. A direct probe returned an empty match list for a doubly encoded credential.
findings.suggestion: Detect protected values through bounded successive base64 decoding while retaining the existing convergence and false-positive safeguards.
findings.failure_scenario: For credential synthetic-secret-credential, the filename YzNsdWRHaGxkR2xqTFhObFkzSmxkQzFqY21Wa1pXNTBhV0Zz is returned unchanged because its first decoded layer is itself base64.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit and publication decoding paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. A direct decoder probe exposed a nested-base64 bypass.

findings.title: Production publication checks omit registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 matcher only checks the entries supplied by its caller. Production publication paths supply private-string entries, not registered credentials: for example, checkPublication in src/pipeline/engine.ts obtains entries from privateEntries, and checkPrivatePublication passes its entries through to content and blob checks. The added test manually adds credentials to its entries, so it does not exercise this production behavior. A base64-encoded registered credential can therefore still be published in PR text or repository content.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected values used by every publication check, and test a production publication path with a registered credential absent from private-strings.txt.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential is base64-encoded in a PR body or changed file while it is absent from private-strings.txt; literal credential redaction leaves the encoding intact and the publication check accepts it.

findings.title: Base64 decoding stops before nested encodings can be inspected
findings.detail: base64Match returns decoded text only when that single decoding already contains a protected value. Consequently, a base64 run containing another encoded form is never handed to the successive decoding loop. The targeted command `bun -e 'import {privateMatches} from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const v="synthetic-secret-value"; const encoded=Buffer.from(Buffer.from(v).toString("base64")).toString("base64"); console.log(JSON.stringify({encoded,matches:privateMatches(encoded,[{value:v,entry:1}])}));'` returned `{"encoded":"YzNsdWRHaGxkR2xqTFhObFkzSmxkQzEyWVd4MVpRPT0=","matches":[]}`. The same decoder is used for audit filenames and publication checks.
findings.suggestion: Inspect bounded successive decoding of candidate base64 runs, including combinations with the existing percent and Unicode decoders, without treating unrelated runs as decoding failures.
findings.failure_scenario: A filename or published text contains a private entry encoded twice in base64, or percent-encoded and then base64-encoded; the protected value survives the check and can be persisted or published.

output.summary: Reviewed the aggregation, invocation storage, eval runner, and CLI and HTTP paths. The provider workload tests passed. The combined targeted test command could not validate CLI or HTTP behavior because the installed dependencies lack an MCP SDK module and have an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Eval panel calls are attributed to the trial's primary provider
findings.detail: For trials without implementation rounds, the aggregation treats the entire trial as one invocation of details.provider and model_id. Review panels can call finders and verifiers on other providers and combine their spend and tokens into the trial totals. Those calls are therefore omitted from their actual providers and charged to the primary provider, while the invocation count is also understated.
findings.suggestion: Use per-call stored evidence where available and represent unattributable panel usage as unknown rather than assigning it to the primary provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval uses provider A for its primary model and provider B for a verifier; the endpoint reports one invocation and all combined cost and tokens under A, with no workload for B.

findings.title: Discard available cache totals for implementation evals
findings.detail: Every trial with round evidence forces cache-read and cache-write tokens to null, even when the trial has persisted cache totals and consists of a single round. Since one null makes the entire aggregate null, a normal implementation eval also makes its provider's input and cached-token totals unavailable.
findings.suggestion: Use the persisted trial cache totals when they can be attributed to a provider and model, including single-round trials; retain unknown values only where attribution is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read and 20 cache-write tokens. Its eval provider, model, role and day totals all report null for those values and for uncached input.

output.summary: Reviewed the storage, aggregation, HTTP, and CLI paths. The workload tests passed, but CLI and HTTP checks could not run successfully because the local dependencies are missing or incompatible: the test run reported a missing MCP SDK module and a Zod prefault error.

findings.title: Eval trials and rounds are reported as individual provider invocations
findings.detail: A trial or round can contain multiple provider calls. The eval runner combines panel calls and resume retries into trial or round totals, but this code counts the combined record once and attributes all of its usage to the trial or round's target provider and model. Invocation counts, success shares, and per-provider/model costs therefore misrepresent those evals.
findings.suggestion: Use stored per-call evidence where available, and represent measurements that cannot be attributed or counted from the stored data as unknown rather than as individual invocations.
findings.failure_scenario: A review panel calls a finder and verifier on different providers: the combined spend is assigned to the trial's provider and counted as one invocation, while the other provider receives no workload.

findings.title: Recorded eval cache totals become unknown whenever rounds exist
findings.detail: The runner persists aggregate cache-read and cache-write counts in trial details even for implementation trials with rounds. This branch discards both values for every round; summarize then makes the provider's entire eval cache and uncached-input totals null if any such record exists. Consequently the requested token totals are unavailable even when the stored trial supplies them.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate the persisted trial-level cache totals at the appropriate provider and model level where attribution is known, while retaining unknown values for breakdowns that cannot be attributed.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation eval with one round and recorded cacheReadTokens of 100 reports null cache-read tokens for the round, its model, and the provider's eval total.

findings.title: A running eval is counted before any provider call occurs
findings.detail: All running trials are selected, and a trial without rounds or invocationStatus is converted to a workload record unless it is skipped or marked as a preparation failure. A trial can be persisted as running while it is preparing or waiting for a provider slot, before any invocation has happened. It is then reported as a failed invocation with zero usage.
findings.suggestion: Only count trials with persisted evidence that a provider call occurred; keep pending trials outside invocation totals.
findings.failure_scenario: A newly started eval trial waits for a provider slot with status running and zero usage; the endpoint reports one invocation and a successful share of zero despite no call having started.

output.summary: Reviewed signature selection, excerpt construction, redaction, and rerun compatibility. The focused test suite could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package. A direct Bun probe reproduced an excerpt that omits the selected failure line.

findings.title: A long Bun failure line is omitted from its excerpt
findings.detail: When an assertion block precedes a long `(fail)` line, the tail window keeps only the last part of that line. The excerpt can therefore omit the selected signature line and the beginning of the failing test name, depriving the fix round of the failure identification the change is intended to provide. The targeted command `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; const r=ciSignature("test", "error: assertion\n"+"x".repeat(3000)+"\n(fail) "+"a".repeat(3000), "fallback"); console.log(JSON.stringify({line:r.line.slice(0,30),excerptHasFail:r.excerpt.includes("(fail)"),length:r.excerpt.length}));'` produced `{"line":"(fail) aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","excerptHasFail":false,"length":1999}`.
findings.suggestion: Reserve excerpt space for the beginning of the chosen signature line, including when the preceding assertion block or the line itself exceeds the budget.
findings.failure_scenario: A Bun assertion emits a large diff followed by a failing test name longer than the remaining excerpt budget.

output.summary: Reviewed signature selection, excerpts, redaction and rerun compatibility. The targeted classifier test could not start because the checkout is missing the entities dependency; an independent redaction probe reproduced a credential leak.

findings.title: Windowed image redaction exposes short credentials
findings.detail: The padded text passed to redactCredentials contains surrounding log characters. Credentials shorter than eight characters are redacted only when the entire input equals the credential, so an image value that previously matched and was redacted is now returned and persisted in the signature. An independent probe reproduced the regression: `bun -e 'import {registerCredential,redactCredentials} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_SHORT","abc"); console.log("old:",redactCredentials("abc")); console.log("new:",redactCredentials("Image: abc\nerror: fail",{start:7,end:10}));'` printed `old: [redacted]` and `new: abc`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve exact-value redaction for the selected publication window while retaining padded matching for longer credentials, and add a regression test for a short credential used as an image value.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential is `abc` and a CI log contains `Image: abc` followed by a failure. The image field and serialized signature contain `abc` instead of `[redacted]`.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker lifecycle, event delivery, retry handling, and lease fencing. The targeted worker test could not run because the checkout is missing the @simplewebauthn/server dependency.

findings.title: Restarting event sequences loses events from retried jobs
findings.detail: Each attempt starts its event sequence at zero, but the coordinator retains event rows from prior attempts and ignores duplicate (job_id, seq) inserts. A reassigned job therefore silently loses every new batch whose sequence overlaps a prior attempt, and can retain stale events alongside the new result.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts distinct event namespaces or coordinate a persisted next sequence and define how prior-attempt events are handled.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batch 0 and loses its lease; worker B leases the same job and posts its own batch 0. The insert is ignored and B's events never reach the event log.

findings.title: Rejected event batches abort without reporting failure
findings.detail: The rejection handler aborts the job controller, so the catch block sees an aborted signal and skips the failure POST. The worker then stops reporting the job, leaving it leased until coordinator expiry instead of promptly failing it with the batch error.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish event-delivery failures from cancellation and use a separate bounded signal to report the failure before releasing the job.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an oversized or invalid event batch with a 4xx response while the lease remains valid. The harness is aborted, but no failure is posted and the job remains leased until expiry.

findings.title: Periodic fencing can allow execution beyond the lease period
findings.detail: The interval checks elapsed time only every heartbeat interval and uses a strict greater-than comparison. A heartbeat failure just after a check can leave an agent running for nearly one additional interval after its lease period has elapsed, while the coordinator may already have reassigned the job.
findings.suggestion: Schedule or reset a deadline timer from each successful heartbeat so running agents are aborted at the lease deadline.
findings.failure_scenario: With the default 60-second lease and 10-second heartbeat interval, a partition starts just after the last successful heartbeat; the agent can continue running for close to 70 seconds before the next fencing check.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker lease, checkout, reporting, and fencing paths. Focused tests could not start because the installed dependencies are inconsistent: `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/agent-test.test.ts` reported a missing `entities` package and an installed Zod without `prefault`.

findings.title: Event sequence numbers restart on every attempt
findings.detail: Each worker attempt starts its event sequence at zero, but agent_job_events is keyed by job ID and sequence and the coordinator silently ignores conflicting inserts. Events from a failed attempt remain in that table, so a later attempt loses every batch whose sequence overlaps the earlier attempt and can leave a mixture of events from different attempts.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts separate event streams or establish the next sequence number and retry semantics with the coordinator before posting events.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batches 0 and 1, then its lease expires. Worker B retries the same job and posts batches 0 and 1; both are accepted but ignored, and the completed job retains worker A's events instead of worker B's.

findings.title: A rejected event batch aborts without reporting failure
findings.detail: The batch rejection handler aborts the same controller used by the job. The catch block then skips the failure POST because jobSignal is aborted. The coordinator is left holding the lease until expiry instead of receiving the required failure and reason.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish event-post failure from cancellation and report it using a signal that remains usable for the failure notification.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid harness emits a batch larger than the coordinator's 1 MiB event body limit. The coordinator rejects it, the worker aborts the job, and no failure is posted; the job remains leased until its lease expires.

findings.title: Fencing can occur substantially after the lease expires
findings.detail: The fence checks elapsed time only at heartbeat-sized intervals and uses a strict greater-than comparison. A heartbeat that succeeds just after a check can leave a running agent active for nearly one additional heartbeat interval after the lease period has elapsed. At the default settings that can mean nearly 70 seconds without a successful heartbeat for a 60-second lease.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing against the deadline of the most recent successful heartbeat and reset that deadline after each success.
findings.failure_scenario: A heartbeat succeeds immediately after a fence check and all subsequent heartbeats fail. The check just before the 60-second deadline does nothing, and the job continues running until the following 10-second check.

output.summary: Reviewed restart reconciliation, adoption, lease handling, and late reporting. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package: `bun test test/lan-agent.test.ts test/agent-jobs.test.ts` reported `Cannot find package 'entities'`.

findings.title: Check for an unreported push before falling back from a dirty worktree
findings.detail: When resume validation fails, reconciliation cancels the open job and goes straight to prepare. If the worktree is dirty, prepare returns null before checking the remote branch, and the executor runs the local session. A worker commit pushed without an accepted report can therefore be overlooked instead of stopping the run for human intervention.
findings.suggestion: After cancelling an unreconciled job, check its expected remote SHA before allowing prepare or local fallback, while retaining the re-read for a job that finished concurrently.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes W while the coordinator is down but has not reported it; meanwhile the coordinator worktree becomes dirty. On restart, resume rejects and cancels the job, prepare returns null on the dirty worktree, and a local implementation starts despite the unreported W.

findings.title: Continue renewing the lease while retrying a fenced result
findings.detail: The new result request survives the fence, but the fence aborts the job controller and heldJobs excludes jobs with an aborted controller. Subsequent heartbeats therefore do not renew that job's lease. If result submissions keep receiving transient errors for a lease period while heartbeats succeed, the coordinator expires the job before the attempt deadline and rejects the eventual report.
findings.suggestion: Keep a published job in the heartbeat lease list while its independent result submission is pending, until the report succeeds or the coordinator rejects the lease.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes a commit during an outage and its fence fires. After restart, heartbeats succeed but the result endpoint returns 5xx for more than one lease period; the job expires and the accepted-report recovery fails even though the attempt deadline has not elapsed.

output.summary: Reviewed the restart, reconciliation, lease, and worker-report paths. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities dependency.

findings.title: Keep renewing the lease while a fenced worker retries a pushed result
findings.detail: The result request now survives the fence, but the fence also aborts the job controller. heldJobs() excludes jobs with an aborted controller, so subsequent heartbeats do not renew this job's lease. If result requests continue failing temporarily while heartbeats succeed, the coordinator expires the lease and rejects the eventual report, despite the worker retrying within the attempt deadline.
findings.suggestion: Keep a pushed result awaiting acceptance represented in heartbeats until the report completes or its attempt deadline expires.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes a commit, the fence fires during coordinator downtime, and after restart heartbeats succeed while the result endpoint remains unavailable for longer than the lease period. The job is retried or failed, and the pushed commit can leave the run needing human intervention.
