findings.title: Document the shorter heartbeat freshness grace
findings.detail: The guide promises an unreachable worker one lease period after restart, but sweepAgentJobs also fails it when heartbeat freshness exceeds the fresh interval, normally 30 seconds, before the 60-second lease period expires.
findings.suggestion: Align the documented timeout with the implemented freshness rule, or reconcile the two requested timeout behaviors.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker remains unreachable for 31 seconds after restart: the job is retried even though the documented 60-second lease period has not elapsed.

findings.title: Keep explicitly pinned local finders off workers
findings.detail: Every panel finder receives a worker checkout, including finders marked local. The executor excludes ordinary local-model targets because they have backend settings, but a run-level review model chain overrides the finder's free-only routing constraint. If that chain selects a Claude or Codex target without backend settings, the local finder is dispatched to a worker, contrary to the requirement that local finders stay local.
findings.suggestion: Carry the finder's local status into the call and omit checkout or otherwise explicitly exclude it from worker eligibility.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel roster contains a finder with local=true, a run pins models.review to a Claude CLI model, and workers are enabled for review and the repository. The finder creates a worker job instead of running on the coordinator.

findings.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers
findings.detail: Every finder receives checkout metadata, while worker eligibility has no indication that a finder is marked local. The free-only routing constraint does not guarantee a backend target: a valid free provider can use the Claude or Codex CLI without backend credentials. Such a finder meets all worker eligibility checks and runs remotely, contrary to the requirement that local finders stay local.

findings.title: The documented command cannot run in a fresh checkout

Consequently the advertised CLI exits with ENOENT before fetching or validating any PR. The new tests supply a temporary casePath, so they do not exercise the documented entry point.

findings.title: Validation retains setup artifacts that grading removes
findings.detail: Validation injects and runs hidden tests immediately after setup, while gradeImplement resets the checkout and runs git clean before injecting them. A test can therefore pass at head during validation but fail when the runner grades the actual head. The new fixture itself relies on an untracked `ready` file created by setup, which grading would remove.
findings.suggestion: Make validation reproduce the runner's reset and clean behavior before injecting the hidden files, and test a case that depends on a removed setup artifact.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup writes an untracked `ready` file and the hidden test reads it. Head validation passes, but grading deletes `ready` before running the same test, so even the reference implementation fails.

findings.title: CLI never looks up available production complexity

Every CLI-generated case is consequently labeled medium even when the factory's run record is available, contrary to the requested production complexity and potentially distorting comparisons by difficulty.
findings.suggestion: Wire a read-only run-record lookup into the CLI and retain the documented fallback only when the record or complexity is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged factory PR has a Run footer identifying a locally stored run with small complexity; invoking the documented CLI records medium instead.

findings.title: The replay-v2 tag cannot select the generated cases

output.summary: Reviewed snapshot creation, gate execution, reuse, and evidence handling. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout has missing or incompatible dependencies: `bun test test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts test/agent-test.test.ts` reported `floors.prefault is not a function` and could not find package `entities`.

findings.title: The gate checks a synthetic commit but reuses its result for a different commit
findings.detail: The snapshot checkout creates a synthetic child commit, while the later gates stage reuses its result solely by tree hash. A test check can inspect HEAD, commit metadata, or `git describe`; those values differ from the actual round commit even when the trees match. The reused result can therefore pass for a round whose real gate would fail, and it can then serve as verify evidence.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the gate observes the same commit identity and metadata as the round it attests to, or decline reuse when that equivalence cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured test checks the round commit message or compares `git rev-parse HEAD` with an expected commit. It passes against the synthetic snapshot commit but would fail against the eventual round commit; the gates stage skips the real test and records the pass.

findings.title: Running only the test check changes the gate's execution context
findings.detail: The in-session execution removes all other checks before running the test. Normal local gates run checks in configuration order in the same checkout, so earlier checks can create or modify files that the test reads. Reusing the isolated test result skips the test in that normal context and can turn a failing gates-stage run into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the normal test check's preceding execution context when producing reusable evidence, or restrict reuse to configurations where that context is demonstrably equivalent.
findings.failure_scenario: The base configuration runs a lint check that generates or modifies a file, followed by a test that fails on that file. The snapshot test runs before lint and passes; the gates stage runs lint but substitutes the earlier pass instead of executing the test afterward.

output.summary: Reviewed the snapshot, execution, retry, reuse, and evidence paths. Focused tests could not start because the available dependencies lack required Zod APIs and the entities package.

findings.title: Verify the snapshot checkout still points to the tested commit
findings.detail: The in-session gate result is recorded without checking whether the gate changed its checkout's HEAD. The normal gates stage explicitly checks HEAD before granting evidence, but this execution can be reused and attributed to the original tree even after a test command checks out or commits a different tree.
findings.suggestion: Record the snapshot commit and verify HEAD still points to it after all attempts before storing reusable evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository test command checks out a different commit, passes there, and exits successfully. The result is stored under the original snapshot tree and reused as passing evidence for the round commit.

findings.title: Synthetic commit makes Git-dependent test results differ from the round gate
findings.detail: The snapshot checkout uses a synthetic commit with a different SHA, message, and timestamp from the eventual round commit. The reuse key contains only the tree and gate environment, so a test that reads Git metadata can produce a different result in the actual round checkout while the synthetic checkout's result suppresses that test.
findings.suggestion: Ensure reuse is safe for checks that observe commit metadata, or execute against the actual commit and key evidence to the identity observed by the check.
findings.failure_scenario: A test checks `git log -1 --format=%s` or uses `git rev-parse HEAD` to select expected data. It passes on the synthetic 'Factory gate snapshot' commit but would fail on the round commit; the gates stage reuses the pass.

findings.title: Apply the normal timeout retry before returning the session result
findings.detail: The in-session path runs the check once and only invokes regression retries, which exclude timed-out results. The gates stage separately retries a timeout from a clean checkout. Consequently a transient timeout is returned to the implementer without the normal retry and cannot be recorded for reuse, so the same suite runs again in the gates stage.
findings.suggestion: Share the gates-stage timeout retry behavior with the in-session execution and preserve its attempts and classification in the stored result.
findings.failure_scenario: The full suite times out once under load and would pass on the normal timeout retry. The session reports failure and the gates stage runs the full suite again on the unchanged tree.

findings.title: Preserve worker sessions' full-suite behavior
findings.detail: The new policy is converted to `refuse` for worker implement sessions. The request explicitly limits the new behavior to local sessions and says workers retain their existing behavior; previously the default full-suite behavior was to run in a slot. With this repository switched to `gate`, worker implementers now have their full-suite requests refused.
findings.suggestion: Map the new mode to the existing worker slot behavior rather than refusal.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker implement round uses the updated repository policy and invokes `bun test`; the wrapper refuses it instead of running the slotted command as before.

output.summary: Reviewed the executor, lease, restart, release, and fallback paths. The focused test command `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts` could not start because the checkout is missing the `entities` dependency.

findings.title: Worktree exclusion is not atomic with job creation
findings.detail: The scan for existing jobs and the later enqueue occur separately, with no worktree claim or transaction spanning them. Two callers can both see an empty worktree and enqueue jobs; separate executor processes can then lease and run both jobs concurrently.
findings.suggestion: Atomically reserve the worktree when creating a job, and retain that reservation until process shutdown is confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: Two daemon processes start gates for the same cwd at the same time, both pass the existing-job scan, and two executors run the checks in that worktree concurrently.

findings.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat or freshness check
findings.detail: Availability is determined solely by whether the registered PID and birth identity still exist. A hung or suspended executor is treated as fresh indefinitely. In particular, waitStopped waits indefinitely for a live but unresponsive owner, so cancellation and fallback can stall a run instead of completing.
findings.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a bounded, fail-closed recovery path for an owner that stops responding.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor is suspended during a gate; its lease expires and the daemon marks the job failed, but waitStopped continues waiting because the executor process still exists.

findings.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate only accepts baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A durable handle for a targeted retry or timeout retry is cancelled on resume even when its executor still holds a valid lease, so the running check is discarded and repeated.
findings.suggestion: Persist and restore the retry context needed to resume these purposes, and include them in the reattachment validation.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is running; the resumed stage rejects its matching handle, cancels the executor job, and starts the retry again.

findings.title: Rollback to an older daemon leaves the executor release marker stale
findings.detail: Only this new daemon writes executor.daemonRelease. After rollback to a release predating this change, that setting still names the newer release, so its executor neither detects the release change nor stops its running jobs. The old daemon can resume and start its own in-process gates while those jobs continue.
findings.suggestion: Use a release identity that remains valid across rollback to older daemons, or otherwise arrange for the old executor to stop before an older daemon resumes work.
findings.failure_scenario: A new-release executor runs a long gate, then deployment rolls back to the previous daemon binary, which never updates executor.daemonRelease; the old executor keeps running the gate alongside the resumed daemon's replacement.

findings.title: Local fallback under LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor
findings.detail: When gates.executor is LAN, gateExecutorFor always returns the LAN executor. For a repository outside the LAN repository list, that executor directly starts local gates, ignoring executor.enabled. Those local gates still die on daemon restart.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local fallback through the in-place executor when it is enabled and available.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon has LAN gates configured for one repository and executor.enabled set; a run for another repository executes its local gate inside the daemon and loses it on restart.

output.summary: Reviewed the executor’s leasing, restart, fallback, and release handling. The targeted command `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts` could not run: Bun reported `Cannot find package 'entities' from 'src/gates/private.ts'`.

findings.title: Rollback to an older daemon leaves the executor running on the newer release
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change solely through this setting. A daemon from the previous release does not write it, so rolling back leaves the newer release SHA in the database. The newer executor continues renewing and running its jobs even after the older daemon starts, contrary to the release boundary and potentially alongside the older daemon's in-process gates.
findings.suggestion: Use a daemon identity and release record whose liveness is verified, and ensure an executor stops when the owning daemon disappears or cannot establish a same-release successor.
findings.failure_scenario: A new-release executor is running a gate when deployment rolls back to the base release. The old daemon never updates executor.daemonRelease, so the executor sees no release change and continues the gate.

findings.title: Restarted targeted retries are always cancelled
findings.detail: Resume explicitly accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A running targeted retry has purpose regression-retry-targeted, so a restart treats its valid handle as a mismatch, cancels it, and restarts earlier gate work. Timeout and other retry purposes are similarly excluded.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage context to resume the recorded retry and accept its matching purpose before rerunning earlier work.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running a long regression-retry-targeted check. The resumed stage rejects that handle even when its round, SHA, and executor lease still match.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor availability is based only on PID and process birth time; there is no heartbeat timestamp. If the executor is suspended or its event loop stalls, new jobs are sent to it despite its inability to pick them up. For an already leased job, sweep eventually marks it failed, but waitStopped continues waiting for the still-existing process indefinitely, so the run cannot fall back or finish cancellation.
findings.suggestion: Track executor freshness independently of process existence and make an expired executor produce a bounded, explicit stop or recovery path before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but stops servicing its event loop during a gate. Its lease expires, but waitStopped loops forever because processBirthSync still matches.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local fallback repositories
findings.detail: Enabling the in-place executor only affects the local executor kind. When gates.executor is LAN, lanExecutor handles repositories outside workers.repos by calling local.start directly, so those local gates still run inside the daemon and are lost on restart despite the in-place executor being enabled and available.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local fallback through the configured in-place executor, while retaining LAN execution for eligible repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation uses gates.executor = "lan" for one repository, enables the executor, and runs a different repository not listed in workers.repos. Its gate runs in the daemon instead of the executor.

output.summary: Reviewed the identity provider, configuration, GitHub call sites, polling, and approval handling. The targeted command `bun test test/github-app.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` package; Bun reported `Cannot find package 'entities' from 'src/gates/private.ts'`.

findings.title: Key validation does not establish that the daemon can read the key
findings.detail: The startup check inspects permission bits but neither verifies the file owner nor attempts to read the file. A regular file owned by another user with mode 0600 passes validation even though the daemon cannot read it. Startup therefore succeeds and configured GitHub operations fail later during signing, contrary to the required startup refusal. The same check also accepts owner-executable modes such as 0700 despite reporting that mode 0600 is required.
findings.suggestion: Verify ownership and actual readability at startup, and enforce the intended allowed permission modes with a clear error.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure `private_key_path` to a regular file owned by another user with mode 0600: `loadConfig` accepts it, but the first App token exchange fails with `cannot read or sign with private key`.

output.summary: Reviewed configuration, identity selection, GitHub call sites, polling, approval handling, and secret isolation. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks installed dependencies: `bun test test/github-app.test.ts test/land-queue.test.ts` reported missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js` and `entities`.

findings.title: An App key outside the config directory can be exposed to agents
findings.detail: The configuration accepts an arbitrary absolute or relative key path, but the agent read policy protects the config directory and does not add this resolved key path to its deny list. A key placed in a readable checkout or another agent-readable location can therefore be read by a tool-enabled agent or gate, despite the requirement that the key never reach them.
findings.suggestion: Either require the key to reside within the protected config directory or include its canonical path in every applicable agent and gate read-deny policy, rejecting configurations that overlap required readable roots.
findings.failure_scenario: Set `private_key_path` to a mode-0600 key in the repository checkout and run a tool-enabled agent against that checkout; the agent can read the private key.

findings.title: Standalone callers silently use the owner identity
findings.detail: The global provider defaults to the owner and is configured only when a `Factory` is constructed. Standalone code that loads configuration and calls the shared GitHub functions without constructing a factory therefore ignores configured App repositories. For example, `scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts` calls `runGh` directly, so its repository calls use the owner's login and also bypass the required fail-closed behavior when App authentication is unavailable.
findings.suggestion: Initialize the shared provider for every supported standalone entry point that uses these GitHub helpers, or inject a configured provider explicitly rather than defaulting configured callers to the owner.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the replay-case script for a repository listed in `[github.app].repos` without starting a `Factory` in that process; its `gh` calls use the owner's login even if the App token exchange would fail.

output.summary: Reviewed identity routing, configuration validation, approval handling, and the manual landing path. The targeted App test could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` package.

findings.title: Startup accepts a key path that the identity provider later refuses
findings.detail: Configuration validation follows symlinks with statSync, but signingKey opens the path with O_NOFOLLOW and refuses a symlink. Consequently the daemon can start successfully with an unusable App configuration, then fail its GitHub operations only when it first requests a token. The request requires startup to refuse an invalid key file.
findings.suggestion: Use the same key-file validation at startup and when signing, including the no-follow and ownership checks.
findings.failure_scenario: private_key_path names a symlink to a mode-0600 regular key file. loadConfig accepts it and the daemon starts; the first GitHub call for a listed repository fails with "symlink refused".

findings.title: Manual landing still merges with the owner's identity
findings.detail: The new provider is not used by scripts/check-private-strings.ts, which scripts/land-pr.sh invokes to perform its final gh pr merge. That script calls sh directly without configuring or selecting the repository identity, so an App-configured repository is merged using the owner's gh login and an App authentication failure cannot stop that merge.
findings.suggestion: Route the manual landing script's repository-scoped gh calls through the configured identity provider and propagate identity failures.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs scripts/land-pr.sh for a repository listed in github.app.repos. The final merge is performed by the owner's gh credentials instead of the App, even if the App token exchange would fail.

output.summary: Reviewed the identity provider, GitHub call paths, configuration, approval handling, and doctor checks. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities and MCP SDK dependencies.

findings.title: Reject unusable App key files at startup
findings.detail: Startup validates the target with statSync, but signing later opens the configured path with O_NOFOLLOW and checks ownership. Consequently, a symlink to a mode-0600 key passes configuration and daemon startup, then every App-authenticated call fails with "symlink refused". A mode-0600 file owned by another user likewise passes the startup check but fails when first used. The check also accepts owner-executable modes such as 0700 despite the requested 0600 requirement.
findings.suggestion: Use the same file-opening, ownership, readability, and mode validation at startup as during signing, and enforce the requested mode consistently.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as a symlink to a valid mode-0600 key. The daemon starts successfully, but its first GitHub operation for a listed repository fails before obtaining a token.

output.summary: Traced Claude parsing, LAN fallback, provider routing, and worker version skew. The targeted test command could not run because checkout dependencies were missing or incompatible: `entities` and `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` were not found, and the installed Zod lacks `z.json`.

findings.title: Older workers still consume rounds on authentication failure
findings.detail: The coordinator relies exclusively on the new optional failureClass field. A worker running the previous release reports the same Claude authentication rejection as an ordinary error without that field, so the coordinator returns it as the implementation result and proceeds to gates and review. This is a realistic rolling-upgrade state and reproduces the issue the change is intended to fix until every worker has been upgraded.
findings.suggestion: Provide a structured, version-compatible way to detect or prevent dispatch to workers that cannot report authentication failures, while retaining support for ordinary task errors.
findings.failure_scenario: A new coordinator dispatches an implement round to an older worker whose Claude OAuth token has expired. The worker returns status error without failureClass; the coordinator records a completed round and runs gates on unchanged code.

findings.title: A late 401 is treated as if the session never ran
findings.detail: Any terminal 401 or authentication_failed assistant event marks the entire invocation as an authentication startup failure, even when earlier turns executed tools and changed files. On a worker, those changes are published and adopted before the coordinator starts the same round locally; locally, routing can start another implementer against the partially changed worktree. The new classification therefore can replay work and side effects after an interrupted, partially executed session.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a rejection before agent work from authentication errors after the session has begun, and preserve the existing partial-session handling for the latter.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude edits files in one turn, then its next API request returns a structured 401. The worker publishes the partial edit and the coordinator invokes a local implementer as though the worker never ran.

findings.title: Provider health can omit the authentication reason
findings.detail: The tracker stores only the CLI's free-text error. A structured 401 with a generic result such as "Rejected" is classified correctly but provider health displays only that text, so it does not show that authentication failed.
findings.suggestion: Pass the structured failure class to provider health or prefix the recorded reason with an authentication label.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude emits an error result with api_error_status 401 and result "Rejected"; provider health shows "Rejected" without identifying authentication as the cause.

output.summary: Reviewed the parser, routing, and worker fallback paths. Targeted tests could not load because installed dependencies were missing or incompatible, including entities, @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime, and the installed Zod version.

findings.title: Authentication rejection after productive turns is treated as a session that never ran
findings.detail: The parser marks any structured authentication rejection as a startup failure, even if earlier turns authenticated and executed tools. The coordinator then falls back to another candidate, and the LAN executor adopts the worker's published changes and starts another local session. Those paths assume the failed session did no work, so a token rejection during a later model call can repeat edits or external tool side effects and can prevent a productive implementation attempt from being counted.
findings.suggestion: Track whether the session made a successful model turn or performed work, and apply the startup-failure fallback only when authentication was rejected before the session ran. Handle a later authentication failure as an interrupted session.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude successfully edits files or invokes a tool, then its token expires before a subsequent API request. The final stream reports authentication_failed; the worker publishes the edits, and the coordinator starts a second session locally as if the first had never run.

findings.title: Timeout during structured authentication retries still consumes an implementation round
findings.detail: The captured CLI stream reports 401 authentication failures in system api_retry events before emitting the final assistant and result events, but the parser ignores those structured retry events. If the invocation deadline or idle timeout expires during those retries, runClaude returns timeout or stuck without failureClass. Context.invoke returns that result as a task-level failure, so implementation proceeds to gates and consumes a round despite the observed authentication rejection.
findings.suggestion: Track structured authentication retry events and preserve an authentication classification when the process ends before a successful response or final result, while retaining cancellation handling.
findings.failure_scenario: An invalid token produces an api_retry event with error_status 401 and error authentication_failed, then the invocation times out before the final result. The unchanged implementation round continues to gates instead of falling back or failing with the authentication reason.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle reconciliation, queue admission, and integration startup. Focused tests could not start because checkout dependencies were missing: `entities` and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are restricted to queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation only runs for repositories listed in githubQueue with a nonempty trusted list. Runs started through CLI, MCP, labels, or comments in other repositories receive no lifecycle labels or comments, although the request requires these updates for every start path and says to fall back to gh where the App does not cover a repository.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and select the GitHub identity per repository.
findings.failure_scenario: A user starts a run with `Closes #12` in a repository absent from githubQueue; no in-progress label or lifecycle comment is posted.

findings.title: Intermediate lifecycle events disappear between polls
findings.detail: Comments and label targets are derived from the run's current status, and an event is recorded as pending only when reconciliation observes it. A transition that begins and ends between polls, or while the daemon is stopped, leaves no durable event to retry. The same problem occurs when a label write fails and the run advances before the next poll.

findings.title: A removed priority label can satisfy re-approval

findings.title: Terminal status prevents restart from finishing rollback
findings.detail: The rejection checkpoint is saved with status `needs_human` before rollback begins. On daemon startup, the scheduler only requeues interrupted `running` and `waiting_input` runs, so it never calls `executeRun` for this checkpoint. The new tests call `executeRun` directly and therefore bypass the scheduler behavior that determines whether a real restart resumes the run. A rollback command failure or shutdown is also swallowed by the rejection handler, leaving the same terminal status without another cleanup attempt.

findings.title: An empty repository never establishes its enable boundary
findings.detail: When the first successful poll returns no open issues, there is no timestamp to store. The next poll containing an issue is treated as the first poll, so its commands are silently skipped and its newest timestamp becomes the boundary. The added test explicitly expects this behavior, but it loses commands created after the queue was enabled.
findings.suggestion: Obtain and persist a GitHub-time boundary on the first successful poll even when no open issue supplies a timestamp.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the queue while a repository has no open issues. After the successful poll, open an issue and post `/limitless fix it` before the next poll. That poll sets the boundary to the comment timestamp and the command never runs.

findings.title: An old command on a closed issue can pass the enable boundary
findings.detail: The maximum timestamp among currently open issues can be arbitrarily older than the first poll. A closed issue's command created after that maximum but before the queue was enabled is absent from the initial response. If the issue is later reopened, its command compares newer than the stored boundary and starts a run even though it predates enablement.
findings.suggestion: Establish a boundary that represents GitHub time at enablement and prevents previously existing commands on subsequently reopened issues from being admitted.
findings.failure_scenario: The newest open issue was updated on Monday. A trusted user comments on a closed issue on Tuesday, the queue first polls on Wednesday, and the issue is reopened Thursday. The Tuesday command is admitted against Monday's boundary.

findings.title: Identity failure disables the factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: A failed App identity lookup is converted to null, after which slash commands continue processing and the bot-login comparison cannot exclude the factory. If the bot login is trusted, a factory-authored command can create a run and be permanently recorded during a transient identity failure.
findings.suggestion: Leave commands retryable when the configured App identity cannot be established, so the factory-author check can be applied before creating a run.
findings.failure_scenario: The trusted list includes the App bot login, its identity lookup fails, and one of its comments begins `/limitless ` with a request. The poll creates a run from that factory-authored comment.

findings.title: An empty first poll permanently skips the first subsequent command
findings.detail: When the first successful poll contains no open issues, no boundary is stored. findings.title: Identity lookup failures disable the factory-author check

The poller can no longer recognize the App's own author and can record and run its comments if that login is trusted. This also consumes commands during an API failure despite the retryability invariant.

findings.title: A timeout rerun with failed setup loses its rerun history

The observation therefore has no matching comparison and is finalized with `no_retry`, although the stage did rerun and failed. findings.title: Reconciliation can leave an executor running the wrong release indefinitely
findings.detail: Reconciliation treats any loaded executor as sufficient. An executor that started on release A but has not yet observed A as the daemon release remains idle on a mismatch and never exits. If the daemon moves to B before that first matching observation, reconciliation sees the A process as loaded and leaves it there indefinitely, so the successful deploy does not bring up an executor for B.
findings.suggestion: Ensure successful reconciliation replaces or otherwise verifies a loaded executor that has not adopted the healthy daemon's release, while preserving the required same-release restart behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor starts with release A while the recorded daemon release is absent or different; before it observes A, a deploy makes the daemon healthy on B. The executor continues idling with A, and deploy exits successfully because launchctl reports the unit loaded.

findings.title: Lowercasing configured repositories can create duplicate registrations
findings.detail: Queue run requests now use the lowercased slug, but repository resolution uses case-sensitive `getRepoBySlug` lookups. An existing registration with mixed-case spelling is therefore missed, causing `resolveRepo` to query GitHub and register a second repository with the lowercase slug. The new registration can have different repository settings, including merge policy, and an unnecessary GitHub lookup can prevent admission if it fails.
findings.suggestion: Deduplicate queue configuration by a canonical comparison key while resolving requests to the existing registered repository case-insensitively.
findings.failure_scenario: A deployment already has `Owner/Repo` registered and configured in the queue. After upgrading, an approved issue is submitted as `owner/repo`; the existing row is missed and a second repo row is created.

findings.title: Every poll performs an ownership query for every historical run
findings.detail: `issueRunObservations()` loads every run in the database, and `decision()` calls `linkedIssues()`, which executes a recursive `issueLinkOwner` query for each one. This synchronous N+1 pass runs before every poll, including for unrelated repositories and runs without issue links. Its cost grows with the entire run history and blocks the daemon event loop, reintroducing the class of stalls the batched queue lookup was intended to remove.
findings.suggestion: Seed observations with a batched ownership lookup, scoped to relevant linked runs, without issuing a database query per historical run.
findings.failure_scenario: A long-running installation has thousands of historical runs, most unrelated to configured queue repositories. Each queue poll synchronously reads all of them and runs thousands of recursive SQLite queries before it can process any issues.

findings.title: Every poll performs an ownership query for every stored run

This reintroduces the class of daemon stalls that the batched lookup was intended to remove.

findings.title: A moved replay is marked lost without classifying the new tip

findings.title: Classify the observed tip before treating a replay race as supersession
findings.detail: Every `moved` result from a replay marks confirmed ownership lost and clears the intent. The claim client can return `moved` for a malformed tip or for a valid tip that does not satisfy the supersession conditions. In those cases recovery must retain the journal and report pending; clearing it can permanently discard a finished run's final status and checkpoint.
findings.suggestion: Classify `result.tip` using the same applied, superseded and pending rules as the initial recovery read, and preserve the intent when the tip is malformed or otherwise unclassifiable.

findings.title: Save confirmation and finalization in the same transaction
findings.detail: Each coordinator confirmation is saved with the post-merge-confirmed checkpoint before the separate save that finalizes observations. If the run is cancelled or otherwise becomes terminal between those saves, terminal handling finalizes the observation as interrupted even though the confirmed result was already durable. This also breaks the requested atomic checkpoint invariant.
findings.suggestion: Persist each completed confirmation together with the corresponding observation finalization, or use a distinct intermediate checkpoint and make the final confirmed save atomic with finalization.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker failure is confirmed passing on the coordinator; the first post-merge-confirmed save succeeds, then the run is cancelled before the following save. The observation is recorded as interrupted instead of platform, flaky, or unclassified according to the OS values.

findings.title: Do not finalize other post-merge executions with the current result
findings.detail: Completion selects observations by purpose, round and SHA but does not restrict rebase observations to the execution or stage being completed. Distinct post-merge executions can share the same round and SHA after an interrupted attempt. The later completion then applies its comparisons and confirmation to the earlier execution's rows, permanently attributing the later retry or coordinator result to a different primary failure.
findings.suggestion: Scope post-merge finalization to the primary execution identity being completed and leave other attempts to be finalized as interrupted.
findings.failure_scenario: A post-merge gate records a failure, is interrupted before its result checkpoint, and is executed again for the same round and commit. When the second execution is confirmed passing, both observations can be finalized with that confirmation even though only the second execution was confirmed.

findings.title: Resumed LAN executions lose the slow-regression flag
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage receives a new stage ID, but reattaching to a completed LAN execution retains its existing observation: insertion is ignored by the execution identity's unique constraint. Filtering observations by the new stage ID therefore excludes that row, so the selector never records slow_regression on it. A passing slow re-check is subsequently classified as flaky instead of load.
findings.suggestion: Associate the selector with the primary execution handle independently of the current stage ID, including when an existing observation is reused after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN post-merge gate fails slowly, its observation is inserted, and the daemon restarts before the confirmation-pending checkpoint. The resumed stage reattaches to the same completed job and its re-check passes.

findings.title: Finalize distinct post-merge executions using their own results
findings.detail: Completion selects every unfinalized rebase observation with the same round and SHA, regardless of execution handle or stage. A local gate cannot be reattached after restart, so a replacement execution can produce a different result while the old observation remains. The replacement's comparison is then applied to both executions, attributing its outcome to the interrupted original.
findings.suggestion: Finalize only observations belonging to the completed primary execution identity; leave abandoned executions to be finalized as interrupted.
findings.failure_scenario: A local post-merge gate fails and records an observation, then the daemon restarts before saving the comparison. The replacement execution passes on the same SHA; its passing comparison is used to finalize the earlier failed execution even though it was interrupted.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease manager, intent recovery, clock predicates, and claim client. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not run: the installed Zod dependency raises `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` while loading `src/evals/settings.ts`. The review found several correctness issues independent of that test failure.

findings.title: Replayed releases bypass lease-time revalidation
findings.detail: Reconciliation delegates to `reconcileLeaseIntent`, which can replay a pending release directly through `client.write` without a `beforeSend` predicate or a fresh GitHub-time sample. The release can therefore be sent after the confirmed generation has expired, including after a restart or a prolonged unconfirmed outcome.
findings.suggestion: Ensure release replay performs the same fresh time decision and send-time revalidation as other same-generation writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is persisted, the process stops before sending, and recovery runs more than ten minutes later while the old tip is still present. Recovery writes the expired generation's release without checking whether it remains renewable.

findings.title: A different run cannot reconcile a pending acquisition
findings.detail: The cross-run check returns `refused` before reconciliation whenever the existing row has an intent. This violates the requirement to reconcile pending intents before every operation and can leave a failed first acquisition blocking the next run until a renewal loop happens to run.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the row first, return `wait` while it remains pending, and then evaluate ownership and whether an unconfirmed row should be forgotten.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition leaves an intent that GitHub can now prove was unchanged. Before the loop starts, run B attempts to acquire the absent ref; it receives `refused` instead of dropping A's intent and acquiring it.

findings.title: Renewal loop omits confirmed leases recovered from storage
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated by writes applied during this manager's lifetime. Confirmed held rows recovered on startup, and first acquisitions confirmed by intent reconciliation, are never added to that map. The loop consequently cannot renew them even when the active hook would return true.
findings.suggestion: Populate or derive loop handles from confirmed held rows after recovery and reconciliation, while preserving generation checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An acquisition reaches GitHub but returns unconfirmed. The loop later reconciles the intent as applied, yet no handle is inserted into `handles`; subsequent ticks never renew the confirmed lease, which expires.

findings.title: Second moved outcome marks ownership lost without checking the tip
findings.detail: After two moved outcomes, any confirmed row for the requested run is marked lost regardless of whether the returned record supersedes its confirmed generation. A malformed or older tip, for example, does not establish supersession, but still clears the lease and invokes `onLost`.
findings.suggestion: Classify the final moved tip against confirmed ownership before marking loss; return an uncertain or refused result when it does not prove supersession.
findings.failure_scenario: Two consecutive writes encounter moved outcomes whose final tip is malformed. The manager marks its confirmed held row lost even though the tip provides no evidence of a superseding generation.

output.summary: Reviewed the manager against the claim journal and GitHub-time APIs. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not reach the tests: the installed dependency fails during import with `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` in `src/evals/settings.ts:14`.

findings.title: Renewal loop omits leases recovered after a restart
findings.detail: The loop renews only entries in the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated only by a directly applied write in this manager instance. Creating a manager with an already-confirmed held row, or reconciling an unconfirmed acquisition to applied, never adds its handle. An active recovered lease therefore receives no periodic renewal and can expire.
findings.suggestion: Populate or derive renewal handles from confirmed held rows after recovery and reconciliation, while retaining the generation and ownership checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A process restarts with a confirmed held lease and calls `start` with `active` returning true. Subsequent ticks never call `update` for that lease because `handles` is empty.

findings.title: Release intent replay bypasses send-time lease validation
findings.detail: The manager delegates reconciliation to `reconcileLeaseIntent`, which replays a pending release through `client.write` without a `beforeSend` hook or a fresh GitHub-time decision. This path can write the old generation after its lease window and expiry have passed, despite the requirement that every same-generation send be revalidated.
findings.suggestion: Ensure release replay obtains and validates the applicable time evidence immediately before sending, including during startup recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is journaled before a crash but its ref update is not sent. The manager restarts more than ten minutes later and recovery replays the release against the unchanged tip without checking expiry.

findings.title: A different run bypasses reconciliation of a pending intent
findings.detail: The cross-run guard returns `refused` before reconciliation whenever the existing row has an intent. The specification requires pending intents to be reconciled before every operation and unresolved intents to return `wait`. In particular, a dropped first acquisition remains a barrier to another run until a loop tick happens, even when it could be reconciled immediately.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the row first, return `wait` if it remains pending, and then apply the cross-run ownership checks to the settled row.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A has an unconfirmed first acquisition whose write did not reach GitHub. Before a renewal loop tick, run B acquires the same ref; it gets `refused` without reconciling and forgetting A's dropped intent.

output.summary: Reviewed the verification, preview, and invocation paths. Focused tests could not start because the checkout resolved a missing entities package and an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Treat browser setup as successful only with positive evidence
findings.detail: The absence of a browser_unavailable event is treated as proof that browser setup succeeded. The local harness emits that event when browserMcp configuration fails, but constructing the MCP configuration does not establish that the MCP server or Chromium actually started successfully. If startup subsequently fails, the verifier can correctly report the browser check blocked, yet this code converts it to unclear, attributes the failure to incomplete verification, and sends it into an implementation feedback round instead of the bounded environment-block path.
findings.suggestion: Record a positive, attempt-specific browser setup outcome and convert blocked rows only when that outcome and preview readiness are established. Preserve the environment-block path when browser startup cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview becomes ready and browserMcp returns a configuration, but the MCP server or Chromium fails to launch. The verifier reports a marked browser criterion blocked because its browser tools are unavailable; no browser_unavailable event was emitted, so the engine records available and converts the row to unclear.

output.summary: Reviewed browser verification, preview state, and resume handling. The targeted test files could not run because the local entities dependency is missing.

findings.title: Existing spec validation rejects the newly permitted browser checks
findings.detail: The prompt now asks authors to create preview-based criteria, but outOfRunCriteria still flags phrases such as “in a browser” and “visually.” The engine then tells the author to replace those criteria with checkout commands and tests and move external concerns out of scope. A focused probe confirmed the conflict: `bun -e 'import { outOfRunCriteria } from "./src/pipeline/spec-criteria.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(outOfRunCriteria({acceptance_criteria:[{id:"AC-1",criterion:"Navigation works",how_to_verify:"Open the preview in a browser and visually inspect navigation",browser:true}]})))'` returned the marked criterion as an out-of-run criterion. The retry can therefore remove the visual or interactive acceptance check that this change is intended to establish.
findings.suggestion: Update the existing criterion validation and its retry guidance to allow checks explicitly marked for the UI preview, while retaining the restrictions on genuinely external checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A spec author marks an acceptance criterion browser=true and writes “Open the preview in a browser and visually inspect navigation” as its verification steps. The engine flags it as invalid and asks the author to replace it with commands or tests.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle publication, recovery, privacy checks, and answer-command dispatch against the request. The targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`; it exited with 0 tests run and a module-resolution error.

findings.title: Recover an uncertain POST before closing its checkpoint
findings.detail: A pending effect with a recovery page is marked done immediately if reinspection of its stored body fails. That closes the checkpoint without looking for a previously accepted comment, contrary to the required recovery ordering. Inspection can fail transiently, including when the private-strings configuration cannot be read.
findings.suggestion: Recover the checkpointed marker independently of whether the body is currently safe to post. After recovery, suppress any new POST if body inspection fails.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but its response is lost. Before the next poll, private-string inspection fails. The effect is marked done without querying GitHub or recording the accepted comment ID.

findings.title: Recheck needs-human status before posting its reason
findings.detail: The eligibility predicate checks the current waiting status and question set only for question effects. A pending needs-human comment remains eligible after the run resumes or is cancelled, including when that transition occurs while the posting identity lookup is awaited. It can therefore publish an obsolete needs-you reason after the run no longer needs attention.
findings.suggestion: Include the current needs-human status in eligibility for needs-human publications and supersede an unsent effect when that status changes, while preserving recovery of uncertain POSTs.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and its comment waits on identity lookup. The user resolves the issue and the run resumes before lookup returns; the code still posts the old needs-you reason.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle publication, recovery, command reservation, and the added tests. The targeted issue-queue test could not run because the checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: A superseded unpublished question set can never be published if waiting resumes
findings.detail: Superseding an unsent or unsuccessfully posted question effect records it as done. If the run later returns to waiting with the same unanswered IDs and issue link, observe treats that done effect as an already published set and never creates another one. This permanently hides outstanding questions even though no matching comment was accepted. The added supersession tests explicitly expect this behavior.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a recovered or successfully published set from a superseded set that was never posted, and allow the latter to be scheduled again when it becomes eligible after recovery completes.
findings.failure_scenario: A run waits on question 42; its POST fails before acceptance. The run temporarily resumes running, so recovery closes the stale effect without finding a comment. The run returns to waiting on question 42; subsequent polls and restarts never publish it.
